(6) public/manifest.webmanifest plus metadata.manifest works, but Next 15's app/manifest.ts is the native route, and installing over a LAN URL needs HTTPS.
items.change: Build toasts in lib/notifyClient.ts toastFromWs from the existing {type:'history'} item for kinds desk, trade, brief and symbol=='MARKET'. Keep fired/signal_fired for price and signal toasts so nothing toasts twice, and drop the metric_snapshot diffing. Add optional `interval` and `ref` (desk call id or trade id) to AlertService.record and AlertHistoryItem, so every toast and history row can call pickSymbol(symbol, interval). Still handle 'desk' and 'desk_scored', but only to dispatch ac:desk-changed. Replace the window CustomEvents sent to dock tabs with a workspace-level pendingFocus {tab, id} state passed through DockPanelProps and consumed on mount. Rule: price and trade toasts stay until dismissed; all others auto-dismiss after 12 s. Use app/manifest.ts. Do the Dock overflow and hotkey titles once, here, and remove them from command-palette and the Dock fix.

items.problems: Mostly confirmed. The pickedLevel bar (ChartWorkspace.tsx ~l.1284) only offers Remove, and the right-click menu (AgenticChart.tsx l.1518-1522) sends 'Alert me at X' and 'Draw a line at X' through onAskAgent → runAnalysis. Partial overlaps: Remove and Del already exist (removePickedLevel). AlertsPanel's Triggers tab can already build a trigger from a chart zone via lib/alerts.ts chartZones(), which already works out long/short from the zone kind, so a new triggerDirection would duplicate it. Risks: (1) Picking is currently limited by `overlays.includes(o)` (ChartWorkspace l.1259). Widening it to all composed overlays would let the card pick alert overlays (kind 'alert', ids 'alert-<id>'), and 'Alert on entry' would then create a duplicate alert on a line that is already an alert. (2) overlayAt (AgenticChart l.1075) tests only y across the whole width, so a box is picked even where it isn't drawn. (3) Moving the card and DrawingStyleBar into ChartCell means threading more callbacks through ActiveProps, and it only matters in grid mode (in 1-chart mode main and the cell are the same area). (4) Parsing ' · 2/2 held' from labels is fragile. The backend writes it at ta_agent.py:637 as `{held}/{tests} held`.
items.change: Exclude kind 'alert' (and 'my_entry') from picking, and limit box hits to the box's time_start..time_end x-range. Make triggerDirection a thin export built on chartZones' existing kind→direction regex. Reuse planTrigger's addTrigger shape for '5m confirmation'. Drop the 'render inside ChartCell' step, or do it with a portal into the active cell's container. Render the actions with the shared PlanActions/alert helpers (see missing). Keep the instant onQuickAlert/onQuickLine. That part is correct and valuable.

items.problems: Confirmed: DrawingLayerPrimitive.pick only returns a drawing id with HIT_PX=6 (no anchor handles), and AgenticChart's pointer move (l.1385-1405) moves all points together. Wrong claim: the design says it will give 'one undo step', but hooks/useUndo.ts already merges same-label changes within COALESCE_MS=700 into one step, so a drag is already one undo entry unless the user pauses. The real cost is that every pointermove calls onDrawingsChange → changeDrawings → usePersistentState stringify, localStorage.setItem and a SYNC event. 'Z' is indeed free (TOOL_HOTKEYS plus panel keys use t,h,f,r,n,p,m,w,a,l,v,q,j,y,x,c,o,e,b,u,d,s,g,k,i). items.problems:
Part A fixes a real bug. I reproduced it: rule_intent('What would invalidate this?', previous=<long plan>) returns features ['support_resistance'] with keep_existing False; 'Does the daily agree?' sets timeframe 1d; 'Is RSI overbought here?' and 'why?' fall to the default S/R+windows. merge_overlays (agent.py:114) then keeps only custom kinds, so every plan_* overlay is dropped.

The design leaves gaps.
(1) ChartWorkspace.tsx:651 runs `if (prompt) setLastIntent(r.intent)`, so the empty question-only intent becomes previous_intent. The next 'Same on daily' or 'again' then follows previous.features=[] and trade_plan=None (llm.py follow_up branch) and redraws nothing, losing the plan anyway.
(2) The pitch overstates the chip problem. AgentPanel.followUps (AgentPanel.tsx:123-150) already branches on plan, setups, gridCoins, scan, sells, ladder, walk, sources and kimi; it is not 'the same five strings every time'.
(3) invalidation.structure_level is 'the newest swing low below entry'. That level can sit below the stop, where it is meaningless as invalidation, or between stop and entry, and the design doesn't say which.
(4) plan_in_focus computes ATR distances and filled/stop-hit on the current chart's df even when focus.interval differs from the chart interval.
(5) Chips like 'Alert me if 7.53–7.57 breaks' go back through rule_intent and must parse as a zone alert. No eval case covers that.
items.change:
Ship A plus the lastIntent fix first, as a standalone S item.
- Backend: when QUESTION_ONLY matches, return previous.model_copy(update={features: [], keep_existing: True, answer_hint: prompt[:200], timeframe: None}) when previous exists, and set AnalyzeResponse.question_only=true.
- ChartWorkspace: skip setLastIntent when question_only, so 'same again' still means the plan.
- plan_in_focus: compute only when focus.interval == the analysed interval; otherwise fetch focus.interval candles. structure_level = the highest swing low strictly between stop and entry, else null with 'stop is the structure'.
- Add intents.jsonl lines for every chip suggest.py can emit, so each chip is proven to parse as intended (alert chips → zone alert, plan chips → trade_plan long).
- Reword E as 'chips derived from facts' layered on the existing contextual followUps, after A ships.

items.problems:
The facts gaps are real. llm.narrate/narrate_stream (llm.py:1074-1110) send no symbol and no DRAFT, and agent.py never sets facts['symbol'] or facts['data_source']. The slim prompt is also justified: narrate_system('normal') measures 7,149 chars.

The guard is much weaker than the pitch claims. postmortem.grounded (postmortem.py:439) passes any integer ≤100. It also passes any number within half a printed unit of ANY leaf in facts, and facts hold hundreds of leaves: zones, EMAs, VWAP, windows, research, scan rows.
- An invented 'RSI 85', '62% odds' or '3x' always passes.
- On a coin trading at 7.5, a 2-decimal price matches some leaf within ±0.005 almost everywhere.
- It cannot catch mis-attribution, e.g. calling the 7.62 resistance 'support' or the stop 'the entry'.
So 'every price it writes is one the chart has' and 'never invents a number' overpromise. Separately, dropping one sentence can leave the next one dangling ('That level…').
items.change:
Keep the facts, DRAFT and NARRATE_BASE/RULES split. Tighten grounding before advertising it:
- Integers ≤100 followed by '%', or within 3 words of rsi|odds|chance|probability|confidence|win, must match a fact leaf ±1.
- Numbers between 0.5× and 2× last_price must match a leaf under a price-like key (low, high, price, entry, stop, target, level, last_price, close, tp) and be printed with at least 3 significant digits. Vaguer ones count as 'rounded' in the stats but are not dropped.
- Add rr and distance_pct to plan, zone and price_in_question facts, so the model doesn't need to compute them.
- When a sentence is dropped and the next one opens with a pronoun (That|This|It|Those), drop that one too.
- Word the UI and StatusPanel as 'numbers checked against chart data', never 'can't invent'.

items.problems:
The rules-only CI script is the right regression guard for the plan-wipe bug.

Problems:
(1) must_not: ['short', 'leverage'] as substrings will false-fail correct answers. The spot note itself ('a short asked for in spot mode → the sell note', SPOT_SHORT_NOTE) and phrases like 'no leverage' contain those words.
(2) The LLM mode depends on LLMClient.last_usage, which only live-thinking adds, but depends_on doesn't list it.
(3) qwen2.5:7b runs at temperature 0.2 (narrate) are nondeterministic, so a single-run '18/20' comparison between models is noise.
(4) The ModelChooser 'agent' mode and ModelSettings columns are a lot of UI for an occasional model switch.
items.change:
- Make must_not phrase regexes that target recommendations, e.g. `\b(open|take|enter) (a )?short\b`, `\b\d+(\.\d+)?x leverage\b`.
- Declare depends_on live-thinking for prompt_eval_count, or record null.
- In LLM mode, pin temperature 0 and a seed, and run each script N=3 times, reporting the mean and the spread.
- Ship conversations.jsonl, converse.py and test_converse.py now. Defer the ModelChooser agent mode and the ModelSettings columns to a later round; the CLI table is enough to decide a model switch.

items.problems:
The cost case is real. LOOP_SYSTEM is 3,550 chars plus 14,734 chars of TOOLS JSON on every request, a heavy load on an 8k context. Step 4 is also confirmed: agent_loop._run_tool only .upper()s the symbol, look() calls get_klines directly, and plan_with_tools' except tuple misses MarketDataError (a RuntimeError).

Risks:
(1) Confident rule misreads now get no LLM second opinion. find_symbol('buy INJ with 500usdt') returns 500USDT (verified), so with the router a confident trade_plan would navigate to a bogus pair and serve synthetic candles.
(2) 'An explicit feature word matched → confident' is too broad. 'Will the 7.5 support hold if BTC dumps?' or 'is this demand safe to buy?' are judgement questions that the tool planner currently researches (market_context, other timeframes).

items.problems:
The idea is high value for a spot holder, but the maths and alerts have holes.
(1) In cost_out, rung 1 sells cost/price coins. When TP1 sits below the average entry (an under-water holder; INJ is plausibly one), that quantity is ≥ qty and the plan sells everything at a loss.
(2) Rungs are capped at +35%, so an under-water holder never sees a break-even rung.
(3) Invalidation is described as 'daily close below 18.90' but armed as a generic 1d lost_support SignalAlert. That alert fires on whatever support the detector picks at that close, not on 18.90, so the alert and the plan can disagree.
(4) HoldingsWatch already arms lost_support for held coins (holdings_watch.py SIGNALS, owner 'holdings'). With its interval set to 1d, the same close pings twice.
(5) The nearest D1 zone below price can be under 1 ATR away, which turns daily noise into 'you're wrong'.
(6) Binance spot minimum notional (about $5) and LOT_SIZE make small rungs unsellable.
items.change:
- cost_out: rung1_qty = min(sellable, cost/price). If price1 < avg_entry, fall back to 'quarters' with a note.
- Every rung below avg_entry shows 'realizes −$X vs your average'. Add an avg-entry marker rung when it lies above price.
- Arm invalidation as a level_close (1d, below, zone_low) alert from close-confirmed-alerts. Until that lands, use a cross alert labelled 'check the daily close'. Skip arming it when a holdings lost_support on 1d already covers the coin.
- Require invalidation ≥ 1 ATR(1d) below price; otherwise use the next zone down.
- Merge rungs whose usdt is below max($10, minNotional); round sell_qty down to stepSize from exchangeInfo.

items.problems:
(1) desk_learning.estimate sets p = random_odds(rr)×lift = lift/(1+rr) (l.152, until the MAX_P cap). Gross expected R is therefore p·rr − (1−p) = lift − 1, independent of the target, and net expected_r = lift − 1 − fee_r(risk_pct). Sorting best_spot by expected_r once n ≥ 20 is just sorting by bucket lift, with ties broken toward WIDER stops (smaller fee_r). That adds no information and biases the scanner toward wide-stop setups.
(2) The 'same plan' claim is false. The desk calls build_plan('long', …, [zone]+resist, …) on 300 bars (desk_calls.candidates), while the chat plan uses all levels on 500 bars, so the entry, stop and even the zone can differ. The drift-guard test only checks the desk's own candidate against itself.
(3) A chat plan outside the desk's sample (distance > MAX_DIST_ATR=4, rr < MIN_RR) would get extrapolated odds.
(4) The odds are conditional on a fill, and the card doesn't say so.
items.change:
- Show the odds line only. Do not re-rank the scanner by expected_r; keep the current score, optionally with a lift lower confidence bound as a tiebreak.
- odds_for computes bucket and rr_level from the chat plan's own zone and targets, and returns None (UI: 'outside the desk's sample') when distance_atr > MAX_DIST_ATR or rr < MIN_RR.
- Label the line 'Desk edge for H4 fresh demand, D1 behind: 41% to T1 before stop if filled (random 29%, n=63)'.
- Replace the drift test with a check that a chat plan on the desk's zone yields the same bucket key.

items.problems:

The moment price touches the zone top, the call becomes 'open'. Step 5 removes the trigger on 'open', which is exactly when price is inside the zone and a 15m confirmation could form.

The ping text 'limit 7.25, TP 8.20, wrong below 7.02, 58%' also attaches the desk's confidence, measured for the limit-at-top entry, to a different entry: the confirmation close with its own suggested stop. That is a misleading number.

fixes.title: A stream that falls back to synthetic never returns to Binance
fixes.note: stream_hub._run calls `await self._run_synthetic(stream); return`, and _run_synthetic is an endless while-True, so the stream never goes back to Binance. The first-connect failure branch also calls mark_binance_down(), demoting REST for every caller. AlertService and SignalAlertService drop synthetic messages, so alerts on that symbol go silent. High severity is justified. Also send a Discord notice when alerts pause (see missing).

fixes.title: One timeout or 429 switches every caller to synthetic candles for 60 s
fixes.note: get_klines and get_range call mark_binance_down() on any non-BinanceRejected exception, including an HTTPStatusError 429 or 418 (market_data.py:155,189). list_symbols caches FALLBACK_SYMBOLS for 3600 s after a single failure (l.244-256). The circuit breaker and the Retry-After pause are the right fix.

fixes.title: Signal checks lose the candle when the feed blips at the close
fixes.note: on_bar_close sets _done[key]=bar_time before _frames(). _frames returns None immediately on a synthetic source (l.731), with no retry. _after_close still calls jobs.ok. The 'never arrived' path also reports ok. Confirmed.

fixes.title: One agent answer over 2000 chars makes every later request fail with a 422
fixes.note: ChatTurn.text has max_length=2000 (schemas.py:337), and ChartWorkspace sends m.text unsliced for the last 10 messages (l.579-582). previous_answer is already sliced to 1500 (chatHistory.ts:69), but history isn't. Truncating in a before-validator is the right fix.

Reproduced:
- 'What would invalidate this?' → features ['support_resistance'], keep False.
- 'Does the daily agree?' → timeframe 1d.
- 'Is RSI overbought here?' and 'why?' → the default features.
merge_overlays then keeps only custom kinds. Ship it together with the lastIntent carry-forward, or the next 'same again' loses the plan anyway.

fixes.note: message() labels only data_source=='synthetic', while a partly synthetic scan is 'mixed' (market_scanner.py:418,452). It also uses result.best(n) with no direction, which mixes in shorts although best_spot exists. tick() re-sends on every due run with no dedupe. Confirmed.

fixes.title: The desk's repeat window is 48 candles on every timeframe, and watched zones can't be called later
fixes.note: REPEAT_BARS = 2×max(ENTRY_BARS) = 48 on every timeframe (agent_desk.py:69). `recent` includes shadow (watched) calls on the same symbol and interval (l.318-321), so any overlapping later candidate is blocked for 48 days on 1d.

fixes.title: Desk paper sizing uses Kelly as the position size, ignoring stop distance and fees
fixes.note: size_for puts Kelly×SIZE_SCALE of equity in as notional (desk_calls.py:228-240), and kelly() uses gross rr. Note the direction of the error: current risk = k×stop%, i.e. UNDER Kelly and inconsistent across stop widths, not over-betting. The fix makes R and paper PnL consistent; with the 1% risk cap the notional often hits MAX_POSITION_PCT, which is fine.

fixes.title: 'What's working now' calls a setup 'working' on 5 zones with no significance test
fixes.note: working_now labels lift ≥1.2 'working' from MIN_RECENT=5 (desk_learning.py:293-313), with no shrinkage. P(≥3 hits of 5 | p=0.33) ≈ 0.21. Zones in one bucket are also correlated (same move, same coins), so the binomial p understates chance; use n ≥ 12 as proposed.

fixes.note: out.verdicts[s.bar] (kimi_agent.py:258), read as verdicts[s.bar] (kimi_service.py:162). Confirmed.

fixes.title: The 'Direction Kimi / +Agent' row counts flat forecasts as wrong
fixes.note: dir_k appends np.sign(kimi_end) == np.sign(real_end) (kimi_agent.py:163). A flat forecast (sign 0) always counts wrong, while +Agent's nudged value is non-zero, so the comparison is unfair. I didn't verify the 3,659/4,975 count; the logic flaw is certain.

fixes.title: Bar replay draws today's Kimi Cooked and stacks future labels on the replay candle
fixes.note: The Kimi effects (AgenticChart.tsx:1155-1211) don't read props.replayTime. Markers keep every signal with time ≥ first candle, and the replay effect sets the candle data to the subset (l.873-892), so later markers snap to the last bar. This is lookahead while practising.

fixes.title: The higher-timeframe confluence tag lands on almost every zone
fixes.note: htf_zones returns every cluster plus every supply/demand zone, and mark_confluence tags any overlap of any size (ta_agent.py:473-491). I didn't verify the 80% figure, but the logic makes a high tag rate certain. The bucket version prefix is required, or desk learning mixes the old and new 'htf' meanings.

fixes.title: The chart, desk, scanner and backtest draw different zones for the same coin
fixes.note: find_swings distance = max(3, min(12, n//60)) (ta_agent.py:241) gives 8, 6 and 5 for 500, 400 and 300 bars. The desk uses 300 bars and the chart 500. This is also why desk-odds-on-plans can't promise 'the same plan'.

fixes.title: supply_demand_zones counts candles instead of visits
fixes.note: tests = ((l[after] <= hi) & (l[after] >= lo)).sum() (ta_agent.py:406). A wick through the whole zone with its low below lo counts 0. Episode counting is the right fix; it changes the fresh/tested buckets, so it needs the same version prefix.

fixes.note: The trendlines block (ta_agent.py:768-779) draws the last two swings with extend_right and never checks the closes after time2. The 41% figure is unverified.

fixes.note: An ungrouped sell has mine=False, so gfills[G] is never debited (paper.py:259-283). A later stop of G sells min(book.held, group_held(G)), which can be the new coins.

fixes.note: sizePlan sets leverage = notional/account (sizing.ts). The PlanCard prints 'needs Nx' (AgentPanel.tsx:320) and orderText adds 'Lev Nx'. For a spot-only user this tells him to buy more than he owns. Rate it medium, not low; it is also a prerequisite for drawing-v2's position tool.

fixes.note: sell_scan uses get_klines for both frames with no closed_only (sell_check.py:196-200), unlike the signal-alert path. Confirmed.

fixes.note: KimiPanel.tsx:120,145 use toISOString().slice(5,16), while the chart formats time with layout.timezone (AgenticChart.tsx:239-245,932).

missing: When alerts go silent because the feed is synthetic (AlertService and SignalAlertService skip synthetic messages; desk, trade manager and signal checks return early), Trick gets no Discord message; at best a Status-tab error. Add an urgent 'Alerts paused since 03:12: Binance feed down' notice after about 3 min, and a 'resumed' notice. This is what a Discord-first trader needs most from the reliability fixes.

LD-prefixed Simple Earn Flexible balances: Binance's /api/v3/account typically lists flexible Earn as LDINJ or LDUSDT. spot_balances (binance_account.py:309) keeps every asset, and positions() builds '{asset}USDT' rows from them. That can create bogus LDINJUSDT holdings, watch alerts and invalid myTrades calls today, and would double-count after holdings-truth merges Earn. Verify on the live key and map LD<asset> to Earn.

Notification coalescing per coin per bar. Holdings lost_support, exit-plan invalidation, desk invalidation and trade-manager structure advice can all fire for INJ on the same daily close; today, and in the package, each sends its own ping. Merge them in the router into one card per symbol.

One probability vocabulary across the plan card, chips and narrator. Desk odds are 'TP before stop, if filled'; Kimi reach is 'touch within N bars, stop ignored'; the track record is a 'backtest win rate'. Define the three once (UI and NARRATE_RULES) and never show two of them for the same target without their qualifiers. Otherwise one card shows three different percentages for T1.

Carry the previous intent forward after question-only turns. ChartWorkspace.tsx:651 overwrites lastIntent with every answer's intent, so the question-only fix alone still breaks 'same again' or 'same on daily' right after 'what would invalidate this?'.

Frontend test runner: vitest is introduced separately by eight items (follow-the-thread, desk-on-chart, kimi-inspector, kimi-odds-anywhere, alert-cards, level-card, command-palette, notification-center). Land package.json with vitest and `npm test` once, as step zero.

Given the request to finish the frontend first, these can ship without backend work:
- notification-center, level-card, watchlist order fix, Dock overflow, spot sizing cap and leverage wording, Kimi replay lookahead, Kimi fetch retry, signal preview direction, KimiPanel local time, localStorage quota banner and pruning;
- the ChatTurn client-side slice(0, 1500).
They give visible wins while the backend items wait.

readers.map:
1. Request: AgentPanel.tsx (prompt box, SHORTCUTS, mostly fixed followUps() chips, cards) → ChartWorkspace.runAnalysis builds the AnalyzeRequest: the last 10 turns sent whole, AI overlays, previous_intent, watchlist, spot_only, detail, coin_note, previous_answer from chatHistory.lastAnswerOn, indicator lengths and up to 500 client candles. It goes through api.analyzeStream (SSE with a 90 s idle timer; falls back to POST /api/agent/analyze).
2. Planning (agent.run_analysis): with an LLM and AGENT_MODE=tools, agent_loop.plan_with_tools gives the model 5 read-only tools (look_at_chart, scan_watchlist, scan_market, market_context, read_kimi) plus draw_on_chart, whose INTENT_SCHEMA has 27 required fields. It may make up to AGENT_MAX_STEPS calls. If that fails it falls back to llm.parse_intent (one structured call; Ollama uses `format`), then to rule_intent (the regex parser, which passes 72/72 rule evals).
3. Execution: spot rules (short → sell check, auto → long). Then symbol, timeframe and navigation are resolved, and about 15 context sources are fetched in parallel. These include HTF frames, window candles, the watchlist and market scans, derivatives, Kimi, futures, calendar and news, session levels, grid, ladder, top-down, sell check, the header overview, chart CVD, vs BTC, Binance positions, the desk and the coach. Several of them only load when a regex matches (KIMI/FUTURES/EVENT/NEWS/HOLDINGS/WORKING/COACH_WORDS).
4. Detection: ta_agent.analyze (SciPy, run in a thread) builds overlays and facts. On top come trade_plan.build_plan plus its track record, take-profits, ladder and sell overlays. merge_overlays then decides what stays on the chart, and build_alerts, trigger alerts and metric alerts are armed. asked_price + ta_agent.price_check answer "what's at 7.15?".
5. Narration: the facts dict goes to ta_agent.describe (the template "built-in writer", used as the fallback) and to llm.narrate_stream. NARRATE_SYSTEM is 7.1k chars with 31 FACTS.* paragraphs; a typical request carries about 2.4k chars of facts. General questions go to general.context + llm.answer (web search on Anthropic/OpenAI only).
6. Response: overlays, plan, scan/setups, steps, facts (shown under "Numbers used") and engine. The frontend renders PlanCard, ScanTable, SetupList, Walk, Ladder, SellList, Sources and TimeframeBadges, plus pins and a localStorage chat history (50 chats).
7. Model ops: model_choice.py switches provider/model at runtime and scores a model on evals/intents.jsonl through parse_intent only, with an Ollama GPU-share check. screenshot.py reads chart images with a vision model and compares them with the detectors. There is no persistent memory beyond per-coin notes and the last answer on the coin, and no check that the numbers in an LLM answer exist in the facts (postmortem.grounded exists but only post-mortems use it).

issues.title: The app's own follow-up chips wipe the trade plan and don't answer the question (rule-parser path)
issues.detail:
After "Give me a long setup", AgentPanel.followUps() offers "What would invalidate this?" and "Does the daily agree?". On the rule path, rule_intent treats both as a fresh analysis. The rule path runs with no model, for 30 s after a connection failure, or after the tool loop and the single-shot plan both fail.

- "What would invalidate this?" hits the follow-up branch (llm.py:824-831, because of the word "this"). It copies previous.features with keep_existing=False.
- "Does the daily agree?" sets timeframe=1d through _TF_PATTERNS and keep=False, so D1 zones are drawn on the 4h chart.
- merge_overlays (agent.py:120-123) then keeps only custom kinds, so plan_entry/stop/target/risk/reward disappear.

Verified on synthetic data: the plan overlay kinds ['demand','plan_entry','plan_risk','plan_reward','plan_stop','plan_target','support'] became ['support'] and ['resistance','support']. The template answer then lists zones and never names the stop or whether D1 agrees. "Is RSI overbought here?", "why?" and "is that a good entry?" also redraw S/R and windows and drop the plan.

Even on the LLM path, a keep_existing answer has no plan in facts (facts['plan'] is only set when intent.trade_plan is set), so "what invalidates this" can only be answered from the 400-char history snippet.

Fix:
- In rule_intent, add a question-only branch ahead of the follow-up branch for these forms: indicator questions (rsi|macd|ema|vwap|bollinger|stoch|sar|cvd), "does the (daily|weekly|4h|htf) agree", "what would invalidate", "is (this|that|it) a good", "why". It should return features=[], keep_existing=True and timeframe=None.
- Have the client send the plan being discussed (see idea 3) so facts carry it.
- Add these conversations to the evals.

issues.title: The narrator is never told which coin it is talking about, or that the data is demo data
issues.detail:
narrate_facts (agent.py:915) comes from ta_agent.analyze facts: timeframe, last_price, zones and so on, but no symbol. llm.narrate/narrate_stream (llm.py:1078-1099) send only CONVERSATION + TODAY + REQUEST + FACTS; CHART: SYMBOL appears only in the planner's _context_block. For "what's the trend here?" the model sees "H4 … 7.80" with no coin, and a 7B model often fills in "Bitcoin".

Also, `source` ('binance'/'synthetic') reaches AnalyzeResponse.data_source but not the facts. During a Binance outage the model therefore narrates synthetic zones as real. The 'demo data' tag lives only in engineNote's meta line, and the Copy button copies the answer text without it.

Fix: set facts['symbol']=symbol and facts['data_source']=source when it isn't binance (also in research rows), and add one NARRATE_SYSTEM sentence: "name the coin; if FACTS.data_source is synthetic, say these are demo numbers".

issues.title: Tool arguments aren't normalised: 'INJ' or 'BTC/USDT' silently turn into synthetic candles, or crash the answer
issues.detail:
_run_tool uses `str(args.get('symbol') or chart.symbol).upper()` with no norm_symbol. A 7B model that writes 'INJ', 'BTC/USDT' or 'solana' sends that string straight to market.get_klines. Binance answers 400, BinanceRejected is raised, and in DATA_SOURCE=auto get_klines (market_data.py:151-158) serves synthetic candles. look_at_chart and read_kimi then return made-up zones tagged data_source 'synthetic', which land in facts['research'] for the narrator.

With DATA_SOURCE=binance, the MarketDataError is a RuntimeError. It isn't in plan_with_tools' except tuple (agent_loop.py:201), so the whole answer fails with a 502.

Fix:
- Run norm_symbol(args['symbol']), check it against market.symbols(), and on a miss return {'error': 'unknown symbol X; use a USDT pair like INJUSDT'} as the tool result.
- Wrap each _run_tool in try/except Exception and return {'error': str(exc)}, so one bad call (e.g. analyze()'s 'Need at least 30 candles' ValueError on a new listing) doesn't end the loop.
- When the chart itself is live, drop or flag research rows whose data_source is synthetic.

issues.title: Ollama ignores tool forcing, and a loop that never calls draw_on_chart throws away its research and pays for a second planning call
issues.detail:
The Ollama branch of tool_turn (llm.py:1040-1054) never reads `force`. The Anthropic branch narrows `offered` to the forced tool; Ollama keeps sending every tool. If qwen2.5:7b keeps calling look_at_chart after AGENT_MAX_STEPS, or answers in plain text (likely for "what is staking?"), plan_with_tools returns None (agent_loop.py:185-187 and the fall-through at 204). That discards `steps` and `research`, and run_analysis then calls llm.parse_intent, a second full planning call with the 2.7k-char INTENT_SYSTEM. On a 3070 Ti that roughly doubles the time to first drawing, and the tools already run are wasted.

Fix:
- For Ollama, when force is a tool name, send only that tool (as Anthropic does). Better still, finish with _structured(INTENT_SYSTEM, digest, INTENT_SCHEMA): Ollama's `format` is grammar-constrained, the tool path isn't.
- Keep research and steps when falling back.
- When tool_calls is empty, also parse a `<tool_call>{json}</tool_call>` or bare JSON from message content.

issues.title: The 8k Ollama context can overflow mid-loop, and Ollama then drops the user's request first
issues.detail:
Every planning round sends TOOLS (json.dumps is 14.7k chars, 10.7k of it INTENT_SCHEMA) and LOOP_SYSTEM (3.5k chars), roughly 4.5-5k tokens. On top come the context block (6 turns × 400 chars, up to 40 overlay rows, the watchlist) and each tool result, which can be up to MAX_RESULT_CHARS=3000 of number-dense JSON.

With OLLAMA_NUM_CTX=8192 the third round can pass the window. Ollama's chat truncation keeps system messages and the last message and drops the oldest others. The first user message, which holds the request and the context, is the first to go, so the model plans from tool results alone.

Separately, agent.py:896-897 puts the unclipped tool results (r['result']) into facts['research'] for the narrator, on top of a 7.1k-char system prompt. Nothing measures any of this.

Fix:
- Read prompt_eval_count from Ollama's /api/chat response, keep the last value in LLMClient.health(), and warn above 90% of num_ctx.
- Send a short research digest instead of raw JSON.
- Use a slimmer schema for local models (idea 6).
- Clip research in narrate facts to the same budget.

issues.title: An agent answer over 2000 chars makes every later request in that conversation fail with a raw 422
issues.detail:
ChatTurn.text has max_length=2000, and ChartWorkspace.runAnalysis (ChartWorkspace.tsx:579-582) sends the last 10 messages' full text as history. A detailed answer that stacks a plan, Kimi lines, holdings, desk calls and actions can pass 2000 chars; the template's detailed answer was already 1,789 chars on synthetic data with no holdings. So can a detailed Claude web-search answer.

Once it happens, every following request fails AnalyzeRequest validation before run_analysis runs. analyzeStream shows the error as a raw JSON string, and it keeps happening until the user starts a New conversation. A pasted prompt over 2000 chars fails the same way (the textarea has no maxLength).

Fix: send `text.slice(0, 1500)` from the client, add a mode='before' validator on ChatTurn.text that truncates instead of rejecting, and set maxLength on the textarea.

issues.title: The built-in writer ignores half of its facts, including what the app's own placeholder suggests asking
issues.detail:
describe() never reads facts.higher_timeframes, facts.indicators (MACD, EMA cross, Bollinger %b, Stoch RSI, VWAP, PSAR, chart CVD), facts.vs_btc or facts.last_time_you_asked, even though run_analysis computes them on every request.

- RSI only appears at ≥70, ≤30 or with a divergence (_momentum_sentence).
- An empty `resistance` list says nothing, while supply/demand get a "no unmitigated zone" sentence.
- Verified: "what's the MACD doing?" gets an answer that never mentions MACD.
- "Is RSI overbought here?" (an AgentPanel.placeholderFor example) says nothing about RSI when RSI is between 30 and 70.
- "how far is the next resistance in %?" doesn't mention resistance.

This is the answer the owner sees whenever qwen is paused or fails. Fix: add topics (macd|ema|bollinger|stoch|vwap|sar|cvd|agree|btc|correlat) to _TOPIC_WORDS, each with a sentence. Examples: an HTF agreement line like "D1 and W1 trend up too, so the timeframes agree", a vs-BTC line, "no resistance above on H4: open space to X", and an RSI value whenever RSI is asked about.

issues.title: "Test it" scores the path the chat doesn't use
issues.detail: ModelChooser._eval → evals.run.eval_case → llm.parse_intent, which is the single-shot fallback. The default AGENT_MODE=tools path (plan_with_tools with free-form tool calls, where Ollama has no schema constraint) is never scored, and neither is narration (grounded numbers, length, naming the coin). Comparing qwen2.5:7b with qwen3:8b in Settings → AI model therefore says little about the answers the owner actually reads. Only 2 of 74 cases are llm_only, and there are no multi-turn cases (the plan-wipe bug above has no test). Fix: see idea 7.

issues.title: No progress, keepalive or Stop while a slow local answer is planned
issues.detail:
The SSE stream sends nothing until on_result, i.e. until planning, every tool call and every context fetch have finished. The market_scan tool alone can wait MARKET_SCAN_WAIT=45 s, and each LLM round has a 30 s LLM_TIMEOUT.

analyzeStream's idle timer (api.ts:133-137, 90 s) can abort a cold-model tool loop as "Request timed out". While busy, the panel shows a fixed "Analysing market structure…", and the send button is disabled with a spinner. stopAnswer exists in ChartWorkspace.tsx:484 but is only reachable through New chat or opening another chat. Steps ("Looked at ETHUSDT on 1d") only appear after planning is done.

Fix:
- Pass an on_step callback through plan_with_tools and emit {type:'step'} SSE events, which also act as keepalives.
- Turn the send button into a Stop button while busy.

issues.title: Small wording and robustness gaps in answers
issues.detail:
- general.template_answer always ends with "Set up a language model in Settings…", even when a model is configured but timed out (agent.py:975-976). Say "the model didn't answer" instead.
- past_answer_facts says "0 hours ago" for answers 3-30 minutes old (agent.py:353, f'{age_h:.0f} hours ago').
- narrate_stream keeps a half-written answer when the stream errors mid-way (llm.py:1106-1111), with no note and engine still set to the model.
- facts['indicators']['lengths'] (≈250 chars of constants) and session_clock are sent to the narrator on every request.
- _clip cuts JSON mid-token with '…' (agent_loop.py:139-141), which confuses small models. Drop whole list items instead.

ideas.title: Grounded narrator for small models: draft, polish, check
ideas.pitch: Ask qwen anything and the answer reads like a trader talking. Every price in it is one the chart actually has, and when the model slips you get the exact built-in sentence instead of a made-up level.
ideas.why: A 7B narrator gets a 7.1k-char system prompt with 31 FACTS.* paragraphs, most of them irrelevant to the question, plus about 2.4k chars of facts. Nothing checks its numbers: postmortem.grounded() exists but only post-mortems use it. The template answer (`fallback`) is already computed for every request and is already grounded, so a small model only needs to rephrase it, not compose from raw JSON. That is the post-mortem pattern (FACTS + DRAFT), applied to chat. It also makes a later switch to Claude safer, since the same guard applies.
ideas.how:
1. Move _leaves/grounded from postmortem.py to a shared app/grounding.py.
2. In llm.py, split NARRATE_SYSTEM into BASE_RULES (about 1.2k chars) and a dict NARRATE_RULES keyed by fact name ('plan', 'kimi', 'your_position', 'spot_buys', ...). narrate_system(detail, keys) includes only the paragraphs whose key is in facts.
3. narrate/narrate_stream get a `draft` argument (agent.py already has `fallback`). The user message becomes REQUEST + DRAFT + FACTS, with the instruction "answer the REQUEST in your own words, lead with what it asks, keep the DRAFT's numbers; add a number only if it is in FACTS".
4. Streaming guard: buffer the stream per sentence (split on '. ' / '? '). Pass each sentence through grounded(sentence, facts, draft) before on_delta. Drop an ungrounded sentence and count it. If over half are dropped, emit the draft instead (a new SSE {type:'replace'}).
5. engine['summary'] becomes e.g. 'ollama:qwen2.5:7b · 1 sentence dropped', and LLMClient keeps a counter for the Status tab.
6. Add facts['symbol']/['data_source'] (issue 2), and precompute distance_pct next to distance_atr in _zone_fact so the model never has to calculate.
ideas.risk: Derived numbers the model legitimately computes (a % gain, a midpoint) get flagged. Precomputing them in facts and allowing small integers (grounded already does) keeps false positives low. Sentence buffering delays the first visible text by one sentence.

ideas.title: Rules first, model only when the rules are unsure
ideas.pitch: Tap "Best spot buys" or "Where do I take profit?" and the drawings land almost instantly. qwen spends its time writing the answer instead of filling a 27-field JSON plan the regex parser already gets right.
ideas.why: rule_intent passes all 72 non-LLM eval cases, and every SHORTCUTS/SUGGESTIONS chip is a phrase it was built for. Yet every LLM request first runs plan_with_tools: about 18k chars of tools and system prompt per round, a few hundred output tokens of draw_on_chart, often two rounds, and a second parse_intent call when the loop fails. On an 8 GB card that is most of the wait, and it is also where a 7B model makes routing mistakes. The model is most useful where the regexes are weak: comparisons, other-timeframe checks, pronouns and vague asks.
ideas.risk: A phrasing the regexes misread confidently gets no second opinion. Mitigate with the unsure markers, the conversation evals (idea 7) and a meta line that shows the fast path was used.

ideas.title: Follow-ups know what 'this' is: the plan, zone or price you are discussing
ideas.pitch: Under a plan, "What would invalidate this?" answers "a close below 7.51, the stop, or an H4 CHoCH under 7.45; the daily still trends up", and leaves the plan on the chart.
ideas.why: previous_intent carries only features/timeframe/max_zones/symbol/trade_plan, not the plan's prices, so the backend can't answer about "this". The rules even redraw and wipe the plan (issue 1). Plan-specific chips ("What would invalidate this?", "Alert me on a 5m confirmation in the zone", "Does the daily agree?") are the most natural thing to ask a spot trader's agent after a setup.
ideas.how:
1. In schemas.py, add AnalyzeRequest.focus: Optional[{kind: 'plan'|'price'|'zone'|'scan', plan?: TradePlan, price?: float, zone?: {low, high, label}, symbols?: list[str], at: int}].
2. In ChartWorkspace.runAnalysis, set focus from the last agent message (its plan, its asked price from facts.price_in_question, or its scan/setups symbols).
3. In agent.py, when focus.kind == 'plan' and the intent draws nothing new, add facts['plan_in_focus'] with:
   - the plan, with live distance to entry/stop in % and ATR;
   - whether the entry filled since focus.at (candles after that time touching the entry);
   - the invalidation: the stop plus the opposite structure break level from structure_breaks;
   - HTF agreement from htf_readings.
   'is that a good entry?' also gets the track record already on the plan.
4. In llm.rule_intent, add the question-only branch from issue 1 (keep_existing=True).
5. In ta_agent.describe, add sentences for plan_in_focus.
6. Add a NARRATE_RULES paragraph (idea 1).
ideas.risk: Low. A stale focus (an old plan on another coin) must be ignored: match the symbol and expire it after a day.

ideas.title: Next-step chips built from what the agent just found
ideas.pitch: Price sits 0.2 ATR above the H4 demand you hold INJ against, so the chip says "Alert me if 7.53–7.57 breaks". Kimi fired B+ two bars ago, so it says "Plan the Kimi B+ long". It reads like an analyst nudging you, not the same five buttons every time.
ideas.why: followUps() in AgentPanel.tsx is mostly fixed strings per answer type; only the Stoch RSI zone varies. The facts already hold everything needed to suggest the one useful next move: zone proximity, Kimi signals, divergences, unusual volume, HTF disagreement, events within 24h, your_position against take-profit zones, and a running desk call. Proactive does not have to mean push notifications: a sharp next question is how a 7B-backed agent feels clever without spending tokens.
ideas.risk: Chips that fire too often become noise. Cap at 4, rank by distance and recency, and unit-test against fixed facts.

ideas.title: "Remember that…": a trader profile the agent carries into every answer
ideas.pitch: Tell it once, "remember I'm holding INJ long-term and only trim above 30" or "I never buy on the 1h", and every later answer and plan respects it. "What do you remember about me?" lists it, and "forget the 1h thing" removes it.
ideas.why: The only memory today is a per-coin note typed into the UI (coin_note) and the last answer on the coin (previous_answer). Grep finds no remember/forget handling. A spot holder's constraints (long-term bags, max buy size, timeframes they trust, coins they won't touch) change what a good answer is. Injecting them is cheap for a 7B model (a few lines in facts), and it is the most 'it knows me' upgrade possible.
ideas.how:
1. New backend/app/memory.py on db.py: migrate('memory', ['CREATE TABLE memory (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, scope TEXT, symbol TEXT, text TEXT, created REAL, last_used REAL)']), with add/list/forget(match)/relevant(symbol, n=8).
2. In llm.rule_intent, add `^\s*(remember|note|don't forget)\b(that)?` → new intent fields memory_add: str and memory_forget: str (keep_existing=True, no features). Add them to INTENT_SCHEMA too, so the planner can set them.
3. In agent.run_analysis, add facts['what_you_told_me'] = memory.relevant(symbol): global rows plus this coin's rows. Planner context: _context_block adds a 'USER PROFILE:' line. trade_plan notes say e.g. "You said you never buy on 1h" when the plan contradicts a memory (simple keyword/timeframe match).
4. Action line: 'Noted: …' or 'Forgot: …'.
5. Settings gets a 'What the agent remembers' list (GET/DELETE /api/memory) so it stays visible and editable.
ideas.risk: Free-text memories can contradict each other or go stale. Keep them explicit (only what the user said, no inferred profiling), show them in Settings, and quote them rather than letting the model reinterpret them.

ideas.title: Two tool profiles: a constrained 'lite' planner for qwen, a full toolbox for Claude
ideas.pitch: On the local model, "does the daily agree with this demand?" gets checked reliably in two quick, schema-locked steps. Switch to Claude and paraphrases like "am I any good at this?" or "what am I sitting on?" just work, with no keyword list to hit.
ideas.why: Ollama tool calls aren't schema-constrained and ignore forcing (issue 4), and the full toolset costs about 5k tokens per round (issue 5). Meanwhile, holdings, the desk record, coaching, news and futures are only fetched when a regex matches (HOLDINGS_WORDS, WORKING_WORDS, COACH_WORDS, NEWS_WORDS, FUTURES_WORDS). A strong model with tools could choose them itself, and a 7B model shouldn't have to.
ideas.risk: Two planners to maintain, and they can drift. The conversation evals (idea 7) must run both. The full toolset raises per-request cost on Claude, so keep AGENT_DAILY_LIMIT in mind.

ideas.title: Conversation evals: score the agent the owner actually talks to
ideas.pitch: Before switching from qwen2.5 to qwen3, or to Claude, one click shows: 'follow-ups kept the chart 18/20, answers grounded 94%, named the coin 100%, 6.2 s median, prompt peaked at 7.1k of 8.2k tokens'.
ideas.why: Today's eval (evals/intents.jsonl) checks single prompts through parse_intent only (issue 8). There are no multi-turn cases, and nothing checks what stays on the chart or whether the narration is grounded. The plan-wipe bug and the missing coin name would both have been caught. Every idea here (rules-first routing, the lite planner, the narrator guard) needs a number to prove it helps.
ideas.how:
1. New backend/evals/conversations.jsonl. Each script has symbol/interval and turns [{prompt, expect: {intent fields...}, chart_keeps: ['plan_*'], chart_has: ['support'], must_mention: ['stop'], must_not: ['short','leverage'], grounded: true}].
2. New evals/converse.py runs run_analysis with DATA_SOURCE=synthetic (deterministic), threading overlays/previous_intent/history/focus exactly as ChartWorkspace.runAnalysis does. It records the intent engine, overlay kinds, the narration with grounding.grounded() and the coin-name check, per-stage latency, and Ollama prompt_eval_count from the response.
3. A rules-only mode runs in CI through pytest (fast, no model).
4. In model_choice.start_eval, add mode 'agent' that runs conversations next to intents; Settings → AI model shows the extra columns.
ideas.risk: LLM runs are slow (about 20 conversations × 3 turns). Keep the agent mode opt-in and show progress the way EvalRun already does.

ideas.title: Make a local model feel alive: live steps, Stop, warm-up and a context meter
ideas.pitch: While qwen thinks you see 'Looking at INJ 1d… Reading Kimi on 4h…', you can hit Stop, the first question after lunch doesn't sit on a cold model load, and Status shows when the 8k context is nearly full.
ideas.why: The SSE stream is silent until on_result, the send button only spins, and stopAnswer isn't reachable from the panel (issue 9). Ollama unloads a model after its idle keep-alive, and the code never sets keep_alive (grep finds none), so the next question pays the reload. Nobody can see how close prompts get to OLLAMA_NUM_CTX (issue 5).
ideas.how:
1. In agent_loop.plan_with_tools, add an on_step(text) callback called before each tool runs. In main.py's stream, put {type:'step', text} on the queue; it also resets the 90 s idle timer in api.ts. In analyzeStream, add handlers.onStep. ChartWorkspace shows the steps in the busy row (AgentPanel.tsx:835-839).
2. In AgentPanel, the send button becomes Stop while p.busy, wired to a new onStop prop that calls stopAnswer.
3. In llm.py, add an OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE setting (default '30m') to every Ollama payload. Add POST /api/llm/warm, which sends an empty /api/generate to load the model; the frontend calls it once when the agent tab opens or the prompt box gets focus.
4. Record prompt_eval_count, eval_count and eval_duration from Ollama's non-streamed and final streamed chunks into LLMClient.health(). The Status tab shows tokens/s and the peak context used against num_ctx.
ideas.risk: A warm-up keeps about 5 GB of VRAM taken for 30 minutes, which matters if the 3070 Ti is also used for games. Make keep_alive configurable and skip warm-up when the provider isn't Ollama.

ideas.title: What-if questions for your bags, including 'if BTC dumps 10%'
ideas.pitch: "What happens to my INJ if BTC drops 10%?" answers: "INJ has moved about 1.4x BTC over 30 days, so roughly −14% to about 6.70, right into the D1 demand 6.75–6.91. Your 120 INJ would be about −$94 from now and still +4% on your 6.45 entry."
ideas.why: Every piece already exists: price_check (the zone at a price and where it goes next if it breaks), vs_btc.beta_30d and correlation_30d, holding_facts (qty, avg_entry, earn). But asked_price's regex excludes percent ("drops 15%") and there is no conditional framing. For a spot holder, 'how bad could it get and where would it stop' is the core question, and a deterministic, numbers-only answer is a natural fit for a 7B narrator.
ideas.how:
1. In agent.py, add a WHAT_IF regex: (what if|if (it|<coin>|btc|bitcoin) (drops|falls|dumps|pumps|rises|goes) (to )?N%?|at PRICE).
2. Resolve the target: a % move on the chart coin gives last×(1±N); 'BTC drops N%' gives last×(1 − beta_30d×N), labelled an estimate from the 30-day beta and skipped when correlation < 0.5.
3. Add facts['what_if'] = {move_pct, price, basis: 'direct'|'btc_beta', beta, correlation, at_price: price_check(df, price, tf, htf_frames), position: {qty, value_now, value_then, pnl_vs_now, pnl_vs_entry}} using your_position plus earn qty.
4. Write a template sentence in ta_agent (reusing _price_sentences) and a NARRATE_RULES paragraph.
5. Add a chip in suggest.py when your_position exists.
ideas.risk: Beta-scaled moves are rough. Label them as an estimate, show correlation, and never present them as a forecast.

ideas.title: Saved questions on a schedule, delivered to Discord
ideas.pitch: Pin "How are my holdings and what should I trim?" to run after every daily close, and have "Is INJ still above the H4 demand?" ping Discord only when the answer changes.
ideas.why: Trick lives in Discord notifications. The brief is fixed sections (BriefSettings has no free prompt), and signal alerts are fixed signal types. Saved shortcuts (ac:my-shortcuts) already capture the questions he repeats, but only on tap, in the browser. run_analysis can run server-side without client candles, and AlertService.send_text and the jobs registry already exist.
ideas.how:
1. New backend/app/standing.py on db.py: table standing_questions (id, prompt, symbol, interval, detail, schedule: 'close:1d'|'times:08:00,20:00', tz, only_on_change bool, last_hash, last_sent).
2. A loop declared in jobs.py ('standing questions'). On each due slot it builds AnalyzeRequest(prompt, symbol, interval, spot_only=True, history=[]) and calls run_analysis with the app's services.
3. Hash the key facts (nearest zone ids, plan entry/stop, sell_check actions, trend) and skip sending when the hash is unchanged and only_on_change is set. Otherwise send summary + plan line via AlertService.send_text, and write to Alerts → History.
4. API: GET/POST/DELETE /api/standing.
5. In AgentPanel, add a clock icon on each saved shortcut chip ('Run this on a schedule') opening a small form.
ideas.risk: Scheduled runs load the GPU, and a model run can fail when Ollama is off. Fall back to the template answer (already automatic) and report failures in Status.

ideas.title: Hover a price in an answer to light it up on the chart
ideas.pitch: Reading "support 7.53–7.57 has held both tests", hover the bold price and that box glows on the chart; click it to scroll the chart there.
ideas.why: emphasize() already bolds prices in answers, and each message carries its overlays. The overlay chips under an answer are static labels with no link to the chart. Connecting words to drawings is the fastest way to trust an answer when four charts and many layers are on screen.
ideas.how:
1. In AgentPanel.emphasize, match each bolded number to m.overlays (box: low ≤ v ≤ high within 0.1%; line: |price − v|/v < 0.1%) and wrap it in a span with onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave/onClick that calls a new onHighlight(overlayId|null) prop. Do the same for the overlay chips.
2. ChartWorkspace keeps highlightId state and passes it to the active AgenticChart.
3. BoxZone and LabeledRay primitives get a `highlighted` option (thicker border, higher alpha). On click, AgenticChart scrolls the price scale or visible range when the level is off-screen.
ideas.risk: Low. The number-to-overlay match can be ambiguous when zones overlap; prefer the overlay whose label appears in the same sentence.

readers.map:
ta_agent.py is the core engine. find_swings uses scipy find_peaks with a 1 ATR prominence and a minimum gap of n//60 bars, then tags each swing HH/LH/HL/LL. cluster_levels builds S/R zones by complete-linkage clustering at 0.6 ATR, merges them up to 1.5 ATR tall and scores them by touches, recency and prominence. supply_demand_zones finds a base followed by an impulse of at least 1.6 ATR and drops a zone once a later candle closes through it. zone_record counts each zone's held and broken tests. htf_zones + mark_confluence tag zones that overlap the next two timeframes. analyze() assembles overlays, facts, the levels list and bias; price_check answers "what's at X"; describe() is the template narrator; indicator_snapshot and htf_readings give indicator and EMA-trend context.
indicators.py: Wilder RSI, MACD, rsi_divergence (two latest swings), structure_breaks (BOS/CHoCH on closes), a 40-bin volume_profile, volume_stats. anchored_vwap is only used by tests.
patterns.py: liquidity_sweeps, fair_value_gaps (tracks partial fills), order_blocks (built on structure_breaks), detect_range, detect_triangle (two fitted lines), detect_double.
trade_plan.py: pick_direction (structure bias beats trend, then whichever side is nearer). build_plan enters at the best entry-grade zone within 6 ATR, puts the stop 0.25 ATR beyond it and places targets on opposing levels at least 0.8R away (R multiples only as a fallback). plan_overlays draws it.
session_levels.py: Asia/London/NY windows with DST worked out in code, previous day/week/month H/L, opening ranges, the time each level was taken, and level_facts for the agent. top_down.py: a 1w→15m walk with stricter filters that skips repeats of higher-timeframe zones. relative.py: vs_btc (1d/7d gap, 30d correlation and beta). scanner.py: watchlist scan (analyze on 300 bars), signals, filters, tickers.
Who reads these detectors: agent.run_analysis (500 bars including the forming one), desk_calls.candidates (300 closed bars), market_scanner.coin_setups (300), backtest/track_record (400-bar causal windows), brief, sell_check and the watchlist scan (300), top_down (400).

issues.title: Higher-timeframe confluence tag is on almost every zone
issues.detail: htf_zones() returns every swing cluster, including single-swing ones, plus every supply/demand zone on the higher timeframe. mark_confluence() tags a zone if any sliver of it overlaps one of those, and adds 0.15 to its score per timeframe. On the real BTCUSDT fixture (tests/data/kimi_BTCUSDT_1h.csv.gz, resampled to 4h/1d/1w, sampled through time) the HTF zones covered 52% of the band within 6 ATR of price. 71% of chart zones in that band got '+D1/W1', and 80% of the zones actually drawn did. What this breaks downstream: desk_calls.bucket_of splits learning into htf/nohtf, but nohtf is nearly empty. In market_scanner.spot_score the gate `if not htf and agree < 0.5` almost never filters, and SPOT_HTF_BONUS goes to almost everyone. Plan cards and track_record notes say 'lines up with D1' by default. Fix: in htf_zones keep S/R with touches>=2 whose zone_record shows broke<=held, keep S/D with tests<=1, and keep pick_nearest(...,3) per side. Require overlap_ratio>=0.3 of the thinner zone and the same polarity (support/demand vs resistance/supply). With that filter coverage fell from 52% to 26% in the same run. Add a version prefix to the desk bucket key so old 'htf' statistics don't mix with the new ones.

issues.title: The chart, desk, scanner and backtest draw different zones for the same coin at the same moment
issues.detail: find_swings sets distance = max(3, min(12, n // 60)), and cluster_levels scores recency as last_idx/(n-1). Both depend on how many candles were loaded. The chart and agent use 500 (AnalyzeRequest.limit; ChartWorkspace sends candles.slice(-500)). desk_calls (agent_desk.CANDLES=300), market_scanner (300), scanner.scan, brief and sell_check use 300. backtest/track_record use WINDOW=400 and top_down uses 400. On the real BTC fixture (1h and 4h, sampled through time) the nearest support/resistance/demand/supply differed between 300 and 500 candles in 91 of 240 cases (38%); synthetic data gave 36/96. So the desk often calls a zone that isn't on the chart, the watchlist 'In demand' badge can disagree with the chart, and the track record and desk priors measure zones the user never sees. The backtest docstring says it 'trades exactly what the agent would have shown'. Fix: take the swing distance from the timeframe or a constant, not from n. Compute recency as exponential decay over absolute bars. Use one ZONE_BARS constant (closed bars) in every consumer, or a shared zones cache keyed by (symbol, tf, last closed bar).

issues.title: supply_demand_zones counts candles, not visits, and can miss a deep test
issues.detail: `tests = ((l[after] <= hi) & (l[after] >= lo)).sum()` (and the supply mirror) counts every candle whose wick lands inside the zone. One visit that lasts 3 candles therefore counts as 3 tests. A candle that wicks through the whole zone and closes back above counts as 0. On the real BTC fixture, 36 of the 125 zones visited exactly once reported tests>=2. A constructed wick-through produced the label 'H4 Demand (fresh) · 1/1 held', where the label and zone_record contradict each other. Level.tests feeds plan.zone_fresh, track_record's setup choice, desk_calls' fresh/tested bucket, the backtest's fresh-only arming and top_down's MAX_TESTS=1, which rejects a zone touched once over two candles. Fix: count episodes of `l <= hi` (demand) or `h >= lo` (supply) after the impulse, the same way zone_record and patterns._episodes already do.

issues.title: Trendlines are drawn after price has already broken them
issues.detail: analyze() 'trendlines' draws a line through the two latest swing highs if they fall (or lows if they rise), with extend_right=True and the label 'Descending resistance' / 'Ascending support'. Nothing checks the closes after the second anchor. On the real BTC 1h/4h fixture, 135 of 330 drawn lines (41%) had already been closed through and were still labelled resistance or support. Minimum fix: after time2, if any close crosses the line by more than 0.1 ATR, drop the line or relabel it 'broken N bars ago'. The full fix is idea 'Trendline engine v2'.

issues.title: change_24h is not a 24h change
issues.detail: change_24h takes `df[df.time >= last.time - 86400]` and uses the first bar's open. On 1d candles that is yesterday's open, so it returns a 2-day change: a test frame gave 18.18% where the true figure is 8.33%. On 1w it returns the change since the week's open; on 4h it covers 24–28h. It is used for the brief's '(x% 24h)' (brief._coin on the brief's interval, user-selectable), sell_check SellSignal.change_pct, ScanResult.change_pct, and as market_scanner's fallback when no ticker is available. Fix: use the close of the last bar that closed at or before now−24h, or the 24h tickers that scanner.tickers already fetches.

issues.title: Detectors read the still-forming candle in the agent, scanner and brief
issues.detail: run_analysis, scanner.scan and brief._coin run analyze() on get_klines output, which includes the open bar; the chart also sends getCandles() with the live bar. As a result structure_breaks can report 'Structure flipped bearish on the last candle' and then lose it before the candle closes. The same flicker affects S/D invalidation (closes_after), sweeps ('closed back inside'), FVGs, and build_plan.pick_direction, which takes that bias as the plan's side. The desk (closed list), backtest (closed_only) and signal_alerts (closed_only) use closed bars, so the agent can disagree with what the desk and alerts saw. Fix: run structure, sweeps and zone invalidation on kimi_service.closed_only(...) bars, and use the live price only for distances and 'inside'. Alternatively, mark any fact that comes from the forming bar as provisional.

issues.title: Zone ranking measures distance in percent while the plan builder uses ATR
issues.detail: pick_nearest ranks by `score - 8 * |mid-last|/last`. On 15m BTC (ATR about 0.25%) a strong zone 6 ATR away loses only 0.12, so far zones beat near ones. On 1d INJ (ATR about 6%) a zone 1.5 ATR away loses 0.72, so the strongest zone is almost never drawn. trade_plan.build_plan penalises 0.12 per ATR instead, so the two rankings disagree, and this selection feeds the desk, scanner and top-down. Fix: rank by score - k*distance_atr with k≈0.1 in both places.

issues.title: Plan R and scanner ranking ignore fees
issues.detail: PlanTarget.rr and market_scanner.score_setup / MIN_RR use gross R. desk_calls already has fee_r(). On 5m/15m scans ('best 5m setups') risk_pct is often around 0.3%, so 0.1% per side is about 0.67R: a '2R' plan nets about 1.3R, and tight-stop plans rank highest exactly where fees hurt most. Fix: add rr_net using FEE_PCT (or the user's fee from position sizing), rank and filter on net R, and add a note when fees take more than 25% of the reward.

issues.title: Top-down walk treats a zone of the opposite kind as confirmation
issues.detail: build_step marks a lower-timeframe zone as confirming any higher-timeframe zone it overlaps by more than 50%, whatever its kind. An H4 demand sitting inside a D1 supply is reported as 'It confirms D1 Supply …' and is not drawn, although buyers defending inside a sellers' zone is a conflict, not confirmation. Fix: only the same side confirms (support/demand vs resistance/supply); otherwise draw the zone and add the note 'inside D1 supply: conflict'.

issues.title: The watchlist scan's HTF-confluence signal can never fire
issues.detail: scan() calls analyze(df, SCAN_INTENT, interval) with no confluence frames, so summarize()'s '{tfl} {k} lines up with D1' branch never fires in the watchlist scan or in the brief (brief._coin does the same). Either pass higher_timeframes frames (cached klines) or remove the branch.

issues.title: Narrator formats each end of a price range with its own decimals
issues.detail: _zone_sentence, _price_sentences and the sweep/FVG/OB lines call _fmt(z['low']) with no reference price, so a range that crosses a power of ten prints as '99.000–100.20' (reproduced); for INJ near $10 it reads '9.9871–10.012'. Pass `last` as ref everywhere in describe(), as is already done for the ATR.

issues.title: Double top/bottom stays 'in play' after its target is reached
issues.detail: detect_double has no played-out state. On the BTC fixture 23 of 94 reported patterns had already reached their measured-move target but were still listed under 'Patterns in play: double top … (confirmed)'. Fix: add target = neckline ∓ height and state 'played out' once it is reached, then drop the pattern or say so.

issues.title: vs_btc calls high-beta coins stronger than BTC
issues.detail: 'strength' compares the raw 7d gap against ±2%. A coin with beta 1.6 shows as 'stronger than BTC' on any BTC up-week from beta alone, and as 'weaker' on any down-week. Fix: compute alpha_7d = coin_7d − beta_30d × btc_7d and judge strength on that, keeping the raw gap as a separate field.

issues.title: Opening-range levels are never marked as taken
issues.detail: _level_rows hard-codes taken=False for opening-range rows, so level_facts can name an OR high that price has crossed many times as the 'nearest untaken level'. Fix: compute first_cross after the OR close, as is done for sessions and periods.

ideas.title: Top-down verdict: structure bias, premium/discount and regime per timeframe
ideas.pitch: Before I buy INJ, one line should tell me 'D1 up, price in D1 discount at D1 demand, H1 flipped up 3 candles ago: aligned buy', or 'wait: H1 hasn't flipped yet'.
ideas.why: Today the top-down walk only draws levels. The trend reads (htf_readings, market_scanner.trend_of) are EMA-based and can contradict the swing-structure bias that describe() also prints ('trending up … structure flipped bearish'). A precomputed verdict is also what a 7B local model narrates well, and the desk can learn whether the verdict adds edge.
ideas.how: In top_down.py add structure_bias(df, tf) built on find_swings + structure_breaks. It returns: swing trend (HH+HL = up, LH+LL = down, else range); the last BOS/CHoCH with bars ago; the dealing range (the swing high and low bracketing the last break leg) with price's position in it (discount <50%, OTE 62–79% retrace, premium >50%); a regime from Kaufman efficiency ratio ER20 (<0.2 = chop) and the ATR percentile; and the valid zone price sits in (valid_zones). verdict(biases) then gives aligned buy / wait (what's missing) / avoid (1d down and price in premium). Add bias[] and verdict to TopDownResult (mirror in frontend/lib/types.ts), compute them in walk(), whose frames are already fetched, and show them in walk_facts and describe_walk. Compute a light version in agent.run_analysis from htf_frames, which are already loaded, so every answer opens with it. Add 'structure_agree' to desk_calls Candidate.features next to the EMA 'agree' so desk_learning can compare the two.
ideas.risk: The thresholds are heuristics, and the dealing range is ambiguous inside ranges. Show the verdict as a read, not a signal, until desk results confirm it.

ideas.title: Range spring and deviation detector (Wyckoff for spot)
ideas.pitch: Tell me when INJ sweeps the bottom of a month-long range and closes back inside: that's my best spot buy. A fake breakout above the range top is my cue to trim.
ideas.why: detect_range and liquidity_sweeps both exist but are never combined. A spring (sweep of the range low, close back in) is the highest-R spot entry and doesn't need a short. The mirror case (upthrust) fits sell_check's trim logic.
ideas.how: Add range_events(df, atr_v) to patterns.py. Build the range box from the core of the range, the 5th–95th percentile of highs and lows excluding the last k bars, because detect_range's h.max/l.min would absorb the spring wick and hide it. Spring = low < box_low − 0.1 ATR and close >= box_low; stronger with volume >= 1.3x the 20-bar average; a later candle testing the spring low and holding is the confirmation. Deviation is the mirror at box_high. Also detect breakout + backup (close above the box, then a retest that holds the box high). Wire it in: ta_agent.analyze 'patterns' (box plus a 'Spring' marker, and facts); signal_alerts SignalId 'range_spring' and 'range_deviation' on closed bars, so Preview works through the existing machinery; backtest Setup 'spring_long' (entry at the spring candle's close, stop at spring low − 0.25 ATR, target range mid or high) so track_record can quote it; desk SPOT_KINDS candidate 'spring'; sell_check 'trim' on a deviation.
ideas.risk: Few events per coin, so backtest samples are small; ranges must be validated, or every chop becomes a 'range'.

ideas.title: Stops set from this coin's own wicks
ideas.pitch: Put my stop where INJ's wicks into demand usually stop, not a flat 0.25 ATR under the zone where it gets hunted.
ideas.why: Every plan, desk call and backtest uses the same 0.25 ATR buffer (trade_plan.build_plan, BacktestRequest.stop_buffer_atr). postmortem already finds the lesson 'stopped, then T1 was reached: the stop sat inside the noise'. The data to size the buffer is already in the zone tests zone_record walks over.
ideas.how: In ta_agent.zone_record, store pierce depth for each held test: (zone_low − lowest low during the test) / ATR, mirrored for ceilings. Add pierce_profile(df, zones, atr_v) returning p50/p75/p90 per zone family on the window. build_plan gets an optional buffer: stop = zone.low − clamp(p75 + 0.05, 0.25, 1.0) × ATR, with the note 'stop beyond 75% of past wicks into H4 demand on INJ (0.46 ATR)'. Add stop_buffer 'adaptive' to the backtest, computed causally per window, so track_record and the desk priors measure the same rule. Store the buffer in desk features.
ideas.risk: Wider stops lower R:R and shift desk sizing and edges. A/B it in the backtest before making it the default.

ideas.title: Trendline engine v2 with break and retest states
ideas.pitch: Only draw a trendline that has really held, at least 3 touches, and tell me when it breaks and when the retest holds.
ideas.why: The current lines are two-point lines, and 41% of them were already closed through (measured on real BTC). Trendline breaks with a retest are a classic spot entry, and today nothing alerts on them.
ideas.how: Add trendlines(df, highs, lows, atr_v, lookback=250) to patterns.py. Every pair of the last ~10 swing highs (lows) defines a candidate line. Touches = swings and bar wicks within 0.15 ATR between the first anchor and the last bar. Reject a line if any close between its first anchor and last touch is beyond it by more than 0.1 ATR; require 3+ touches and a sane slope; keep the best line per side by touches × span. State: intact / broken (first close beyond it by ≥0.2 ATR, with bars ago) / retested (after the break, a wick back to the line that closes on the break side). Replace the 2-point block in ta_agent.analyze, with labels like 'H4 Descending resistance (4 touches)' or '(broken 3 bars ago, retest held)'. Add Level kind 'trendline' using the line's value at the next bar, so build_plan can target it. Add signal_alerts 'trendline_break_up'.
ideas.risk: Costs O(k²·n) per call, which is fine at k≈10. Keep one line per side to avoid clutter.

ideas.title: Liquidity pools: equal highs and lows plus session and period highs and lows as targets and sweep grades
ideas.pitch: Show me where the stops are resting (equal highs, untaken PDH or Asia high) and set my take-profit just under them.
ideas.why: Sweeps today only use major 1-ATR swings, and targets ignore where liquidity sits. session_levels already computes PDH/PDL/PWH and session highs/lows with taken_at, but nothing in trade_plan or patterns uses them.
ideas.how: Add liquidity_pools(df, highs, lows, atr_v, session=None) to patterns.py. Equal highs (lows) = 2+ swing highs (lows) within 0.1 ATR, using find_swings at prominence 0.5 ATR, at least 5 bars apart and never traded through. Add the untaken session and period levels from SessionLevelsService (*_taken_at is None). Each pool gets {side, price, members, kind, age}. Uses: build_plan adds pools on the target side as Level kind 'liquidity', front-run by 0.1 ATR (label like 'T1 under equal highs ×3'). liquidity_sweeps gets grade 'pool' when the swept level is an equal low or PDL; that grade reaches signal_alerts' sweep text and the zone_triggers sweep confirmation. Draw dotted 'EQH ×3' rays, and add a describe sentence 'Untapped liquidity above at 26.40'.
ideas.risk: Session levels add a cached 30m/4h fetch; cap at the nearest 2 pools per side.

ideas.title: Volatility squeeze (coiling) detector and firing alert
ideas.pitch: Ping me on Discord when one of my coins has been coiling for weeks and then closes out of the coil on volume.
ideas.why: Compression comes before expansion, and spot traders mostly profit from expansion. Nothing measures volatility state today: Kimi only has vol_regime on its forecast, and 'squeeze' appears only in an agent regex.
ideas.how: Add squeeze(df, look=180) to indicators.py: BB(20,2) width percentile over `look` bars, ATR14/ATR100, and the count of inside bars and NR7 bars in the last 10. Coiling = width percentile ≤10 and ATR ratio ≤0.75 for 8+ bars. The coil box is the high/low since coiling began. firing_up = a closed bar closing above the box with volume ≥1.5x the 20-bar average (firing_down mirrors it). Add facts['volatility'] to analyze() (cheap, always on) and a describe sentence 'coiling for 23 candles, Bollinger width in its lowest 8% of 6 months'. Add 'coiling' and 'breakout_up' filters to scanner.score plus a watchlist badge. Add signal_alerts 'squeeze_fire_up' / 'squeeze_fire_down', and backtest setup 'squeeze_long' for a track record.
ideas.risk: Breakouts often fail; the volume filter and backtest calibration matter.

ideas.title: Detector report card and parameter tuning harness
ideas.pitch: Show me, per timeframe, which detectors actually beat random levels on my coins, and tune them from data.
ideas.why: Every constant (impulse 1.6 ATR, cluster 0.6 ATR, prominence 1 ATR, stop 0.25 ATR, the HTF overlap rule) is hand-set. The bugs above (confluence tag on 80% of drawn zones, zones depending on window length) went unnoticed because no measurement guards detection quality. The desk's random-walk baseline already gives the right yardstick.
ideas.how: Add backend/evals/detectors.py, run as `python -m evals.detectors --symbols … --tf 1h,4h,1d`. Walk forward over candle_store SQLite data using the backtest's causal window loop. For each detector family (fresh demand/supply, S/R by touch count, OB, FVG, sweep, double, triangle, trendline, spring), score the first touch with zone_record's rule (reaction of 1 ATR before a close 0.25 ATR through) against random control bands of the same height, ATR distance, side and time. Report lift with a Wilson CI per family and timeframe, and grid-search the key constants with walk-forward splits. Write JSON under .cache plus a table. Add a pytest on the BTC fixture that asserts the fresh-demand lift stays above a floor, so refactors can't quietly make detection worse.
ideas.risk: Needs months of cached candles (fetched once). Tuning to a single regime can overfit; use time splits.

ideas.title: Period opens, Monday range and anchored VWAPs
ideas.pitch: Tell me whether INJ is above or below its weekly, monthly and yearly open, the Monday range, and the VWAP anchored at the last big low.
ideas.why: These are among the most widely watched crypto levels and are cheap to compute. indicators.anchored_vwap is already written but only used by tests. session_levels already has the fetches, period windows and taken_at logic to reuse.
ideas.how: session_levels.compute_levels gains: 'opens' (day/week/month open from the 4h frame, quarter/year open from one extra cached 1d fetch in SessionLevelsService.get); 'monday' (this week's Monday UTC high/low from 30m bars, live while Monday runs, with taken_at); and 'avwaps' (indicators.anchored_vwap anchored at the last major 1d swing high and low via find_swings(prominence_atr=3), and at the yearly open). level_facts adds above_opens / below_opens and 'reclaimed/lost the weekly open N bars ago', with a sentence in level_lines. The frontend session-levels layer draws 'W open', 'M open', 'Mon H/L' and 'AVWAP' rays.
ideas.risk: More lines on the chart; default to just W/M open and the Monday range.

ideas.title: Relative-strength rotation board for the watchlist
ideas.pitch: Which of my coins is holding up best against BTC this week, and which one's chart against BTC is breaking out?
ideas.why: relative.vs_btc only reads one coin at a time and ignores beta. A spot trader choosing what to buy needs leaders and laggards across the watchlist.
ideas.how: Add rs_board(daily: dict[str, df], btc) to relative.py. Per coin: 7d/30d return, 60d beta, alpha = coin − beta × BTC, the RS line (coin/BTC) and whether it is at a 30/90-day high or low, RS swing structure via find_swings on the RS line, and downside capture on BTC down days. Add GET /api/watchlist/rs, scanner filter 'strongest', agent facts for 'which coin is strongest?', and a 'Leaders/laggards vs BTC' section in the brief. Data: 120 1d candles per watchlist coin, served from the candle cache.
ideas.risk: Daily data reacts slowly; RS signals can whipsaw in chop.

ideas.title: Kimi Cooked levels as a confluence factor the desk learns from
ideas.pitch: When an agent zone lines up with a Kimi S/R level or the golden pocket, show it, and let the desk find out whether my indicator adds edge.
ideas.why: Kimi's levels (with reach odds) and Fib golden pocket are computed for every chart, but the desk, plans and scanner never use them (grep shows no 'kimi' in desk_calls, agent_desk, trade_plan or market_scanner). It's Trick's own indicator, and measuring its value to his own calls is exactly what the learning loop is for.
ideas.how: When KimiService has a cached result for (symbol, tf), use only that and never force a run. Tag zones overlapping an active KimiLevel zone_low..zone_high, or KimiFib.pocket_low..pocket_high: Zone.meta['kimi'] = {'odds': lv.odds, 'pocket': bool}; label '+ Kimi 64%'; Level.kimi. Add desk_calls features['kimi'] (as a feature first, a bucket dimension later), so desk_learning's bucket_table and working_now can show lift with and without Kimi. describe() gets 'Kimi has a 64% support at 24.10 inside this zone'.
ideas.risk: Kimi runs on 5000 bars, so only cached results keep the desk loop fast. A new bucket dimension thins the data, so start with logged features.

readers.map:
agent_desk.AgentDesk: 45 s after each 1h/4h/1d close it runs desk_calls.candidates (ta_agent.analyze with the HTF frames) on every watchlist coin. Each support or demand zone at most 4 ATR below price becomes a DeskCall. Per coin and timeframe, one becomes a real call (best expected R, confidence >= min, ER >= 0.1R, gets a quarter-Kelly paper position via size_for); the rest are 'watched' (shadow=True).
desk_calls.score_call re-scores every record every 2 min on 5m/15m/1h candles with journal.evaluate_entry rules (only candles after the call, stop first, fees). level_reach also records level_hit and reach_r against the full level, separate from the take-profit, so a learned TP can't bias the learning.
desk_learning.estimate: p = 1/(1+R) random-walk odds x lift. The lift is shrunk in steps: timeframe+kind across every coin, then the bucket (fresh/HTF/trend agreement), then the coin (track_record backtest as pseudo-calls plus the coin's live rows), with a 90-day half-life. take_profit learns a 70-90% TP fraction from reach_r. calibration, verdict, bucket_table and working_now only report; nothing feeds back into the confidence.
track_record.TrackRecordService runs backtest.backtest_frame (detectors re-run every 5 bars, first touch, next-level target, 50-bar hold) per coin/TF/setup and caches it 30 min to 6 h. It is both the desk's coin-level prior and the 'track record' line on plan cards.
kimi_agent (called from kimi_service._agent): per chart, a walk-forward decayed ridge on 5 causal features corrects Kimi's forecast end and marks Kimi signals take/skip. Each switch turns on at t >= 1.65, recomputed from scratch on every candle.
journal.evaluate_entry replays your logged trades on 1m candles. postmortem.PostMortemService writes rule-based lessons (stop_too_tight, gave_back, ...) with an optional LLM rewrite that is kept only if grounded() passes. The weekly review counts lessons that keep coming back.
level_review.LevelLog logs the zones the chat agent draws and sorts them weekly into held, broke or untested.
Loops that close today: desk outcomes feed the desk's lift and TP fraction. Loops that don't: calibration, post-mortem lessons, level review, Kimi verdicts (never reach Discord alerts), desk odds (never reach your plans or the scanner), and sell/trim signals (hand-set scores, never scored).

issues.title: The repeat window is 48 candles on every timeframe, and a watched zone can't be called later
issues.detail: REPEAT_BARS = 2 * max(ENTRY_BARS.values()) = 48 (line 69) is applied in candles to every timeframe. In _coin (lines 318-321), any zone overlapping a record from the last 48 candles is dropped before scoring. On 1d that is 48 days, although a 1d buy expires after 10 days (ENTRY_BARS['1d']); on 4h it is 8 days against a 3-day entry window.
