It also blocks calls: _coin makes at most one call per coin per run (line 348: shadow unless out.call is None) and none while the coin has a call running (can_call). So the deeper zone B, seen next to called zone A, is saved as watched. When A is invalidated and price heads into B, B can't be called for 48 candles. That is exactly the ladder buy a spot trader wants. Nothing records why a zone was only watched. Fix: make the repeat window per timeframe (2 x ENTRY_BARS[tf]), or block only while the earlier record on that zone is still waiting. Store a skip_reason on watched zones (capacity / running_call / low_confidence / er). On the next run, promote a still-waiting watched zone whose reason was capacity or running_call to a call (link it via features['from_watched'] and keep the watched copy out of learning).

issues.title: The random-walk baseline ignores the hold window
issues.detail: random_odds (line 59) = 1/(1+R) is the no-skill chance of reaching +R before -1 with unlimited time. But level_reach (desk_calls.py 277-282) counts a level not reached within HOLD_BARS as a miss. A driftless simulation with sigma ~ ATR/1.6 gives about 3% instead of 9% for a 10R level with 1 ATR of risk on the 4h 60-bar window. For 3R with 2 ATR of risk on the 1d 45-bar window it gives about 13% instead of 25%. So the learned lift mixes zone skill with how often the clock ran out, and it transfers wrongly between near and far levels and between tight and wide stops. Under this baseline ER = p*(rr+1) - 1 - fee_r = lift - 1 - fee_r (before the MIN_P/MAX_P clip and the TP fraction): R cancels out, so the ranking prefers wide-risk zones (lower fee_r), which is exactly where the window bites hardest. Fix: baseline_odds(R, risk_atr, hold_bars, sigma) = two-barrier first-passage probability within T, from a precomputed table on a = R*risk/(sigma*sqrt(T)) and b = risk/(sigma*sqrt(T)) or the image-series formula. Use it in _count, estimate, _backtest, working_now and take_profit, and store sigma*sqrt(T) in DeskCall.features at call time.

issues.title: The coin level of the edge is confounded by the coin's setup mix
issues.detail: In estimate() (lines 140, 148-149), on_coin pools every bucket the coin has on that timeframe and kind, plus the backtest. It computes an absolute hits/expected ratio and then shrinks it toward the bucket's lift. Example: INJ 4h history is mostly 'tested, trend against' zones (lift ~0.7). A fresh, D1-behind, with-trend INJ zone (bucket lift 1.5) then gets pulled toward 0.7 once INJ has ~10 finished zones. The coin's mix of setups overrides the setup in front of it. Fix: model the coin as a residual on top of the bucket. expected_c = sum of w * odds(c) * lift_of(c.bucket) from the two parent levels; coin_mult = _shrink(hits, expected_c, 1.0); p = odds * bucket_lift * coin_mult. Do the same for the backtest prior and compare it with the timeframe+kind lift, since demand_long backtests only fresh zones.

issues.title: Paper sizing treats Kelly as the position size and ignores the stop distance and fees
issues.detail: size_for (lines 228-242) uses quarter-Kelly as the share of the wallet put into the position. Kelly's fraction is the share of equity lost at the stop. As a result the dollars at risk are notional x risk_pct: a call with a 10% stop risks 10x what a 1% stop call risks at the same confidence and R. The desk wallet's equity curve is then dominated by wide-stop calls and no longer tracks the R record. kelly() (line 223) also uses gross rr. With fee_r 0.3R, p 0.5 and rr 2, the gross fraction is 0.25, about 2.8x the net p/(1+fee_r) - q/(rr-fee_r) ~ 0.09. Fix: risk_budget = SIZE_SCALE x net Kelly x equity (capped at e.g. 1%); notional = risk_budget / (risk_pct/100); then apply the 15% cap and the free cash. Use net Kelly in the ok check too (agent_desk.py line 338). Update test_sizing_scales_with_confidence_and_respects_the_cash.

issues.title: Kimi take/skip verdicts are keyed by bar and collide
issues.detail: signal_filter stores out.verdicts[s.bar] (line 258) and kimi_service._signals looks verdicts up by s.bar (line 162). The engine's register() (kimi_v574.py ~967-987) can register several signals on the same bar i: harmonics, pattern break-outs, regular/hidden DIV and Early, in either direction. A later signal's verdict overwrites an earlier one, so a B+ can show the take/skip and predicted R of a harmonic, or of a short on the same candle. Fix: key verdicts by (bar, typ, dir) in both places.

issues.title: Evidence is counted as independent, though coins move together and zones are re-recorded
issues.detail: _count and _shrink weight every finished zone as an independent sample. When 40 coins' demand zones fail together in one market-wide flush, that counts as 40 pieces of evidence. A zone still standing is also re-recorded every 48 candles (agent_desk REPEAT_BARS). With K_EXPECTED = 3 expected hits (~10 zones), one bad day can swing the 'every coin' lift, and with it every call's confidence, for weeks. Fix: weight rows by 1/sqrt(n) within (interval, UTC day) clusters, or cap a cluster at the weight of 3 zones, and show 'effective N' next to n. Placebo pairing (see ideas) removes the market move altogether.

issues.title: 'Working now' calls a setup working on 5 zones with no test
issues.detail: working_now (lines 296-314) labels a setup 'working' at raw lift >= 1.2 on as few as MIN_RECENT = 5 zones, with no shrinkage and no test. Example: 3 hits on 5 zones at 33% odds shows as 1.8x 'working', but that happens about 21% of the time by chance. agent.py (lines 848-851) passes this straight to the narrator for 'what's working right now?', so you are told noise is an edge. Fix: compute the Poisson/binomial tail probability against expected hits and a shrunk lift. Say 'working' only when p < 0.1 and n >= 12, otherwise 'too early', and put n in the answer.

issues.title: The backtest prior trades a different setup and double-counts the live period
issues.detail:
_backtest (lines 118-129) turns the track record into pseudo-calls, but:
- demand_long backtests only fresh zones, while the desk's buckets include tested ones.
- backtest.target_for aims at S/R cluster lows and swing highs, not supply, and holds 50 candles against the desk's 72/60/45.
- The target distance is reverse-engineered from avg_r as (avg_r + 1 - w)/w, which timeouts and fees distort, even though every BacktestTrade has its exact entry, stop and target.
- The backtest covers the last ~year (track_record.history_bars), which includes the desk's own live calls, so the same zones count twice.
Fix now: add TrackRecord.expected_wins = sum of random_odds((target-entry)/(entry-stop)) over its trades, and cut the backtest at the earliest live desk record for that coin/TF. Later, replace it with the desk replay (see ideas).

issues.title: Kimi + Agent switches can turn on by chance and flicker; shorts are mixed into a spot judgement
issues.detail: Both switches (forecast_fix line 190, signal_filter line 282) are recomputed from scratch on every candle at one-sided t >= 1.65 (MIN_T), on every coin x timeframe Kimi runs on. About 5% of charts switch on by chance, and a chart whose t hovers near 1.65 flips the Kimi + Agent line and the X-greying on and off between candles. signal_filter also judges longs and shorts together, though Trick can only act on longs (a B- is a trim). Fix: hysteresis (on at t >= 2.0, off below 1.3), with the state stored per (symbol, interval) in the db; require both halves of the walk-forward to improve; and add a long-only judgement (B- scored as an exit) for the spot view.

issues.title: Level review counts 'touched and not broken yet' as held
issues.detail: In judge() (lines 60-81), 'held' means price touched the zone and no candle has closed through it yet. A zone touched on the last candle counts as held with a 0.1% bounce, which inflates 'Held X%'. Older zones are judged on coarser candles (_interval_for can fall back to 1d), where a break needs a daily close through the zone, which is more lenient. There is also no baseline for what a random band of the same width would do. Fix: report 'holding' until N candles of the zone's timeframe have passed since the touch (or price has moved 1 ATR away); judge on the zone's own timeframe via get_range; quote the placebo rate once the desk records controls.

issues.title: The confidence verdict mixes watched zones with calls but says 'calls'
issues.detail: summary() (lines 221-237) computes calibration and verdict over self._real(), which includes watched (shadow) zones. Yet the verdict says 'On N closed calls', and DeskPanel says 'how often calls in each range reached the take-profit'. brief_lines (lines 512-513) prints the calls' 'X/Y reached the take-profit' next to a verdict computed mostly on watched zones. The calls, the selected subset that is actually traded, can be miscalibrated while the pooled number looks fine. Fix: return calibration for calls and for calls + watched separately, label each, and have the brief use the calls' figure.

issues.title: Higher-timeframe frames include the still-open candle
issues.detail: _coin (lines 313-316) fetches HTF candles with get_klines and keeps the still-open D1/W1 candle. A call's htf/agree bucket and its HTF zones then depend on how far into that candle the 1h/4h close happened: the same zone can land in different buckets hour to hour, and no replay can reproduce it. kimi_service already uses closed_only. Fix: apply closed_only(candles, h, now) to the HTF candles before candles_to_df.

issues.title: Post-mortem Kimi levels are 'known' before Kimi could show them
issues.detail: kimi_context (line 245) treats a Kimi level as active from lv.time_start. The port creates levels with born = i - plen (kimi_v574.py line 856: Ls.append([px, i - plen, ...]), plen 2-15 and adaptive), so a level can count as active at entry up to 15 candles before Kimi confirmed it. Levels evicted from LEV since then (maxSR cap) are missing entirely. The docstring calls this approximate. The fix is cheap: carry the confirm bar on each level (the way Signal.pivot_bar was added) and require confirm_time <= taken_at.

issues.title: The 'Edge' column isn't the edge the desk uses
issues.detail: bucket_table (lines 270-287) computes Edge as _shrink(hits, exp, BASE_LIFT): shrunk toward 1.0 and over CLOSED rows only. estimate() shrinks each bucket toward the timeframe+kind lift and uses every row whose level outcome is known. So the Edge shown under By setup differs from the one applied to calls. Fix: return estimate()'s per-level values for each bucket, or show both.

issues.title: Wallet reset isn't saved
issues.detail: reset_wallet (lines 419-422) sets paper_group = None in memory only (no _save) and leaves notional and size_pct on old calls. After a restart, old calls get their old group back, and the call and brief texts still describe positions that no longer exist. Fix: clear the paper fields and persist the touched calls.

ideas.title: Placebo twins: each zone gets a random-line control
ideas.pitch: Every time the desk looks at a buy zone, it also tracks a random price line with exactly the same stop and target distance. After a month I see 'my zones reached the level 41% of the time, random lines 33%', with drift, fees and the clock all priced in.
ideas.why: Today the edge is measured against a theoretical walk with no drift, no time limit and no fill mechanics. In a bull month every buy zone looks skilled; in a flush every one looks broken (issues on the baseline and correlated evidence). Paired controls on the same coin, at the same moment, with the same scoring, cancel the market move and the window. They also give a McNemar test of whether the detectors add anything at all, and they give level_review its missing baseline.
ideas.how:
1) desk_calls.candidates also returns every detected level.
2) New desk_calls.control_for(cand, df, levels, seed): pick an entry uniformly in [live - MAX_DIST_ATR*ATR, live] that overlaps no detected support/demand. seed = hash(symbol, interval, bar), so it is reproducible. Copy the candidate's geometry in ATR units: stop = entry - risk_atr*ATR, tp_level = entry + level_atr*ATR, same ENTRY/HOLD windows.
3) agent_desk._coin saves it as a DeskCall with shadow=True, a new control: bool field and features['control_of'] = the candidate's id. score() scores it with the unchanged score_call/level_reach, in the same symbol/resolution group, so no extra candle fetches.
4) desk_learning: keep controls out of the bucket learning in learnable(). New placebo_table() gives per interval and R-bin: zone vs control hit rates, paired counts and a McNemar p.
5) Once a timeframe has 200+ pairs, _count's expected hits use the control rate for the matching (interval, R-bin, last 30 days) instead of 1/(1+R).
6) Exclude controls from calls(), calibration, coach._desk_zones and changes. Add a 'Zones vs random lines' section to the DeskPanel Record tab.
ideas.risk: Roughly doubles the rows in desk_calls (still about 100 a day). By construction the control can't sit on detected structure, but it can sit on structure the detectors missed, which slightly understates the zones' edge (the conservative direction). Keep the analytic baseline until enough pairs exist.

ideas.title: Desk replay: a year of the desk's own history on day one
ideas.pitch: Instead of waiting months for 1d calls to resolve, the desk replays itself over the last year of candles, with the same detectors, buckets and scoring, and starts with hundreds of finished zones per setup and coin.
ideas.why: Learning is slow: a 1d zone takes up to 55 days to resolve, and each level needs about 10 finished zones before it speaks for itself. The only prior is backtest.py, which trades a different setup (fresh-only demand, a different target and hold, no fresh/HTF/trend buckets) and overlaps the live period. A replay of the exact desk pipeline gives bucket-level priors, a calibration curve and 'working now' history immediately. It also lets every learning change (windowed baseline, placebo, stop buffer) be tested on thousands of zones before it touches live calls.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/desk_replay.py:
1) For each desk coin and timeframe, load ~12 months of closed candles with get_range.
2) Walk bar by bar (every bar on 1d/4h, every 2nd on 1h). At each bar, slice the HTF frames to candles closed by that bar and run desk_calls.candidates. I measured ~18 ms per call: a 4h coin-year is ~40 s, a 1h one ~2-3 min, all 40 coins on all timeframes ~2 h of one core, once.
3) Apply the same REPEAT/overlap rule and new_call(..., shadow=True).
4) Score each record with score_call on SCORE_RES candles; score 1h replays on 15m to keep downloads down.
5) Mark rows features['origin'] = 'replay' and stop at the first live record for that coin/TF, so nothing is counted twice.
6) desk_learning.weight() multiplies replay rows by REPLAY_WEIGHT (0.5), and _backtest is skipped for coins that have replay rows.
7) Run it as a jobs.py job with progress in the Status tab and a 'Replay history' button in desk Settings; new coins replay incrementally.
ideas.risk: Heavy CPU and Binance load on the first run; throttle with the desk's CONCURRENCY and the candle cache. Survivorship bias: today's watchlist coins are the ones that did well enough to be watched, so show that caveat. The replay must use closed-only HTF frames (the fix above) or it will disagree with live.

ideas.title: Learned trims: score every sell and trim signal on the coins you hold
ideas.pitch: When INJ reaches resistance and Discord says trim, tell me how often that exact kind of trim was right on INJ 4h: 'price fell to 6.80 before closing above the zone in 62% of 29 cases (random odds 45%)'.
ideas.why: Trick trades spot only, so his most frequent decision on holdings is when to trim or sell, and that side has no learning at all. sell_check.py scores are hand-set constants (0.7 + 0.2 for D1..., 0.35 + 0.15...). holdings_watch arms lost_support and at_resistance on every holding, and nothing records what happened after they fire. The desk's machinery (records, level_reach, the edge hierarchy, calibration) can learn this without any paper shorts.
ideas.how:
1) New desk_sells.py. At the desk's candle closes, run sell_check's frame detection (at_resistance and lost_support) on every desk coin.
2) Save a DeskCall-shaped row with features['side'] = 'sell' and a bucket like '4h|at_resistance|wick|rsi_hot|d1'.
3) Score it with a mirrored level_reach: 'right' when price reaches the next support below (or 1R, R = distance to the zone top + 0.25 ATR) before a close above the zone, within HOLD_BARS; 'wrong' on a close above the zone first. reach_r is the deepest fall.
4) Learn with desk_learning.estimate: random odds or placebo baseline, same shrinkage.
5) sell_check.check and the SELL_SIGNALS alert text in signal_alerts.py read the learned p and n instead of the constants. holdings_watch alerts and the brief quote them.
6) Optional fast prior: signal_alerts.scan_history already finds where a sell signal fired on past candles. Score each of those hits over the next HOLD_BARS for an instant per-coin record.
ideas.risk: 'Right' must count a missed rally (a close above the zone first) as wrong, or the record flatters selling in a downtrend. Regime matters a lot on this side, so pair it with the regime features.

ideas.title: Desk odds on every long plan and scanner row
ideas.pitch: When I ask for a long setup on INJ, the card says 'Desk odds 41% to T1 before the stop (random 29%, 1.4x edge on H4 fresh demand with D1 behind, 63 zones)' and suggests the learned take-profit, not just a backtest line.
ideas.why: Everything the desk learns stays inside the desk tab. agent.py attaches only the backtest track record to plans (around line 794), and market_scanner ranks by R:R, agreement and track record. The learned edge, the coin's live record and the TP placement are exactly what someone deciding on a limit buy needs, and they already exist as pure functions (estimate and take_profit, used only by agent_desk).
ideas.how:
1) AgentDesk.odds_for(symbol, interval, plan, trends, track) builds the bucket with desk_calls.bucket_of: plan.zone_kind, plan.zone_fresh, plan.zone_htf, and agree_level over the analyze trend plus desk_calls.trend_of on the HTF frames agent.py already loads.
2) rr_level comes from plan.targets[0]. Call desk_learning.estimate, reusing the TrackRecord just fetched, then take_profit.
3) Return {p, random_odds, lift, levels, basis, tp_price, tp_fraction}. Only for long plans on support/demand on 1h/4h/1d.
4) Add TradePlan.desk_odds in schemas.py. Fill it in agent.py next to track_record, and in market_scanner for the top rows.
5) The frontend plan card shows one line, with the edge chain on hover. The narrator gets it in its facts.
ideas.risk: If trade_plan.build_plan changes for chat plans but the desk keeps the old logic, the odds would describe a different setup. Add a test that a desk candidate and a chat plan on the same zone get the same bucket and entry/stop.

ideas.title: Learn where the stop and the limit should sit, not only the take-profit
ideas.pitch: The desk already learned to take profit 85% of the way to resistance. Let it also learn 'on 4h demand, a 0.5 ATR buffer under the zone survives the wick that kills 0.25 ATR stops, worth +0.12R a call'.
ideas.why: Every call uses the fixed stop (zone low - 0.25 ATR, trade_plan.build_plan) and the fixed entry (top of the zone). The most common post-mortem loss lessons ('stop too tight', 'no reaction', 'early entry') are about exactly these two choices, and nothing measures them. The data is already in the candles score_call replays.
ideas.how:
1) desk_calls.level_reach also records, from the fill to the end of the hold window (not stopping at the stop):
- dip_atr: (zone_low - lowest low before the level was reached) / ATR
- level_ever: whether the level was reached at all in the window
- deepest_in_zone: how far into the zone price went before the level
Store the ATR in features at call time. A new path_final flag keeps score() running until the window ends.
2) desk_learning.stop_buffer() mirrors take_profit. For buffers 0.1/0.25/0.5/0.75 ATR: a zone survives when dip_atr < b; hit_b = level_ever and survived; rr_b = level distance / risk with b; ER_b after fees. Pick the best once there are MIN_TP_SAMPLES rows and it gains at least TP_MIN_GAIN.
3) entry_depth() does the same trade-off between fill rate (deepest_in_zone >= d) and the better R.
4) new_call applies both and says so in confidence_basis. DeskPanel shows the tables.
ideas.risk: Stop, entry and TP learned on the same rows interact. Learn them all on the full-level outcome (as take_profit does) and apply the stop first. Wider stops need the risk-based sizing fix, or the paper wallet will over-risk.

ideas.title: Kimi x Desk: measure whether Kimi confluence makes zones better
ideas.pitch: My own indicator should get a report card from the desk: 'H4 demand with a Kimi support inside: 1.6x edge (58 zones). Without: 1.1x. With a recent B+ the agent would take: 1.9x (17).'
ideas.why: The desk and Kimi never meet. AgentDesk isn't given the KimiService (main.py line 153), and Candidate.features has no Kimi fields, though Kimi is Trick's own tool and Kimi + Agent already predicts which signals pay. If Kimi confluence adds edge, the desk should use it; if it doesn't, Trick learns that too.
ideas.how:
1) Pass app.state.kimi to AgentDesk.
2) In _coin, on 4h and 1d first (a Kimi run is ~1 s on 3,000 bars, cached per candle by KimiService), add to features:
- kimi_level_in_zone: an active Kimi support overlapping the desk zone and already confirmed by this bar
- kimi_long_recent: a B+/U/B+? confirmed within 10 bars, plus its agent verdict
- kimi_fc_up: the Kimi + Agent forecast ends above the close
3) desk_learning.split_table(history, flag) gives, per timeframe/kind, the lift with and without each flag, with n and a range. Show it in the Record tab and quote it in call_text ('Kimi support 7.15 inside the zone').
4) Feed the flags into the feature model (next idea). Once a flag's split is significant, it can become a bucket dimension.
ideas.risk: CPU on 1h: 40 Kimi runs an hour, queued behind KimiService's one-at-a-time lock with the charts, so start with 4h/1d. A Kimi level must only count from its confirmation bar (the post-mortem issue above).

ideas.title: A walk-forward model on top of the buckets, with market regime
ideas.pitch: Same zone, same bucket, but RSI 24, price 3 ATR away and BTC in a daily downtrend. Let the desk learn how much those shift the odds, and use it only once it has beaten the plain buckets on calls it wasn't fitted on.
ideas.why: Every call stores distance_atr, rsi, zone_score, atr_pct, risk_pct, agree_ratio and bias (desk_calls.candidates), and none of them is learned from; the only inputs are three bucket bits. Market regime (BTC or total-market trend) is the biggest driver of whether any long works, and the desk doesn't capture it anywhere. Kimi + Agent already shows the pattern that works here: learn a correction, switch it on only when walk-forward proves it.
ideas.how:
1) desk_learning.feature_fix(history, now): sort rows by closed_at. Target = level_hit - p_level, where p_level is the hierarchy's level confidence at call time; store it as raw_p_level on DeskCall, since confidence holds the TP-adjusted value.
2) Reuse kimi_agent.Ridge (decay ~0.995) on the features scaled to [-1, 1], plus two new ones captured in _coin: btc_trend (desk_calls.trend_of on BTCUSDT 1d, one fetch per run) and coin_rank (30-day return rank among the desk's coins).
3) Walk-forward: predict each row only from rows closed before its created_at. Switch on when, over 150+ judged rows, its Brier score beats p_level with a paired t >= 2.
4) Then p = clip(p_level + prediction, MIN_P, MAX_P), and confidence_basis gets 'model +4 pts: RSI 24, BTC down'. The Record tab shows its walk-forward score and weights, like the Kimi tables.
ideas.risk: Overfitting and leakage: order strictly by created_at and keep the gate. The BTC fetch adds one request per run.

ideas.title: Close the calibration loop: correct the confidence when it is consistently off
ideas.pitch: If calls the desk says are 45% only work 35% of the time, the next call should say 35% and be sized for it, instead of only showing me a chart about the gap.
ideas.why: calibration() and verdict() only report. Nothing in estimate, take_profit or size_for reacts to a measured gap, so a known overconfidence keeps oversizing paper positions and inflating the expected R in Discord messages.
ideas.how:
1) desk_learning.recalibrate(rows): walk-forward Platt scaling, logit(p_true) = a + b*logit(p_stated), fitted with a few Newton steps on rows closed before each judged row.
2) Switch it on when, on 100+ rows, its Brier beats the raw p with a paired t >= 2 (the same kind of switch as Kimi + Agent).
3) agent_desk._coin applies it after take_profit and stores raw_confidence and confidence on the DeskCall.
4) The Record tab shows the raw and corrected curves, and the verdict says which one is in use.
ideas.risk: Fitting on calls + watched zones can still miss a bias specific to the calls actually made. Fit on both and require them to agree, or fit on calls alone once there are 100.

ideas.title: Honest numbers everywhere: ranges, base rates and 'too early'
ideas.pitch: '14 trades, 57% win' should read '14 trades, 57% win (35-77%), random odds for those targets 31%', so I know whether it means anything.
ideas.why: Every learning surface quotes point estimates: track_record's win rate has no baseline and no range; the desk's Edge column has no range; working_now calls a setup working on 5 zones; calibration bins show no counts; verdict's 'skill > 0.002' has no test. Small samples look as solid as large ones, and the LLM narrator repeats them.
ideas.how:
- track_record.record_from_result: add expected_wins (sum of 1/(1+R) per backtest trade, from its entry, stop and target) and a Wilson 80% range to TrackRecord and its summary line.
- desk_learning.bucket_table and estimate: an 80% range for the lift from a Gamma(hits + K*parent, exp + K) posterior, shown as '1.4x (0.9-2.0)'.
- working_now: Poisson tail probability against expected hits; 'working' only when p < 0.1 and n >= 12.
- Calibration bins: show n and Wilson bars.
- verdict: paired bootstrap of the per-call Brier differences; say 'better than a flat guess' only when 90% of resamples agree.
- Frontend: DeskPanel, the plan card, the Backtest tab.
ideas.risk: More numbers on small screens: show the range on hover where space is tight.

ideas.title: 'What the desk learned this week' on Discord
ideas.pitch: Sunday evening: 'H4 fresh demand with D1 behind went from 1.2x to 1.5x (+11 zones) and is now callable; 1h tested support dropped to 0.8x and stopped calling; 4h take-profits moved to 85%; confidence ran 6 points high and is now corrected; best call ARB 4h +2.1R, worst INJ 1h -1.0R (no reaction from the zone).'
ideas.why: The learning happens silently; Trick only sees individual calls on Discord. A weekly diff of what the desk has learned is how he'd notice it getting smarter, or drifting, and decide whether to trust it. It is also a well-grounded writing job for the local LLM.
ideas.how:
1) Once a day, store a snapshot in desk_kv['learn_snapshots']: {bucket: lift, n}, the TP fraction per interval/kind, the calibration gap and the Brier score.
2) desk_digest.py diffs the last 7 days: setups that became callable or stopped being callable (lift - 1 - typical fee_r crosses MIN_EXPECTED_R), the biggest lift moves with their n, TP and stop changes, the calibration change, and the best and worst call with post-mortem-style facts from desk_calls.
3) Schedule it with the ReviewSettings / weekly_due_slot pattern from postmortem.py, or add a desk section to the existing weekly review.
4) Send the template text. An optional LLM rewrite is accepted only when postmortem.grounded() passes.
ideas.risk: Week-to-week moves on small n are noise. Show n, and only list moves whose 80% ranges don't overlap (previous idea).

ideas.title: Pool Kimi + Agent across coins so the correction can prove itself
ideas.pitch: Kimi + Agent says 'learning 12/30' on most of my charts. Train it on every watchlist coin's Kimi forecasts at that timeframe and judge it per chart, so INJ 4h gets a correction learned from 40 coins.
ideas.why: forecast_fix fits one chart's history only. It needs MIN_TRAIN (20) thinned forecasts before it corrects anything and MIN_EVALS (30) more to be judged: about 50 x H candles. So many charts never switch on, and the ones that do are partly the lucky ones (the switch issue above). The features are already scale-free (ATR units, RSI, range position), so forecasts from different coins on one timeframe are comparable.
ideas.how:
1) Keep the latest result per (symbol, interval) in KimiService.
2) Per interval, fit one decayed Ridge on every desk coin's finished, thinned forecast records (features at their bar, error in volatility units, timestamp), added in time order across coins.
3) forecast_fix gains a prior fit. Walk-forward per chart uses the pooled fit trained on records (from all coins) finished before each forecast's bar, plus the chart's own residual fit. The same paired-t switch, with hysteresis, decides per chart.
4) Do the same for signal_filter: signals across coins, one-hot by type.
ideas.risk: Records from different coins happen at the same moments and are correlated, so the effective sample is smaller than it looks: judge per chart and keep the switch strict. It also needs Kimi runs on desk coins nobody is viewing, which costs CPU.

readers.subsystem: kimi (Kimi Cooked port, service, drawing, tables, Kimi signal alerts, Kimi + Agent)
readers.map:
Engine: backend/app/kimi/kimi_v574.py is Trick's bar-by-bar port of v5.7.4, run on closed candles. patterns_v574.py adds 12 chart patterns and 10 harmonics (lifecycle, the Pat BO and Harmonics signals, the w2/w3 factors, TP magnets). sessions_v574.py adds the session filter (off by default), and w8 (HTF divergence) is computed inside the loop. Inputs are fixed to Inputs.users_chart() through kimi_service.kimi_inputs(); no UI or env setting changes them. A run takes about 1.5 s per 5,000 candles (I timed it on 4h and 1h).
Service: KimiService.get() in kimi_service.py loads KIMI_BARS chart candles plus 1,000 daily candles for intraday charts and drops the forming candle. It runs compute() in a thread behind one asyncio.Semaphore(1) and caches 64 (symbol, interval) entries until the next close + 3 s. compute() turns the engine Result into a KimiResponse: S/R levels with reach odds, the Fib ladder and pocket, up to 15+15 labels, the forecast (path, band, texture, next candle), patterns, break-outs, harmonics, and the PATH VERIFY and Signal Stats rows. summarize() turns it into facts for the agent, LLM and brief.
Kimi + Agent (kimi_agent.py): a walk-forward ridge correction of the forecast's end point, plus a take/skip filter on signals. Their rows go into `agent`; forecast.agent holds the corrected path. On the frontend, kimiAgent.withAgent swaps in that line unless "Kimi's own line" is ticked.
Frontend: AgenticChart fetches /api/indicators/kimi when Kimi is on (K key, or "show my Kimi") and fetches again 6 s after a new candle arrives. KimiPrimitive draws zones and rays with odds, the Fib ladder, the band, the best-guess and textured paths, the next-candle triangle, the end label, patterns, harmonics and PRZ boxes. B+/B-/U/Dn/B+?/B-? are series markers, greyed with ✕ when the filter skips them. The Layers tab toggles 6 parts. The KimiPanel pill holds both tables, the Kimi + Agent rows, the latest 6 signals and the patterns.
Consumers: signal_alerts (kimi_buy = B+, kimi_sell = B-, kimi_any; checked on close with retries; Preview reads the capped label list), backtest (kimi_long/short/any replay the engine's own outcomes), brief, changes, postmortem, and the agent's read_kimi tool and ta_agent._kimi_lines narrator. Kimi is not used by the agent desk, the watchlist and market scanners, holdings_watch, sell_check, trade plans, paper trading or bar replay.

issues.title: Bar replay draws today's Kimi and stacks future labels on the replay candle
issues.detail: During replay ChartWorkspace.tsx (~l.1240) still passes `indicators` and `kimiParts` unchanged. Only the AI overlays are swapped for replayLevels. The Kimi effect in AgenticChart (~l.1180-1211) never reads props.replayTime, so KimiPrimitive keeps drawing the latest run: S/R zones born after the replay point, today's Fib, patterns and harmonics, and the forecast (start_time = last_closed, mapped into the future area). The markers effect does not re-run either. When the replay effect (~l.873) calls candleRef.setData(subset), lightweight-charts 4.2.3 _recalculateMarkers maps each marker with timeToIndex(time, true) and NearestLeft, so every B+/B-/U/Dn after the replay point snaps onto the replay's last candle. Result: lookahead while practising. Fix: when replayTime != null, detach the Kimi primitive and set markersRef.current.kimi = [] (and filter s.time <= replayTime), then offer 'Kimi as of then' (see the ideas).

issues.title: 'Direction Kimi / +Agent' counts flat forecasts as wrong (my test run read 13% vs 54%)
issues.detail: forecast_fix appends `np.sign(kimi_end) == np.sign(real_end)` for every judged forecast. While Kimi's learned gains are off its line is exactly flat (sign 0), so those count as misses. On synthetic INJ 4h, 3,659 of 4,975 finished forecasts were exactly flat. KimiPanel then showed 'Direction Kimi / +Agent 13% / 54%', which tells the indicator's author his line gets direction right 13% of the time, and makes the agent look far better than it is. Fix: score direction only where |kimi_end| > the node tolerance. Report Kimi's call share separately ('called 27%, right 52%'). Compare +Agent on the same subset and, separately, on the flat ones. Update the row label and the reason text in kimi_service._agent to match.

issues.title: Signal filter verdicts are keyed by candle, so same-candle signals share one take/skip
issues.detail: signal_filter stores `out.verdicts[s.bar]`, and kimi_service._signals reads `verdicts[s.bar]`. Two signals that confirm on the same candle overwrite each other: a B+? and a B-? (seen at bar 848 in a 4h test run), or a DIV and a Pat BO. A long can then show the short's verdict and predicted R, and its marker gets greyed with ✕ (AgenticChart ~l.1198) for the wrong reason. Fix: key verdicts by (bar, typ, dir) in both places (and in tests/test_kimi_agent.py).

issues.title: 'Watching' patterns already through their break-out line are shown as still pending
issues.detail: ChartPatterns.lifecycle (patterns_v574.py ~l.475) only breaks out on a *cross* with a volume spike, and not while paused or ranging. A quiet cross never fires again, so the pattern stays 'watching' until it goes stale. That matches the script. But _patterns reports breakout_level = brk_a*last + brk_b, so KimiPanel prints 'breaks 6.51' and ta_agent._kimi_pattern_lines says 'breaks out on a close above 6.51' while price is 7.73. Past a wedge's apex the invalidation line is even on the wrong side (bullish FW: break-out 6.51, invalid 6.76). On synthetic data 10 of 12 watching patterns were like this. Fix (presentation only, engine untouched): add `through: bool` and `past_apex: bool` to KimiPattern. Phrase it as 'crossed without the volume spike Kimi needs: no Pat BO', and drop the level lines when they are inverted, in KimiPanel, _kimi_pattern_lines and summarize.

issues.title: One engine run at a time, shared with all background work; the cache evicts the oldest-inserted chart
issues.detail: compute runs in asyncio.to_thread behind `_cpu = Semaphore(1)`. It is pure Python and GIL-bound. The chart, signal_alerts._kimi_signals, the brief, changes, postmortem and backtest (which borrows kimi._cpu) all share that slot. With Kimi alerts on a 30-coin watchlist on 1h, each hour close queues about 45 s of runs. The chart you are watching sits in the same FIFO ('· updating'), and Discord alerts arrive up to a minute late. At 00:00 UTC the 1h, 4h and 1d closes stack. Separately, the cache trims with `self._cache.pop(next(iter(self._cache)))`. Re-assigning a key keeps its original position, so once there are more than 64 keys the first chart you opened is evicted first. Fix: a ProcessPoolExecutor (2-3 workers; numpy arrays in, a pydantic model out, both pickle) with a priority lane for /api/indicators/kimi, and LRU via move_to_end.

issues.title: Kimi's past labels and confluence shift as the 5,000-candle window slides
issues.detail: Bar 0 moves forward one candle at every close, and the engine depends on its whole path (adaptive weights, conf_hist tiers, S/R evict-weakest state). I ran windows 200 candles apart on synthetic data. Of the signals both windows share, 25-32% changed confluence and 7-10% changed tier, and on ETH 1h 4 labels disappeared and 3 new ones appeared. The newest labels were stable. So the 'confluence 62' quoted in a fired alert (signal_alerts._kimi_hit) can read differently on the chart later, and the Signal Stats table is rebuilt from scratch on every run. TradingView behaves the same way, but nothing in the app keeps a frozen record. Fix: freeze each signal when it first appears (Kimi forward ledger idea) and add a note to NOTES.

issues.title: A failed Kimi fetch is not retried until the next candle closes
issues.detail: The fetch effect (~l.1156) catches the error, sets `error` and waits for kimiTick, which only moves when a new candle arrives (~l.706). After a backend restart or a Binance hiccup, a 1d chart shows 'Kimi Cooked unavailable' for up to a day, and a 4h chart for up to 4 h. Fix: while kimiOn && error, retry with backoff (5 s, 20 s, 60 s, then every 5 min). Abort the retries on symbol or interval change.

issues.title: Kimi pill times are UTC; the chart axis uses your timezone
issues.detail: Latest signals and Patterns use `new Date(t*1000).toISOString().slice(5,16)`, which is UTC. The axis follows the layout timezone, which defaults to 'local' (SettingsDialog). For a CEST user a B+ shows as '10-08 12:00' in the pill and 14:00 on the chart. Fix: pass layout.timezone into KimiPanel and format with Intl.DateTimeFormat (or append 'UTC').

issues.title: The narrator and LLM facts mention harmonics that died 500-1,000 candles ago
issues.detail: summarize() passes every set in HM.sets, and ta_agent._kimi_pattern_lines narrates `k['harmonics'][-1]` whatever its state or age. My runs produced 'Harmonic: bearish AB=CD (failed), D 8.1608 516 bars ago ...' and 'Three Drives (failed) ... 1050 bars ago' in answers to 'what does Kimi say?'. Fix: in summarize, keep active and compromised harmonics, plus tp1/failed ones whose end_time is within about 2×horizon. Apply the same recency cut to chart_patterns.

issues.title: Filter row reads '+0.00R (0/172)' when it would take nothing
issues.detail: _agent formats `(sf.take_r or 0)`. With took == 0, take_r is None, and the row shows a taken R of +0.00 next to 0 trades. Show 'none taken' instead. Also show skip_r, which signal_filter already computes.

issues.title: The 'Any Kimi label' preview draws every hit as a buy arrow
issues.detail: runPreview picks `long` from a list that contains kimi_sell but not kimi_any. Every kimi_any hit, B- and Dn included, becomes arrowUp below the bar, labelled 'Any Kimi label'. Fix: return direction and label per hit from SignalAlertService.preview (KimiSignal has both) and use them. Kimi previews could also list each past label's outcome and R, since k.signals already carry them.

issues.title: The docs contradict themselves and point to a missing TradingView-parity harness
issues.detail: README l.587 says 'Only the higher-timeframe divergence factor is not ported', while l.589 says w8 is ported. backend/app/kimi/PORT_README.md lists data.py, run_example.py, sample_BTCUSDT_1h.csv and validation/compare_with_tradingview.py; none are in the repo. Its parity table predates the patterns/harmonics/w8/sessions ports, so the Pat BO and Harmonics rows have never been checked against TradingView. test_kimi.py only locks the port's own numbers. Fix the README line, and see the parity-checker idea.

ideas.title: Kimi forward ledger: a frozen, live-scored record of every signal
ideas.pitch: Every B+, U, B+?, Pat BO and harmonic is logged the moment it fires, never changes afterwards, and is scored forward with real fees. I finally see how my indicator does live, not re-derived on a sliding 5,000-candle window.
ideas.why: The Signal Stats table is in-sample and rebuilt every run. Measured: about 30% of shared signals changed confluence when the window slid 200 candles. A frozen forward record is something TradingView can't give the author. It also gives Kimi + Agent's take/skip calls a clean out-of-sample scorecard, and spot framing for B-/Dn ('trim calls').
ideas.how: New backend/app/kimi_ledger.py that owns a `kimi_ledger` table via db.migrate. Columns: id, symbol, interval, label, type, dir, confirm_time, entry, tp_price, sl_price, expiry_time, conf, tier, factors mask, agent, agent_r, status, result, r, mfe, mae, resolved_at. Prices come from engine Signal.tp/sl (ATR distances), so kimi_service must expose them. Hook it into agent_desk's close loop (same 1h/4h/1d +45 s schedule and watchlist): after the desk run, call KimiService.get per coin/TF and insert labels with confirm_time == the closed bar. Score every 2 min on finer candles with journal.evaluate_entry, like desk_calls.score_call with SCORE_RES (0.1% fees per side, stop checked first). Longs score as paper trades on Kimi's own bracket. B-/Dn score as trims: did price fall 1 ATR before it rose 1 ATR, and the drawdown avoided. Endpoints: GET /api/kimi/ledger?symbol=&interval=&type= and /api/kimi/ledger/summary (per type, tier, take vs skip: n, hit %, avg R, against the in-sample row). UI: a 'Live record' block in KimiPanel and a section in the Desk Record tab. The brief and weekly review get one line.
ideas.risk: Needs weeks of closes before samples mean anything (show n and 'too early' under 20, like the desk). Also adds engine runs at each close, so do it after the process-pool fix.

ideas.title: Signal inspector: hover or click a Kimi label to see why it fired and act on it
ideas.pitch: Hover a B+ and I see its confluence broken down by factor (near S/R ✓, HTF anchor ✓, volume ✗...), its tier, Kimi's own target and stop drawn on the chart, how it ended, and whether the agent would take it. One click paper-buys it or logs it to my journal.
ideas.why: The engine already records which of the 10 confluence factors were present (Signal.mask) and the current adaptive weights (final['factor_weights']), but the app throws that away. The chart shows a bare 'B+'. JournalEntry.source already allows 'kimi' (journal.py, lib/journal.ts), but nothing ever creates such an entry.
ideas.how: Backend: extend KimiSignal (schemas.py) and kimi_service._signals with id = f'{typ}:{dir}:{bar}', factors (names from the fac order in kimi_v574 ~l.919: near S/R, retest, pattern, harmonic, HTF anchor, RSI extreme, drift, volume, HTF divergence, multi-osc, each with present and weight), tp_price = entry ± tp, sl_price = entry ∓ sl, expiry_time, resolved_time (res_bar), p_random (the random-entry baseline at resolution). Frontend: give the Kimi markers `id` (LWC 4.2.3 supports SeriesMarker.id and MouseEventParams.hoveredObjectId). In AgenticChart's onMove, set a kimiTip state rendered like eventTip (~l.1618). Clicking pins it, and KimiPrimitive draws the bracket box (entry→TP green, entry→SL red, confirm→resolution). Buttons for long labels: Paper buy (build a TradePlan and reuse lib/paper.ts planToPaperOrders), Log trade (POST /api/journal with source 'kimi'), Alert at entry/stop (existing alerts API).
ideas.risk: Confluence of older labels shifts between runs (see issues). Mark values as 'as of this run' unless the label is in the ledger.

ideas.title: Kimi alerts that are worth a Discord ping
ideas.pitch: When Kimi fires on a coin I watch, Discord gets a green or red card: label, type, tier, Kimi's stop and target prices, this signal type's edge on this chart, the agent's take/skip, the forecast and the nearest S/R odds. I can also ask for 'only top tier' or 'only what the agent would take', plus pattern break-outs, harmonics, and sell labels on coins I hold.
ideas.why: Today _kimi_hit sends 'Kimi printed B+ (long) at X - confluence 62'. Pat BO and harmonics aren't alertable (KIMI_SIGNALS has only kimi_buy/sell/any). holdings_watch arms only lost_support and at_resistance. alerts.Channel sends plain `{'content': text}`. For a spot trader, B- on a held coin means trim, which the app never says.
ideas.how: signal_alerts.py: add SignalIds kimi_pattern_bo and kimi_harmonic. KimiResponse.signals currently drops typ ≥ 3, so either expose them in a separate list or derive them from breakouts/harmonics. Add optional fields min_tier ('top') and agent_take_only to SignalAlert and CreateSignalAlertsRequest; _kimi_hit filters on them. Build the text from KimiSignal (tp/sl from the inspector idea), the matching stats row (stats_rows: 'DIV 45% (14/31) +14pt z 1.7'), forecast.headline and the nearest held level with odds. Spot framing: if the coin is in binance_import positions, say 'B- on a coin you hold: consider trimming'. alerts.py: let a Channel take an optional embed builder (Discord `embeds` with colour and fields; Telegram keeps text). holdings_watch.py: an option to add kimi_sell to SIGNALS.
ideas.risk: Richer messages need the KimiResponse at fire time, which the fire path already has. Keep messages within Discord's 2,000-character and 25-field limits.

ideas.title: Kimi radar: watchlist badges and a timeframe strip for the current coin
ideas.pitch: My watchlist shows what Kimi sees on each coin ('B+ 2 bars ago, take', 'in golden pocket', 'in bullish PRZ', 'wedge 0.4 ATR from break-out'), sortable. The Kimi pill shows 15m/1h/4h/1d side by side (▲ +0.8%, ►, ▲, ▼), so I see at a glance whether Kimi agrees across timeframes.
ideas.why: Kimi lives on one chart at a time. scanner.py, market_scanner.py and Watchlist.tsx never touch it. With INJ and several holdings, opening each coin to check Kimi is the friction this removes, and runs are cheap (about 1.5 s per coin, cached per close).
ideas.how: New backend/app/kimi_radar.py with pure functions over a KimiResponse. A flags() helper returns the newest long or short label within k bars (with agent verdict and tier), price inside fib pocket_low..high, price inside an active bullish harmonic PRZ, a watching pattern within 1 ATR of break-out (using the `through` fix), forecast pct_change and next_candle, and the nearest S/R with odds. Endpoints: GET /api/kimi/radar?symbols=&interval= (one KimiService.get per coin, using the same semaphore) and GET /api/kimi/mtf?symbol=. Warm watchlist coins right after the desk's close run. Frontend: lib/api.ts fetchKimiRadar; a Kimi badge column and a 'Kimi' sort in Watchlist.tsx; a one-line MTF strip at the top of KimiPanel. Agent: a radar entry in agent.make_toolbox so 'what does Kimi say across my watchlist?' works.
ideas.risk: CPU at closes when the watchlist is long. Cap the coin count and depend on the process-pool fix.

ideas.title: Kimi odds at any price: crosshair, plan targets, alerts, price questions
ideas.pitch: Hover any price and Kimi tells me the chance it trades there within the forecast window. Every plan target and alert price gets the same number.
ideas.why: Kimi's odds come from its own empirical reach curve, rch: 40 buckets of 0.25σ√H learned on this coin, up and down. Result.level_odds is about 12 lines. Today the odds appear only at Kimi's own levels and Fib ratios, but the same math answers 'can T1 at 27 be hit in 20 candles?'.
ideas.how: Add to KimiResponse a `reach` block {close, sig, horizon, lean (path end - born), n: rch[40], up: rch[0:20], down: rch[20:40]}, taken from res.final and last_forecast() in compute(). Frontend lib/kimiOdds.ts ports level_odds, including the n < 50 logistic fallback. Uses: a crosshair price readout in AgenticChart onMove ('Kimi 34% / 20 bars'); a 'Kimi odds to T1/T2' line on the AgentPanel plan cards next to track_record; the alert edit dialog; and a backend helper kimi_service.odds(k, price) so ta_agent.price_check answers include it and the desk can use it. When Kimi + Agent is active, choose explicitly which lean to use (Kimi's or the agent's).
ideas.risk: The odds are one-sided (reach), not target-before-stop. Label them clearly so nobody reads them as a win rate.

ideas.title: Kimi in bar replay: Kimi as it stood at the replay candle
ideas.pitch: In replay I see Kimi exactly as it stood then: labels up to that candle (outcomes hidden until they resolve), the S/R and the forecast it was drawing, then I step forward and watch it play out. That is TradingView bar replay for my own indicator.
ideas.why: Today replay leaks Kimi's present (see issues). Replay already has '/api/replay/levels' for the agent's zones but nothing for Kimi. The engine already records every bar's forecast (res.forecasts: y/up/lo per bar), so the forecast can step bar by bar without re-running.
ideas.how: Backend main.py: GET /api/replay/kimi?symbol&interval&time. Using market.get_range (as replay_levels does), run kimi_service.compute on bars_for(interval) closed candles ending at `time`, and return KimiResponse plus `forecasts_after`: the per-bar forecast records for the next ~300 candles from a full run, so stepping redraws the forecast without a rerun. In signals, mask result/r when resolved_time > the replay time. Frontend: ChartWorkspace gets a 'Kimi as of then' button beside the replay-levels one (auto-load on pause). AgenticChart takes a `kimiOverride` prop used while replaying and filters markers to s.time <= replayTime.
ideas.risk: About 1.5 s per reload, so load on pause or every N steps, not every step. Levels' odds and states are exact only at the reload point.

ideas.title: Kimi Lab: edit Kimi's inputs, run parameter sweeps, pool stats across the watchlist
ideas.pitch: Change Kimi's inputs in the app the way I do on TradingView, then sweep one input (Node Tolerance, Coverage, confMinAlert, statCostPct, pivotLen) across my watchlist. I see which value really improves Skill vs RW, Cover and the DIV/Early edges, with pooled z-scores instead of one chart's 14/31.
ideas.why: The inputs are hard-coded to Inputs.users_chart(): no env setting, no UI. statCostPct is 0.15% while Binance spot is 0.1%. One chart's Signal Stats rows are tiny samples, and pooling 20-40 coins is what makes an edge readable. Having written the indicator, Trick tunes it, and this turns tuning into evidence.
ideas.how: Backend: kimi_service.compute(..., inputs=None) with KimiService keyed by (symbol, interval, inputs hash). Persist the user's inputs in `.cache/kimi_inputs.json` via read_store/write_store. GET/PUT /api/kimi/inputs groups Inputs fields like the TradingView panel. New kimi_lab.py: sweep(symbols, interval, param, values) as a jobs.py-tracked background task. Per run, keep raw (wins, n, expected e, variance v) per stats row; stats_table's cell() already computes them, so add a stats_raw() next to it and a pooled z. Split by signal bar at 70/30 to flag in-sample-only gains. POST /api/kimi/lab/sweep and GET /api/kimi/lab/{id}. Frontend: KimiLabDialog.tsx (inputs form with a 'My TradingView chart' reset, sweep form, results table), opened from the Kimi pill.
ideas.risk: Overfitting by sweeping. Show the 70/30 split and never auto-apply a winner. Changing inputs makes plain Kimi stop matching TradingView, so show it in the pill.

ideas.title: Confluence factor scoreboard in the Kimi tables
ideas.pitch: A third table shows which of my 10 confluence factors actually pulled their weight on this coin: current adaptive weight, win% when present against absent, and edge against the random baseline.
ideas.why: The adaptive weights move with f_wins/f_loss inside the engine, but the author never sees why. Each resolved Signal carries mask, result and p_random, so this needs no engine change and runs in milliseconds.
ideas.how: kimi_service: factor_rows(res). For each factor k (names in the fac order at kimi_v574 ~l.919), take the resolved non-random signals with (mask >> k) & 1. Compute W/N, sum(p_random) as expected wins, edge points and z (the same formula as stats_table.cell), the same for signals without it, and the weight from res.final['factor_weights'][k]. Add `factors: list[KimiRow]` to KimiResponse and types.ts, and render it in KimiPanel under Signal Stats with the existing tones. summarize() gets the top two and bottom two so the agent can say 'on INJ 4h the HTF anchor carries the edge, volume doesn't'.
ideas.risk: Small per-chart samples. Show N and tone only where |z| >= 1, as stats_rows does.

ideas.title: Forecast ghosts: past forecasts against what happened, on the chart
ideas.pitch: Behind today's line I see Kimi's last few forecasts as faint ghosts, each ending in a dot showing where price really was at its horizon: inside the band or not, right direction or not.
ideas.why: PATH VERIFY (Traj Acc, Cover, Skill) is a wall of numbers. The engine already keeps every forecast's path, band and outcome (res.forecasts[i]['out']: close_at_H, inside, traj_hits), so the track record can be shown where it happened.
ideas.how: kimi_service: past_forecasts(res, times, every=H, n=8) picks the last 8 finished, thinned records (as kimi_agent does) → {start_time, step, path (y), band_end_low/high, actual_close, inside}. Add `history: list[KimiPastForecast]` to KimiResponse. KimiPrimitive.drawBack draws them at 0.25 alpha with an end dot (green if inside the band, red if not). Add a Layers entry 'kimiHistory' in lib/layers.ts, off by default.
ideas.risk: Visual clutter on low timeframes. Keep it off by default and capped at 8.

ideas.title: Agent desk × Kimi: does my indicator improve the desk's zone buys?
ideas.pitch: Every desk call notes whether Kimi agreed at the time: a recent B+/U the agent would take, good Kimi odds to the take-profit, the forecast pointing up. The Record tab then shows whether calls with Kimi on side did better.
ideas.why: The desk (agent_desk.py, desk_calls.py, desk_learning.py) never consults Kimi. DeskCall.features already stores context per call, so the evidence would build up for free and answer a question the author cares about.
ideas.how: In agent_desk at call time (and for watched zones), call KimiService.get(symbol, tf) and store features['kimi'] = {long_label_bars_ago, agent, tier, odds_tp (via the reach block from the odds idea), forecast_pct, tp_near_kimi_resistance}. Add a desk_learning.kimi_split(calls): hit %, avg R, n and Welch's t for agree against not. Show it in DeskPanel's Record and one line in the brief's desk section. Only once both sides have 30+ finished calls and t >= 1.65 would it become a confidence multiplier in estimate().
ideas.risk: Adds a Kimi run per desk coin per close (they are cached, and signal alerts often warm the same keys). Keep it out of the confidence math until proven.

ideas.title: TradingView parity checker for the newly ported modules
ideas.pitch: I type the numbers from my TradingView tables for a chart (or paste its CSV export) and the app runs the port on the same candles and shows row by row where it differs, including Pat BO and Harmonics.
ideas.why: The parity table in PORT_README predates the pattern, harmonic, w8 and session ports, and its validation script isn't in the repo. Nothing confirms that 'plain Kimi still matches TradingView' after those additions, which is the promise Kimi + Agent is built on.
ideas.how: POST /api/kimi/parity {symbol, interval, bars, last_time, tv: {'DIV +/-': '5/24', 'Pat BO': '3/7', 'Evaluated': 5981, 'Cover': 73.69, ...}} runs KimiCooked on the `bars` closed candles ending at last_time (the port's last_n rule) and returns per-row port vs TradingView with '='. An optional CSV upload parsed like the old load_csv. A 'Save as fixture' button writes the candles plus TradingView numbers to backend/tests/data/parity_*.json, and a parametrized test in tests/test_kimi.py asserts them, so parity can't silently drift. UI: a 'Parity' tab in the Kimi Lab dialog, or a small dialog from the pill.
ideas.risk: TradingView's and Binance's feeds can differ by a candle (the LINK 1h case in PORT_README). Show candle-level diffs to tell feed differences from port bugs.

ideas.title: 'Since you last looked' covers all of Kimi
ideas.pitch: Back on INJ after a few hours, the card also tells me a Kimi wedge broke out (target X), a harmonic hit TP1, a Kimi support broke, or the forecast flipped from up to down.
ideas.why: changes.py reports only DIV/U/Dn/Early labels (k.signals with confirm_time >= since). Break-outs, harmonic states and level breaks are already in the KimiResponse but left out.
ideas.how: In changes.changes(): add breakouts with time >= since; harmonics whose end_time >= since or whose time >= since (state tp1/failed/active); levels whose time_end >= since (Kimi S broke at X); and the forecast's direction compared with the previous fetch (store the last headline per (symbol, interval) in a small dict in KimiService). Lines go into out['lines'] and render unchanged in SinceLastLooked.tsx.
ideas.risk: Low. Keep at most 4 Kimi lines so the card stays short.

readers.map:
market_data.py (MarketData) serves all candles. It fetches Binance REST klines (paged 1000 at a time; 3h is resampled from 1h) behind a 5 s TTL cache keyed (symbol, interval, limit). It switches to the binance.vision hosts on a 451/403. In DATA_SOURCE=auto, any non-400 error calls mark_binance_down(): for the next 60 s every caller gets deterministic synthetic candles.
candle_store.py is the SQLite cache. The `candles` table keeps the newest 5000 closed bars per series and backs get_klines. The `range_candles` table keeps up to 570k bars and backs get_range, which the journal, paper, grid bots, coach and desk scoring use.
stream_hub.py runs one upstream Binance kline WebSocket per (symbol, interval). It is shared by /ws/klines browsers, AlertService (1m per alerted coin) and SignalAlertService (per symbol and timeframe). 3h is aggregated from 1h. When Binance is unusable it switches to a synthetic tick generator. It also keeps the last price per symbol for the demo heatmap.
derivatives.py feeds the header: open interest summed over the top 40 perps, and the !forceOrder@arr liquidation stream (rolling 24h totals plus the last 200 per symbol, saved as JSON). Its symbol_snapshot (funding and OI) goes to the agent and the brief.
futures_data.py covers one coin for the Market data tab and the agent's futures_context: funding, OI history, long/short ratios, spot CVD (raw klines field 9, not cached), order-book walls (REST depth 1000) and estimated liquidation clusters. Every result is tagged binance, synthetic or unavailable.
orderbook_heatmap.py polls spot depth every 10 s for each viewed symbol (8 at most), bins it and keeps 4 h of history in memory. On failure it shows a demo book.
market_scanner.py scans the top 100 USDT pairs by 24h quote volume on the scan's timeframe and 2 higher ones. It ranks longs, shorts, spot buys and grid coins with track records, and can run on a timer and post to Discord.
market_metrics.py builds the header from CoinGecko /global, alternative.me Fear & Greed and the derivatives figures, with jittered mock values as the fallback. market_index.py builds TOTAL/2/3 from about 20 coins' klines times circulating supply.
events.py reads the Forex Factory calendar and RSS news, tagging coins from a 37-coin map. symbols.py turns free text into a USDT pair. scanner.tickers serves /api/tickers from Binance's 24h ticker with no cache.
At every 1h/4h/1d close, the desk, signal alerts, trade manager, Kimi and the brief all call get_klines at about the same moment, so failover and caching behaviour at that moment decides what gets judged.

issues.title: A stream that falls back to synthetic never returns to Binance, so price and signal alerts go blind without any warning
issues.detail: StreamHub._run checks market.binance_usable() before every (re)connect. If it is false it calls _run_synthetic(), which is an endless `while True` loop, and then `return`. Nothing leads back to _run_binance. Binance becomes 'unusable' for 60 s after any failed REST call anywhere (MarketData.get_klines/get_range/list_symbols, FuturesDataService.cvd). It also becomes unusable after this stream's own first-connect failure: the branch `stream.source in ("connecting","synthetic")` calls mark_binance_down(), then `continue`, then lands in synthetic. Binance also drops every WebSocket after 24 h, so each long-lived stream goes through this check daily. AlertService._sync (1m per alerted symbol) and SignalAlertService._sync (per symbol and timeframe) hold their subscriptions for the life of the process, and both _watch loops drop source=='synthetic' messages. Once demoted they never fire again until a restart. The 'alerts' job keeps reporting OK from _expiry_loop; only the raw stream list shows 'synthetic'. The same happens at boot if the backend starts before the network (Windows login). Fix: _run_synthetic checks binance_usable() every ~15 s and returns so _run loops back to Binance. A stream's own connect failure should not demote all of Binance without a REST ping. AlertService and SignalAlertService should jobs.fail when a watched stream has been non-binance for more than 2 minutes.

issues.title: One timeout or 429 switches the whole backend to fake candles for 60 s, usually at a candle close
issues.detail: get_klines, get_range and list_symbols, plus FuturesDataService.cvd's live(), call mark_binance_down() on any exception that isn't BinanceRejected: ReadTimeout, 429, 5xx. For the next 60 s every caller gets synthetic data. At each 1h/4h/1d close the desk, signal alerts, trade manager, Kimi and the brief all hit Binance together, so that is when one slow answer is most likely. Consequences: (1) SignalAlertService._frames returns None on synthetic without using its RETRIES, and on_bar_close has already set _done[key]=bar_time, so that candle's signals are lost for good. (2) AgentDesk._coin returns an empty result for demo candles and the candle is never looked at again. (3) TradeManager skips the check. (4) The market scan carries on with synthetic data for the remaining coins. (5) The heatmap discards its history (separate issue). Fix: a circuit breaker. Mark Binance down only after 3 or more network failures within 30 s, or when /api/v3/ping fails. Retry a single failed request once with jitter. A 429/418 should pause requests for Retry-After without ever switching to synthetic. _frames should keep retrying on synthetic within RETRIES instead of returning.

issues.title: A timed market scan can post demo-data setups to Discord as if they were real
issues.detail: _scan merges setups from coins whose candles loaded as synthetic (for example after a mid-scan demotion, see above) with the real ones, so data_source becomes 'mixed'. MarketScanner.message() adds '(DEMO DATA)' only when result.data_source == 'synthetic'. result.best() does not filter on MarketSetup.data_source. With MARKET_SCAN_NOTIFY_TOP > 0, tick() can therefore send 'LONG XYZ: entry …, stop …, T1 …' built from random-walk candles to Discord with no label. Fix: when any coin loaded live, drop the synthetic rows (or rerun those coins). Label each line by its own data_source. Never notify from a mixed scan.

issues.title: One failed depth request throws away up to 4 hours of real order-book heatmap history
issues.detail: In auto mode, one httpx error in _fetch (timeout, 429, 5xx) leaves live=None in _sample, and so does a global 60 s demotion. Source becomes 'synthetic', which differs from tr.data_source 'binance', so tr.samples.clear() runs. A DemoBook is then created and _backfill adds 45 minutes of made-up history. When the next live sample succeeds, the source flips again and clears once more. Binance has no depth history, so the real columns cannot be recovered. test_failure_in_auto_mode_serves_a_marked_demo_book_with_backfill only covers a failure on the first sample. Fix: once a track holds live samples, skip a failed sample (leave a gap and set note='paused, retrying'). Switch to the demo book only when no live samples exist.

issues.title: 1000x perpetuals are not mapped, so PEPE, SHIB, BONK, FLOKI, LUNC, XEC and others show no futures data
issues.detail: funding, open_interest, long_short, walls(market='futures') and DerivativesService.symbol_snapshot all send the spot symbol to fapi as-is. /fapi/v1/premiumIndex?symbol=PEPEUSDT returns 400, which raises NotListed, so the panel says 'Binance has no perpetual for PEPEUSDT'. futures_context then tells the agent and the brief that there is no perp. LiquidationTracker stores events under '1000PEPEUSDT', so recent('PEPEUSDT') is always empty, and liquidation_levels gets no OI weighting. Fix: a spot→perp map built from /fapi/v1/exchangeInfo (PERPETUAL, TRADING; baseAsset prefixes 1000, 1000000, 1M), cached for 6 h. Apply the multiplier to mark/index prices, liquidation prices and quantities shown on the spot chart.

issues.title: find_symbol reads amounts like '500usdt' as a coin
issues.detail: The first regex accepts a digits-only base. Verified: 'buy INJ with 500usdt' gives '500USDT', and 'buy 200USDT of INJ' gives '200USDT'. llm.rule_intent (used when there is no LLM or it fails) uses the result without validation. The agent switches the chart to 500USDT, get_klines gets a 400 (BinanceRejected) and serves synthetic candles, and the agent draws zones on demo data. Fix: require a letter in the base (e.g. `(?=[A-Za-z0-9]*[A-Za-z])` before group 1). Also check the result against MarketData.list_symbols() before navigating, and fall through to the name and ticker scan when it isn't listed.

issues.title: list_symbols caches the 20-coin fallback list for an hour
issues.detail: When exchangeInfo fails once, or binance_usable() is false during a 60 s demotion, list_symbols still stores `self._symbols = (now + 3600, FALLBACK_SYMBOLS)`. For the next hour symbol search offers only 20 coins, and MarketIndexService.klines builds TOTAL/2/3 only from coins in that list. The failure also calls mark_binance_down(), which demotes all market data. Fix: cache the fallback for 60 s only, keep and return the last good list (persist it next to the candle cache), and don't demote Binance over exchangeInfo.

issues.title: No Binance rate-limit awareness: weight is never read and 429/418 Retry-After is never honoured
issues.detail:
A grep finds no use of X-MBX-USED-WEIGHT-1M or Retry-After anywhere in the backend. Main consumers of the shared 6,000/min IP weight:
- heatmap depth at limit 1000: weight 50 every 10 s per symbol, i.e. 300/min, up to 2,400/min at MAX_SYMBOLS=8, or 1,500/min per symbol with HEATMAP_DEPTH_LIMIT=5000
- uncached /api/tickers every 10 s per watchlist tab: weight 40 for 21–40 symbols, i.e. 240/min per tab
- each TOTAL chart: about 20 kline calls every 15 s
- market scans: 300+ kline calls plus track-record backtests
- the signed account import (myTrades and allOrders, weight 20 each) on the same IP
Binance turns repeated 429s into 418 IP bans lasting from 2 minutes to 3 days. In auto mode a 429 currently flips everything to demo data; in binance mode callers just retry. FuturesDataService._fapi and DerivativesService ignore it too. Fix: one shared gate used by MarketData._binance_get, _fapi and BinanceAccount that tracks used weight from the response headers, pauses for Retry-After, and defers background work (heatmap, scans, index) above about 70%.

issues.title: Gaps in the live stream are never repaired, upstream or in the browser
issues.detail: _run_binance seeds only derived intervals (get_klines(base, factor)) and publishes nothing from REST when it reconnects. On the browser side, AgenticChart.tsx connect() reconnects in ws.onclose without refetching via /api/klines?since=, and nothing listens for visibilitychange. A bar that closed during an upstream reconnect keeps its last partial OHLC on every open chart. After a laptop sleep or Wi-Fi drop, the missed bars are absent until a reload, and indicators and Kimi are computed on a series with holes. Fix: on every upstream (re)connect, publish the last 3 REST bars (closed=True for all but the newest) before streaming. In the frontend, refetch since=<last bar time> when the WebSocket reopens and when the tab becomes visible.

issues.title: Saving liquidations writes every event of the last 24 h as JSON on the event loop, once a minute
issues.detail: _run_stream calls LiquidationTracker.save() inline every 60 s. It serialises the whole 24h _events deque plus up to 200 events for every symbol. Binance sends up to one event per symbol per second across about 500 perps, so a cascade day reaches 100k+ tuples: several MB of JSON built and written on the loop that also runs every kline stream, alert and API request. That stall lands exactly when alerts matter. snapshot() also sums the full deque on every header refresh. Fix: keep the totals in 1-minute buckets (1,440 of them), keep the per-symbol cap, and write the file via asyncio.to_thread.

issues.title: Price alerts look only at the streamed close, so wicks between updates are missed
issues.detail: AlertService._watch calls on_price(symbol, candle.close) and ignores the high and low the kline update carries. Binance pushes 1m kline updates about every 2 s, so a wick that taps an alert level or demand zone and reverts between pushes never fires. For a spot trader with limit buys at demand, a wick fill is the event that matters. Fix: track each bar's running low and high per symbol, and evaluate the side using low (for levels below) and high (for levels above) before the close. Or use @bookTicker/@aggTrade for alerted symbols.

issues.title: get_klines caches per requested length and doesn't share requests in flight
issues.detail: The _cache key is (symbol, interval, limit). At one close the callers ask for different lengths: the desk CANDLES+1, signal alerts WINDOW+2, the trade manager LOOKBACK_BARS, Kimi 5000, the brief 300. Each one misses the cache, reads up to 5000 SQLite rows into pydantic Candles, makes its own forward REST call and upserts the same rows. Concurrent identical calls are not merged. The 256-entry FIFO is flushed by every market scan (100 coins × 3 timeframes). Fix: keep one in-memory series per (symbol, interval) at the largest length asked for and slice it per caller, share in-flight requests per key (asyncio future), and switch to LRU.

issues.title: /api/tickers calls Binance on every watchlist poll
issues.detail: tickers() sends every request straight to /api/v3/ticker/24hr?symbols=… (weight 2–40). Watchlist.tsx polls every 10 s (TICKER_MS) in each open tab, and nothing is shared between tabs or users. It also bypasses _binance_get's region fallback by calling market.client with market.rest_url. Fix: a 2–3 s server cache keyed by the symbol set, or serve from an all-market miniTicker stream (see ideas).

issues.title: Each TOTAL index poll makes about 20 Binance kline calls
issues.detail: Index charts and Compare overlays poll every 15 s (customSymbols.ts POLL_MS) with limit 3. That becomes klines(name, iv, 10) with a 15 s TTL, which runs about 20 get_klines(f"{tk}USDT", iv, 12) calls, each doing a forward REST fetch. One open TOTAL chart costs about 80 REST requests a minute. Fix: refresh history only when a candle closes, and build the live bar from streamed or miniTicker prices × the cached supply.

issues.title: Timed market scans ignore the candle clock and analyse the still-open candle
issues.detail: due() fires `minutes` after the previous scan, whatever the candle clock says. _scan passes get_klines output, whose newest bar is still open, to analyze and build_plan. A 4h scan at 13:20 therefore builds zones and impulses from a candle that is 1h20m old and can still turn, and the Discord top-N list reshuffles on the next run. The desk already waits for the close plus 45 s. Fix: schedule scans at the close plus 45 s, detect on closed bars only, and use the live price only for distance and R:R.

issues.title: When CoinGecko doesn't answer, the header shows hardcoded placeholder numbers jittered to look live
issues.detail: _mock uses MOCK_BASE (a $2.93T market cap, 57.3% BTC dominance, Fear & Greed 68) with random jitter whenever the keyless CoinGecko or alternative.me call fails, for example on a CoinGecko 429. The value is tagged mock, but it is meaningless and moves around. Fix: keep the last live value per metric and serve it as 'stale since HH:MM'. Mock only in synthetic mode or when nothing live has ever been fetched.

issues.title: News coin tags only know 37 hard-coded coins
issues.detail: COINS maps 37 tickers to full names. For any other coin, coin_pattern only matches '$X', '(X)' or the ticker in capitals (3+ letters). Headlines that name Render, Ondo, Jupiter or Fetch.ai by name never show on those coins' charts, and the agent's 'any news on X?' misses them. Fix: build the name map from CoinGecko /coins/markets (top 250, `name`) intersected with Binance base assets, cached daily. Keep COINS as overrides and keep the AMBIGUOUS guard.

ideas.title: Binance gateway: weight budget, shared requests, real circuit breaker and live candle tail
ideas.pitch: Charts and alerts never fall back to demo data because one request timed out. Candle closes are judged on real data every time, and opening a coin I'm already streaming is instant.
ideas.why: It fixes at the root the class of failures behind the worst bugs: global 60 s demotion, alert streams stuck on synthetic, lost signal and desk candles, and no 429 handling. It also removes most duplicate REST traffic at closes, which frees weight for the new data feeds below.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/binance_gate.py with BinanceGate.request(host, path, params, weight, priority). It reads x-mbx-used-weight-1m from every response, keeps a priority budget (interactive /api/klines and the agent > alerts/desk/trade manager at closes > scans, heatmap, index), and on 429/418 pauses that host until Retry-After without ever switching to synthetic. MarketData._binance_get, FuturesDataService._fapi, the DerivativesService calls and BinanceAccount all route through it.
Circuit breaker: gate.report_failure() replaces the mark_binance_down() calls. Binance counts as down after 3 network failures in 30 s; while down, /api/v3/ping (weight 1) is probed every 15 s, and on recovery the gate notifies StreamHub, which restarts synthetic streams on Binance.
Sharing in MarketData: one in-memory numpy series per (symbol, interval) replaces the per-limit _cache, an asyncio future per key around _binance_cached shares in-flight requests, and StreamHub._publish feeds closed bars into it (market.ingest_closed(), which also saves to candle_store). get_klines then needs no REST call for a streamed key whose last closed bar is current.
/api/status market block gains weight_used/limit, paused_until, breaker state and coalesced count.
Tests: httpx.MockTransport cases for 429 + Retry-After, coalescing, breaker thresholds and synthetic→Binance recovery.
ideas.risk: Touches the hottest path. DATA_SOURCE=binance/synthetic behaviour and the existing tests must stay intact. Background jobs could be starved (give each priority a floor). The live tail has to fall back to REST when a stream missed a close.

ideas.title: Market radar: one all-market stream for live movers, volume spikes and breadth
ideas.pitch: A Discord ping when one of my coins wakes up, e.g. 'INJ +3.8% in 5 min on 7x its normal volume, H4 supply 1.2% above', plus a radar tab showing what's moving and how broad the move is, without waiting for a scan.
ideas.why: Today nothing watches the whole market in real time: the scanner runs on demand or on a timer over candles, and the watchlist polls REST every 10 s per tab. One free WebSocket covers every USDT pair every second. It replaces the uncached ticker polling and the scanner's weight-80 universe call, and gives breadth, the market-wide context a spot buyer lacks.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/ticker_hub.py TickerHub, started in main.lifespan. It holds one connection to {ws_url}/!miniTicker@arr, with the same reconnect and backoff as DerivativesService._run_stream, and stores the latest fields s, c, o, h, l, v, q, E per symbol. Every 5 s it appends (t, c, q) to a per-symbol deque (1 h). Derived on demand: ret_5m/15m/1h, volume rate (positive Δq per minute ÷ (q/1440), EWMA), distance to the 24h high/low, and breadth over the top 100 by quote volume (advancers/decliners, % above the 24h open, median return).
Endpoints:
- GET /api/radar: movers, spikes, breadth.
- /api/tickers: served from TickerHub when data is under 5 s old.
- WS /ws/tickers?symbols=: pushes watchlist prices every second; Watchlist.tsx drops its TICKER_MS polling.
- MarketScanner.universe(): read from TickerHub.
RadarAlerts loop (every 15 s, jobs.declare): checks the watchlist, Binance holdings and desk coins for a 5-minute move of at least k × ATR with vol_rate ≥ 4. Messages go out via AlertService.notify with the nearest zone (WatchlistCache) and the newest matching headline (EventsService.headlines). Per-coin cooldown.
Agent tool market_radar in agent_loop for 'what's moving?'. A 'Radar' dock tab in dockPanels.tsx.
ideas.risk: miniTicker is a rolling 24h window, so volume deltas are noisy as old volume rolls off: use positive deltas and an EWMA. It pushes only symbols that changed. A single connection needs the REST fallback. Default the alerts to watched or held coins only to avoid spam.

ideas.title: Who is driving the move: spot vs perp flow read
ideas.pitch: Before I buy, the app tells me whether a pump is real spot buying or leverage that's likely to unwind, and whether a dump is longs getting flushed while spot buyers absorb.
ideas.why: Spot CVD, OI, funding and liquidations are all fetched already but shown separately, and only the agent sees them, as raw numbers. A spot-only buyer gets the most from the combination: a leverage-led rally (perp CVD and OI rising, spot CVD flat, funding up) is the classic 'don't chase', and a long flush with positive spot CVD is the classic dip to buy.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/flow_read.py.
Inputs:
- perp CVD from /fapi/v1/klines (weight 1–5) through FuturesDataService._fapi, reusing cvd_rows (field 9 is taker-buy base volume on futures too)
- spot CVD from FuturesDataService.cvd
- open_interest(period) rows
- funding() rate and mark−index basis
- derivatives.recent_liquidations
Per window (last 4/12/24 bars of 1h or the chart's timeframe) compute Δprice%, spot Δ USD, perp Δ USD, ΔOI%, Δfunding and long/short liquidation USD. Rules map these to one label: spot_led_rally, leverage_led_rally, short_squeeze, long_flush, spot_absorption or distribution, each with a one-line reason and the numbers.
Outputs:
- GET /api/flow?symbol=&interval=
- futures_context['flow'] and a sentence in ta_agent._futures_lines
- a card in MarketDataPanel.tsx and a brief line per held coin
- AgentDesk stores features['flow'] at call time, so the Record tab can later show which flows its demand calls work in
Each label and the following 24h return go into an SQLite table (db.migrate), so the panel can show each label's hit rate once there are enough samples. Spot-only coins fall back to spot CVD plus price.
ideas.risk: The thresholds are heuristics: present the output as a read, not a signal, until the stored hit rates back it. Needs the 1000x perp mapping fix. Futures data is unavailable from US IPs.
