ideas.title: Capitulation-into-demand alert from the liquidation stream
ideas.pitch: 'INJ long flush: $1.4M of longs liquidated in 5 min (9x normal), OI −6%, price inside H4 demand 23.90–24.30, spot buyers absorbing.' That's the dip I want to bid, sent to Discord as it happens.
ideas.why: The !forceOrder@arr stream already runs and keeps per-symbol events, but they only feed a 24h header total and a list in the panel. For a spot buyer, forced selling into support is among the best entries, and no current signal alert uses order flow (SIGNALS in signal_alerts.py covers price, RSI, Kimi and structure only).
ideas.how:
Add listeners to LiquidationTracker.add_events in derivatives.py. New backend/app/flow_alerts.py FlushWatch keeps 1-minute long and short liquidation buckets per perp symbol in SQLite (db.migrate 'liq_minutes(symbol, minute, long_usd, short_usd)'), giving a 7-day baseline as the median and MAD of 5-minute sums.
It fires on a watched or held coin when the 5-minute long-liquidation sum is at least max(MIN_USD, median + 4·MAD) and price is inside or within 0.5 ATR of a 4h/1d support or demand zone (ta_agent.analyze on cached candles).
The message adds the 15-minute OI change (open_interest '5m') and the sign of spot CVD over the last 15 minutes. It is registered as signal kind 'liq_flush' in signal_alerts.SIGNALS, so it appears in the Signal alerts UI and History and goes through AlertService.notify, with a suggested limit at the zone top and an invalidation under it.
Optionally the desk logs it as a watched zone, so its learning compares flush entries with ordinary zone entries.
ideas.risk: Binance sends at most one liquidation per symbol per second; comparing against each coin's own baseline cancels most of that bias. Coins without a perp can't use it. Dumps in a strong downtrend give false positives; the zone and CVD conditions filter most of them. Needs the 1000x symbol mapping, with prices scaled.

ideas.title: Keep order flow in every candle: taker-buy volume, trade count, quote volume
ideas.pitch: The agent can say 'sellers hit hard into the demand zone but price held: absorption', and CVD loads from cache instantly instead of re-downloading.
ideas.why: Binance klines already carry taker-buy volume (field 9), trade count (8) and quote volume (7), and the stream carries V, n and q. Both parsers throw them away. The detectors, the desk features and the backtests are therefore blind to delta, and futures_data.cvd has to page raw klines uncached (_spot_kline_rows) on every 60 s chart poll.
ideas.how:
candle_store.py: add migration columns taker_buy REAL, trades INTEGER and quote REAL to candles and range_candles (checked via PRAGMA table_info).
Parsers: parse_binance_kline and the _binance_span tuples keep r[7], r[8] and r[9]; stream_hub.parse_ws_kline keeps k['q'], k['n'] and k['V'].
Schemas: schemas.Candle gains optional taker_buy, trades and quote_volume, left out of /api/klines unless `fields=flow`. candles_to_df and _rows_df add taker_buy and delta columns.
FuturesDataService.cvd becomes a projection of get_klines/get_range.
New detectors in patterns.py: absorption(df, zone) (a touch bar with delta ≤ −2σ that closes back inside or above the zone) and delta divergence at sweeps.
desk_calls.candidates adds features delta_touch and trades_ratio; scanner.summarize adds an 'absorption at demand' signal; synthetic data reuses synthetic_cvd_raw's taker share.
Old rows with NULL flow fields get a market.ensure_flow(symbol, interval, n) that re-downloads those bars once.
ideas.risk: Schema migration on a possibly large cache file. A mix of NULL and filled rows until the backfill finishes. Bigger in-memory frames. This is Binance spot taker flow only, not exchange-wide.

ideas.title: Delist and monitoring guard for coins I hold
ideas.pitch: If Binance schedules a delisting of anything I hold, have in Earn, watch or the desk trades, I hear about it on Discord the hour it's published, with my position size, and the desk stops buying it.
ideas.why: For a spot holder a delisting is the single most damaging event and it is rare. Nothing in the app watches for it today (grep finds no delist, listing or announcement logic). The read-only key already in place is enough.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/listing_watch.py ListingWatch, run hourly (jobs.declare 'listing_watch'):
(a) a new BinanceAccount.delist_schedule() makes a signed GET to /sapi/v1/spot/delist-schedule (weight 100), returning [{delistTime, symbols}].
(b) an exchangeInfo diff saved in db.py: symbols leaving TRADING, and new USDT pairs counted as new listings.
(c) optional BINANCE_ANNOUNCEMENTS=on reads the Binance announcement list for the delisting and new-listing categories.
Results are matched against BinanceImportService.positions() (spot and Simple Earn), desk symbols, the active watchlist and paper holdings. Each (symbol, delistTime) is notified once via AlertService.notify and record().
GET /api/listings drives a Watchlist badge ('delist 15 Oct'). MarketScanner.pick_universe and AgentDesk._coin skip delisting coins. The agent's facts get listing_status, so 'should I buy XYZ?' warns.
ideas.risk: Check the delist-schedule endpoint on Trick's key first; the answer format is assumed from the docs. The announcement endpoints are unofficial and can change, so keep them optional. Without a key it falls back to the exchangeInfo diff.

ideas.title: Market regime tape: record the market's state on every desk call and learn from it
ideas.pitch: The desk's Record shows whether its demand calls work in risk-on vs risk-off markets, and the brief opens with 'Regime: risk-off (BTC 1d down, breadth 28%, stablecoin dominance +0.4 pt)'.
ideas.why: desk_calls.candidates records only coin-level features (kind, freshness, HTF, trend agreement, RSI, ATR%). Nothing about BTC, breadth, stablecoin flows, OI or upcoming CPI/FOMC is captured, so the learning can never find that a setup only works when the market cooperates. All the inputs already exist or come almost free.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/market_regime.py RegimeService, hourly at :01 (jobs). Inputs:
- BTCUSDT 4h/1d trend via market_scanner.trend_of
- breadth: % of the top 100 above EMA50 on 4h, from candles the last scan cached, or TickerHub's % above the 24h open
- stablecoin dominance (usdt + usdc from the same CoinGecko /global payload)
- 24h change of total OI (derivatives.open_interest)
- median funding of the top-40 perps from one /fapi/v1/premiumIndex call without a symbol (weight 10)
- Fear & Greed
- a high-impact USD event in the next 24h (events.upcoming_events)
These give a score, a label (risk_on, neutral or risk_off, with hysteresis) and the reasons, stored as regime(ts, label, score, json) via db.migrate.
AgentDesk._coin stores features['regime']. desk_learning gets regime_table() (like bucket_table), shown in DeskPanel.tsx as 'By market regime'. It is report-only until each regime has 20+ finished calls; after that an optional REGIME_SIZING setting scales the Kelly size by the regime's edge. Brief line and agent tool 'market regime'.
ideas.risk: More splits mean thinner evidence, so keep it to reporting before it gates anything. The label could flip back and forth near thresholds (hysteresis prevents that). Breadth by volume rank is skewed by memecoins.

ideas.title: Header: stablecoin and ETH dominance from the same call, and last-good values instead of mocks
ideas.pitch: A USDT+USDC dominance figure in the header, the risk-off gauge many spot traders watch, with an alert when it jumps. When CoinGecko hiccups I see the last real number and its age, not a placeholder.
ideas.why: MarketMetricsService._coingecko already receives market_cap_percentage for usdt, usdc and eth but reads only btc. Mocked values with jitter make a CoinGecko rate limit look like data.
ideas.how:
market_metrics._build: add Metric 'stable_dominance' (usdt + usdc) and 'eth_dominance' from gecko['market_cap_percentage']. Keep hourly samples in the service so the header can show a 24h change, since /global gives none for these. metric_alerts.NAMES and POINTS gain both (moves in points). MarketHeader.tsx renders them.
Replace _mock with self._last_live[key], returned as source 'stale' with a note such as 'CoinGecko didn't answer; value from 14:02'. That means adding 'stale' to schemas.Metric.source and the frontend types. overview_facts treats a stale value as available and gives its age. Mock only in synthetic mode.
ideas.risk: The Literal change reaches the frontend types and metric_alerts (stale values must not fire alerts). CoinGecko's percentages are of its own total, which includes stablecoins.

ideas.title: Korea and Coinbase premium gauges
ideas.pitch: 'INJ Korea premium 6% vs BTC's 0.8%: Korean retail is chasing it' warns me off buying a local top, and a negative Coinbase premium tells me US spot is selling.
ideas.why: These are free, keyless spot-demand gauges a spot trader uses, and the app has nothing like them. They complement Binance-only order flow with demand from other venues and are cheap to fetch.
ideas.how:
New backend/app/premiums.py.
- Upbit: GET https://api.upbit.com/v1/market/all (cached daily) to know which coins have KRW markets, and GET https://api.upbit.com/v1/ticker?markets=KRW-BTC,KRW-USDT,KRW-INJ,… (one batched request).
- Korea premium for a coin = KRW price ÷ KRW-USDT ÷ Binance USDT price − 1. Report the coin's premium minus BTC's, so the structural part cancels.
- Coinbase Exchange: GET https://api.exchange.coinbase.com/products/BTC-USD/ticker (and {COIN}-USD for held coins listed there). Coinbase premium = BTC-USD ÷ BTCUSDT − 1.
Cached 30 s, with an hourly history in SQLite for 7-day sparklines.
Shown as a card in MarketDataPanel.tsx, as 'premiums' in the agent facts (agent.py, next to futures_context) and as a brief line per held coin. A new metric alert, e.g. 'Coinbase premium below −0.1% for 3h'.
ideas.risk: Not every coin has a KRW market (handle missing ones). KRW-USDT carries its own premium, which is why it is used as the FX rate. Upbit and Coinbase public rate limits (cache, batch). This adds two outside dependencies; they degrade to 'unavailable' like events.py.

ideas.title: Build the heatmap's order book from the depth stream, with trade bubbles and pulled-wall detection
ideas.pitch: The heatmap updates every second instead of every 10, shows where trades actually printed, and tells me when a big bid wall was pulled just before price got there.
ideas.why: Polling REST depth costs weight 50 per 10 s per symbol, the largest steady weight consumer, and it can't see walls that flash between snapshots, which is where spoofing hides. Executed volume, the other half of a Bookmap-style view, isn't shown at all.
ideas.how:
In orderbook_heatmap.py, add _LocalBook per tracked symbol. It uses one combined stream {ws_url}/{sym}@depth@100ms/{sym}@aggTrade and Binance's local-book procedure: buffer the diffs, take one REST snapshot (/api/v3/depth?limit=1000), drop events with u ≤ lastUpdateId, apply from U ≤ lastUpdateId+1 ≤ u, and resync on a gap. It keeps a price→qty dict within ±range_pct.
_sample runs every 1 s from the local book; bucket_book is unchanged. aggTrade quote volume is summed per bin into each column (a new 'trades' array) for frontend/lib/heatmap.ts to draw as bubbles.
wall_events: a wall bin that loses more than 70% while price is over 0.1% away is 'pulled'; one price traded through is 'eaten'. They are returned with walls and surfaced as chart markers.
futures_data.walls reads the live book when the symbol is tracked, so the second depth fetch goes away. REST polling stays as the fallback.
ideas.risk: Resync and sequence-gap bugs. Python CPU for BTC at 100 ms (trim to ±range; sample at 1 s). More memory per symbol. Needs tests driven by recorded streams.

ideas.title: News tagging from the exchange's own coin list, plus 'why is it moving' on alerts
ideas.pitch: Headlines about Render, Ondo or Jupiter show on those charts, and a radar or flush alert carries the headline that most likely explains the move.
ideas.why: events.COINS is a 37-coin hard-coded map, so most watchlist alts are only tagged when a headline writes '$X' or '(X)'. The agent's 'why is X pumping?' misses them too.
ideas.how: events.py gets build_coin_map(): Binance base assets from MarketData.list_symbols() intersected with CoinGecko /coins/markets names (top 250; MarketIndexService already calls that endpoint for 50), cached daily. COINS stays as overrides. Bases that are English words get added to AMBIGUOUS automatically (name or $ticker required). EventsService.headlines(symbol, hours=6, limit=1) is attached to the radar and flush alert messages and to the agent's facts for 'why' questions.
ideas.risk: Coin names that are common words (Render, Jupiter, Ondo) can tag the wrong headlines. Require the name near a crypto word or ticker.

readers.map:
alerts.py (AlertService): price alerts (cross/zone, repeat with a fixed 5-min cooldown, expiry, note) stored in JSON. It holds one 1m StreamHub subscription per symbol and checks every live update, skipping synthetic prices. It also owns /ws/alerts (snapshot providers plus broadcast), the 500-item AlertHistory, and the only delivery path: Channel = Telegram sendMessage / Discord webhook `{"content": text}`, plain text, sent by send_all/send_long, with fire-and-forget notify().
signal_alerts.py (SignalAlertService): 16 signals (Kimi labels, RSI divergence/OB/OS, sweeps, new zones, BOS, the sell_check lost_support/at_resistance, zone_trigger). Each is judged per (symbol, interval) stream 2 s after a candle closes. Preview replays the detector with scan_history. `owner` marks app-managed alerts (sync_owned).
zone_triggers.py: pure lower-timeframe confirmation (CHoCH/BOS, sweep, engulfing) inside a fixed or re-detected higher-timeframe zone. It fires once per touch, with a cooldown and a suggested stop.
metric_alerts.py: header metrics above/below/moves, polled every 60 s, fire once.
holdings_watch.py: every 10 min it syncs lost_support + at_resistance alerts (owner="holdings") to Binance spot holdings and tracked bot coins.
trade_manager.py: advises managed trades on each closed candle (stop, targets + breakeven, structure/ATR trail, CHoCH against) and closes Binance-sourced trades when the position goes.
brief.py: scheduled plain-text brief (mood, holdings, desk lines, per-coin blocks, today's events) plus the weekly level check. The desk, market scanner and journal review also call alerts.send_text.
jobs.py: ok/fail/overdue registry behind the Status tab.
Frontend: useAlerts (ws snapshots, beep + desktop Notification for price/signal/trade_advice). AlertsPanel has the Price/Signals/Triggers/History/Brief tabs with previews drawn on the chart. MarketAlerts polls every 30 s. AlertToasts shows only price and signal toasts (max 4, manual dismiss).
No embeds, images, links, buttons, priorities, quiet hours, digests or delivery tracking exist anywhere.

issues.title: One Binance blip at a candle close permanently skips that candle's signal checks
issues.detail: on_bar_close() sets self._done[key]=bar_time BEFORE _frames() succeeds. _frames() returns None at once (no retry) when get_klines answers 'synthetic'. MarketData.get_klines (DATA_SOURCE=auto) answers synthetic for 60 s after ANY failed klines request (mark_binance_down, market_data.py:130). So one timed-out request at a busy close (00:00 UTC: the 1h, 4h and 1d closes, the desk, Kimi and the trade manager all hit REST together) makes every signal check in that minute return None. Those bars are never re-checked, because _scheduled/_done already hold them and the next close only schedules the next bar. That day's 1d Kimi B+ or lost_support on INJ is silently lost, and _after_close still reports jobs.ok. _kimi_signals has the same synthetic → None path. Fix: treat synthetic or missing candles as 'retry later'. Keep retrying for about 2 minutes (longer than the 60 s down window), set _done only after a real check, and on final failure call jobs.fail and reset _scheduled so the next kline message re-queues the bar.

issues.title: Notification bursts hit Discord's webhook rate limit and are dropped silently
issues.detail: Every producer sends its own HTTP POST concurrently: AlertService.notify() → _spawn(send_text) for each signal fire (signal_alerts._fire), trade advice (trade_manager._announce) and metric fire, plus on_price's send_all and the desk's send_text 45 s after a close. Discord webhooks allow about 5 requests per 2 s; Telegram allows 1 msg/s per chat. Nothing reads 429 / Retry-After: Channel.send calls raise_for_status, send_all/send_long log a warning and drop the message. At 00:00 UTC (1h+4h+1d closes) with holdings watch on 8 coins plus watchlist Kimi alerts, several fires arrive within the same 2 s, and the ones past the limit never reach the phone. Fix: one asyncio queue + worker per channel. It honours Discord's JSON retry_after / X-RateLimit-Reset-After and Telegram's parameters.retry_after, retries 5xx with backoff, and coalesces messages queued within about 2 s into one post (Discord allows 10 embeds per message).

issues.title: Coins parked in Simple Earn drop out of the holdings watch
issues.detail: HoldingsWatch.coins() reads only positions['manual']['spot'] (plus bots). binance_import.positions() puts Earn holdings under manual.earn, which is never read. Moving INJ into flexible or locked Earn is not selling it, yet at the next 10-minute run sync_owned() removes its lost_support/at_resistance alerts. The same gap exists in brief.holdings_lines() and brief.build(include_holdings). Fix: merge manual.earn rows by symbol (sum value, keep product and redeem_at) with source='earn'. The message can then say 'locked until 14 Oct'.

issues.title: Managing an older trade fires a burst of stale advice to Discord
issues.detail: TradeManager.add() → check() → review() walks every closed candle since opened_at (from_journal uses e.taken_at) across up to 300 bars. Each historical event gets its own key and is _announce()d, one notify() each. A journal long taken 3 days ago, managed on 15m, replays about 288 bars and can emit several 'Trail the stop to …' and 'Structure broke down …' messages for things long past, all at once (also feeding the 429 problem). Fix: run the catch-up review with quiet=True (keep the advice on the trade, mark old ones 'done', no notify), then send one summary: 'Caught up 3 days: T1 hit, best stop now 7.42'.

issues.title: Delivery failures are invisible: Status shows 'Discord connected' while every message fails
issues.detail: /api/status returns alerts.channel_status, which only says a channel is configured, and StatusPanel draws it green ('connected'). send_all/send_long return {discord: False}, but notify(), signal _fire, trade _announce and metric check ignore the result. brief.send() records 'Market brief' in History even when every channel failed, and BriefService._run reports jobs.ok. A deleted webhook (HTTP 404) means weeks of missed alerts behind a green Status tab. Fix: AlertService tracks last_ok, last_fail, last_error and failures_24h per channel, exposed in /api/status and the ChannelBar. History items get delivered: {discord: bool}. Scheduled senders call jobs.fail when every channel failed.

issues.title: Jobs report 'ok' right after failing, so errors never show in Status
issues.detail: TradeManager._loop calls jobs.fail() inside the per-trade except, then calls jobs.ok() at the end of the same iteration, so last_ok > last_fail and the state is 'ok'. sync_positions() exceptions are only logged. The same pattern appears in brief.py, where tick() swallows send exceptions (log.exception, return False) and _run() calls jobs.ok, and in holdings_watch.py, where run() turns a positions failure into last.error and the loop calls jobs.ok. Fix: count failures per iteration, call jobs.ok only when there were none, and have tick()/run() return an error the loop can report.

issues.title: Timed market-scan notifications send short setups to a spot-only trader and repeat the same list
issues.detail: tick() sends self.message(result, n), and message() uses result.best(n) with direction=None, so longs and shorts are mixed, although best_spot() already exists. With MARKET_SCAN_SCHEDULE=15m=10 the same top setups are re-sent every 10 minutes. Fix: notify from best_spot (or add MARKET_SCAN_NOTIFY_SIDE, default spot) and skip setups (symbol+entry key) already sent in the last N hours.

issues.title: Repeat price alerts on a choppy level fire every 5 minutes all day
issues.detail: evaluate() re-arms on time only (REPEAT_COOLDOWN_MS = 5 min) and fires on any change of side of the live 1m close, which updates every ~2 s. Price oscillating around 7.95 gives up to 12 Discord messages an hour, and every flip also rewrites alerts.json and broadcasts a snapshot. Fix: hysteresis. After a fire, re-arm only once price has been rearm_pct (e.g. max(0.3%, 0.25 ATR)) beyond the level on the far side, and make the cooldown a per-alert field.

issues.title: Discord messages allow @everyone / @here mentions
issues.detail: build_channels() sends {"content": text[:2000]} with no allowed_mentions. Labels and notes (including ones the agent's LLM writes) go into the text verbatim, so '@everyone' in a note pings the whole server. Fix: always send allowed_mentions: {"parse": []}, and later allow only the owner's user id for urgent cards.

issues.title: The brief follows the watchlist only when the Brief tab is opened and saved
issues.detail: BriefTab keeps 'Use my watchlist' in localStorage (ac:brief-use-watchlist) and sends the symbols only on Save ('Your watchlist changed since the last save' warning). ChartWorkspace already pushes the active watchlist to the desk with syncDeskSymbols. Fix: add follow_watchlist to BriefSettings and resolve symbols from the list the desk follows (desk.symbols()), so adding a coin reaches the next brief with no clicks.

issues.title: Market alerts: no toast or sound, no re-arm, and polling instead of the WebSocket
issues.detail: metric_alerts.check() only records history and calls notify(). useAlerts ignores 'metric_snapshot' (and 'desk' messages), so a fired market alert never beeps or toasts in the app. MarketAlerts re-fetches every 30 s although the backend broadcasts metric_snapshot on every change. A fired alert can only be deleted, never re-armed: there is no endpoint, and a 'moves' alert would need base_value reset. Fix: handle metric_snapshot in useAlerts and add POST /api/metric-alerts/{id}/rearm.

issues.title: History has no Trade filter, and the MARKET symbol opens a chart for a pair that doesn't exist
issues.detail: HistoryTab's filter offers All/Price/Signals/Briefs/Desk, but trade advice is recorded as kind 'trade', so it is reachable only under All. metric_alerts records symbol 'MARKET', and the row's symbol button calls p.onPickSymbol('MARKET'), switching the chart to a pair that doesn't exist. Fix: add a Trades filter, and render the symbol button only for real pairs (skip 'MARKET').

issues.title: Signal preview draws sell signals as buy arrows
issues.detail: In SignalsTab.runPreview, `long` is true unless the signal is in [kimi_sell, rsi_bear_div, sweep_high, new_supply, bos_bear, rsi_overbought]. lost_support and at_resistance are missing from that list, so previewing 'Lost support (sell)' draws up-arrows below the candles. Fix: add both, or better, take the side from a shared SIGNAL_SIDE map in lib/alerts.ts.

issues.title: Toasts never auto-dismiss, can't be clicked, and skip trade, desk and market events
issues.detail: Toasts are created only by onAlertsFired/onSignalFired and stay until dismissed by hand (capped at 4). Clicking a toast doesn't open the coin. trade_advice gets a beep and a desktop notification but no toast; desk calls and metric fires get nothing. The desktop notification body uses the raw number (`price ${price}` in useAlerts), not formatPrice. Fix: auto-dismiss non-urgent toasts after about 12 s, make click → onPickSymbol(symbol, interval), add toasts for trade/desk/metric events, and use formatPrice.

ideas.title: Alert cards: Discord embeds with a clickable deep link into the app
ideas.pitch: Every ping on my phone looks like a trading card: green for buy-side, red for sell/stop, the levels in neat fields, and one tap opens INJ 4h in my app with the alert focused.
ideas.why: Today every message is one plain `content` string (Telegram: a plain sendMessage). The brief splits into 6-10 walls of text, and a desk call is three run-on sentences. Embeds make alerts scannable in a second, and the link closes the gap between 'pinged' and 'looking at the chart'. This is also the base the chart images, buttons and digest ideas build on.
ideas.how: New backend/app/notify.py with Notice {kind, symbol, interval, title, description, fields[(name,value,inline)], side buy|sell|info, url, image?, priority, text (plain fallback)}. Channel.send_notice(): Discord POST {embeds:[{title,url,description,color,fields,timestamp,footer}], allowed_mentions:{parse:[]}}; Telegram sendMessage with parse_mode=HTML (escaped). A builder next to each producer: alerts.describe_fire (Level/Zone, Price, Label, Note), signal_alerts._fire (Signal, Close, Suggested stop for triggers, Note), desk_calls.call_text/outcome_text (Buy zone, Limit, TP %, Invalidation %, Confidence, Expected R, Paper size), trade_manager._announce (Action, Take %, New stop, R now), metric_alerts.check, and brief.render_brief as up to 10 embeds (header plus one per section, coins as inline fields; 6000 chars max). Deep link: env PUBLIC_APP_URL (LAN or Tailscale address) → url `${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/?symbol=INJUSDT&tf=4h&focus=alert:<id>`. On mount, ChartWorkspace reads window.location.search, sets the active chart, opens the matching dock tab (Alerts/Desk/Live trades), then history.replaceState. Delivery goes through the per-channel rate-limit queue from the 429 fix, which coalesces notices queued within 2 s into one post. send_text stays for tests and plain fallback.
ideas.risk: Discord embed limits (25 fields, 1024 chars per field, 6000 per message) need truncation. The link only works where PUBLIC_APP_URL is reachable (fine on LAN or Tailscale; omitted when unset).

ideas.title: Chart snapshot on every card
ideas.pitch: When 'Lost support' fires on INJ 4h I see the candles, the broken zone, the next support and where it fired, right in Discord, without opening anything.
ideas.why: A picture answers 'is this real?' in two seconds. The alert service runs with every tab closed, so the browser's camera button can't help. The image has to be rendered on the backend from the candles and levels the alert already has.
ideas.how: backend/app/chart_render.py using matplotlib (Agg backend; add matplotlib>=3.8 to requirements.txt). render(df, boxes, lines, markers, title) -> PNG bytes: the last 120 closed candles of the alert's timeframe in the app's dark palette, the zone as axhspan, the level as axhline, the trigger's suggested stop dashed red, the desk call's entry/TP/invalidation, a marker on the firing candle, and a last-price tag. Inputs already exist at each fire: signal _fire has the Frame df and the hit, zone triggers have ZoneBand and stop, desk calls have zone_low/high, entry, tp and stop, managed trades have entry, stop, targets and advised_stop. Run it in asyncio.to_thread behind Semaphore(1), with a cache keyed by (symbol, interval, last bar, overlay hash) so several alerts on one close render once. Attach it only to signal, trigger, new desk call and trade advice cards, not to repeat price alerts. Discord: multipart payload_json + files[0] with embed image.url='attachment://chart.png'. Telegram: sendPhoto with caption up to 1024 chars, then the full text if longer.
ideas.risk: New dependency, and 100-250 ms CPU per image during close bursts. Skip the image when the send queue is long or the render fails; the card still goes out.

ideas.title: Two-way Discord bot: buttons on cards and /ask from the phone
ideas.pitch: I tap [Snooze 4h], [Moved it] or [I took it] under an alert, and type /ask how does INJ look on the 4h? from my phone and get the agent's answer with a chart.
ideas.why: Every alert today is one-way. Snoozing a noisy level, confirming a moved stop or pausing a coin all mean walking to the PC. The agent and the brief are only reachable in the browser. A bot connected over the gateway needs no public URL, which suits a backend running at home. The exchange key is read-only, so buttons only change the app's own state.
ideas.how: backend/app/discord_bot.py on discord.py 2.x, started in main.py's lifespan when DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID and DISCORD_OWNER_ID are set. Cards go through the bot instead of the webhook. Persistent buttons use View(timeout=None) with custom_id 'ac:<action>:<kind>:<id>', routed in on_interaction and owner-only (interaction.user.id). Price alert: Snooze 1h/4h (new PriceAlert.snoozed_until, checked in evaluate()), Disarm, Re-arm. Signal alert: Pause coin 24h, Off (SignalAlertService.update). Trade advice: Moved it (TradeManager.update advice_id + advice_status='done', which moves the tracked stop), Dismiss. Desk call: I took it (POST journal entry from the call + TradeManager.add). Slash commands: /ask text [coin] [tf] → the same function as POST /api/agent/analyze, with interaction.response.defer() because qwen2.5:7b can take more than 3 s, replying with the summary and a chart snapshot. Also /brief (BriefService.build), /holdings, /desk (summary + running calls) and /alerts (armed alerts nearest price). The bot token goes into the logging redact filter like Channel.secrets.
ideas.risk: New dependency and a long-lived gateway connection (reconnects handled by the library). The token must never reach the browser. Every interaction must check the owner id. Keep the webhook path as a fallback when the bot is down.

ideas.title: Notification router: priorities, quiet hours with a morning digest, per-kind channels
ideas.pitch: At night only things that matter for my bag wake me (a lost support on a coin I hold, a stop hit). The rest waits for a single 'while you slept' card, and desk chatter goes to its own channel.
ideas.why: Every source posts straight to one webhook, around the clock, at equal weight. A Kimi label on a watchlist coin, a desk fill, a market scan and a stop hit look the same. Volume grows with each feature (desk, holdings watch, triggers), so without triage the owner learns to ignore the channel.
ideas.how: Settings in SQLite (db.py kv table) or a NOTIFY_STORE JSON, with a 'Delivery' section in AlertsPanel's ChannelBar: quiet hours (start, end, tz), minimum priority while quiet, per-kind on/off, per-kind channel. Env DISCORD_WEBHOOKS=alerts=url,desk=url,brief=url,trades=url, with DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL as the default. Priority map in notify.py. Urgent: trade stop/structure, lost_support or at_resistance on a held coin (owner=='holdings'), price alerts marked urgent. Normal: signals, triggers, new desk calls, trade targets. Low: desk fills and expiries, market scans, metric alerts, repeat fires. While quiet, non-urgent notices go to a held_notices table and are flushed at quiet end as one digest card grouped by coin ('INJ: lost H4 demand 7.10, Kimi B- 4h · SOL: desk call filled'). Urgent cards put <@OWNER_ID> in content with allowed_mentions.users=[owner], so the phone pings even with the channel muted. 'Mute INJ 12h' rows in the same table are honoured by the router, and History shows held items with a 'held' badge.
ideas.risk: A misconfigured quiet window can hide something important, so urgent always bypasses it and the Alerts tab shows how many notices are being held.

ideas.title: Holdings guard: alerts that know your position (Earn included)
ideas.pitch: 'Rejected at resistance' on INJ also tells me I hold 312 INJ ($2,350, 18% of my coins) at avg 6.10 (+23%), that 120 are locked in Earn until the 14th, and what 25% would be.
ideas.why: Sell and trim signals are generic text today, even for coins the app knows you hold with their average entry. Spot traders decide by position size and P&L. Earn-locked coins can't be sold before redemption, and redemption dates pass unnoticed.
ideas.how: holdings_watch.py: merge positions['manual']['earn'] into coins() (fixes the Earn gap). Keep the latest positions snapshot from run() and add context(symbol) → {qty spot+earn, avg_entry, value, pnl_pct, share_of_coins, locked_qty, redeem_at}. signal_alerts._fire: when the symbol is held, add a 'Your position' field/line, plus an optional trim helper from new WatchSettings (trim_pct_at_resistance=25, sell_pct_on_lost_support=50) → '25% ≈ 78 INJ ≈ $590'. New owned alerts (owner='holdings'): signal 'below_entry' (a close X% under avg entry on the watch timeframe, avg taken from context) and an Earn unlock reminder sent once 24 h before redeem_at, keyed by position_id in HOLDINGS_WATCH_STORE. brief.holdings_lines also lists Earn rows with APR and end date.
ideas.risk: avg_entry exists only for coins with imported buys; the field is left out otherwise. Size suggestions are arithmetic on user-set percentages, not advice.

ideas.title: Desk-to-you handoff: auto-arm a timing trigger inside every desk call zone
ideas.pitch: When the desk calls 'buy INJ 7.10–7.25', I get pinged again at the moment a 15m candle confirms inside that zone, with the call's TP and invalidation, instead of hours before price gets there.
ideas.why: A desk call is announced at the close it is made, often 10-20 candles before price reaches the zone, so the owner either watches the chart or misses the fill window. The zone-trigger engine already does exactly this kind of lower-timeframe confirmation, but nobody connects it to the desk.
ideas.how: main.py: give AgentDesk a reference to SignalAlertService once both exist. Add DeskSettings.arm_triggers (default on). In AgentDesk._notify(c, 'new') for non-shadow calls: signals.add_trigger(ZoneTriggerSpec(symbol=c.symbol, interval={'1h':'5m','4h':'15m','1d':'15m'}[c.interval], zone=TriggerZone(source='fixed', price_low=c.zone_low, price_high=c.zone_high, direction='long', label=f'Desk {tfl} buy zone'), confirm='any', cooldown_min=60, repeat=False)) with a new owner=f'desk:{c.id}' parameter on add_trigger (SignalAlert.owner already exists). In AgentDesk.score(), when a call moves to tp/invalidated/expired/timed_out, remove alerts with that owner. The trigger fire appends the call: 'Desk zone confirmed on 15m: limit 7.25, TP 8.20 (+13%), wrong below 7.02, 58%.' The Triggers tab shows a 'Desk' badge for owner desk:*.
ideas.risk: Adds one closed-candle stream per active call, capped by max_active. Must be cleaned up on every terminal status, or orphan triggers stay armed.

ideas.title: Alert scorecard: does this alert actually lead anywhere?
ideas.pitch: Before I arm 'Lost support' on INJ 4h, the preview tells me it fired 9 times and price was lower 24 candles later 7 of 9 times (avg −4.1%). Months later the app tells me 'RSI > 70 on 1h has no edge, switch it off?'.
ideas.why: There is no feedback loop for alerts at all, while the desk has a full learning loop. Knowing which signals have worked on which coins and timeframes is the best noise filter there is, and it puts the owner's own Kimi labels to the test on his own coins.
ideas.how: (a) Instant backfill: in SignalAlertService.preview/preview_trigger, compute for each hit from scan_history/scan_triggers the forward return over 6 and 24 bars, the max run-up and the drawdown, from the candles already loaded (WINDOW+bars), and return stats {n, worked, avg_24, median_mfe, median_mae}. PreviewResult shows one sentence. (b) Live: table alert_outcomes in db.py (history_id, kind, signal, symbol, interval, side, fired_at, price, ret_6, ret_24, mfe, mae), filled by a 15-min job with market.get_range from fired_at. Side comes from a SIGNAL_SIDE map: buy = kimi_buy, rsi_bull_div, sweep_low, new_demand, bos_bull, rsi_oversold, long triggers; sell = the rest plus lost_support/at_resistance. For spot, a sell signal 'worked' when price was lower, i.e. selling saved that %. (c) SignalRow shows '7/9 worked, avg 3.2%', each card gets one record line, and after 15+ fires with a win rate of 40-60% and |avg| under round-trip fees, Signals/History flag 'no edge: switch off?'.
ideas.risk: Small samples mislead, so show n and say 'too few' under about 8, as track_record.py does. Forward-return windows overlap for frequent signals.

ideas.title: Candle-close confirmed level alerts, and hysteresis instead of a timer
ideas.pitch: 'Alert me if the 4h closes above 7.95' fires once on the close, not on a wick at 3 a.m., and a repeating alert doesn't chatter while price chops around the level.
ideas.why: Price alerts fire on any live 1m tick through the level, so wick fake-outs ping the owner. Repeats are throttled only by a 5-minute timer. Breakout and breakdown decisions for spot are made on closes, and signal alerts have no 'close beyond my level' option today.
ideas.how: schemas.py AlertSpec/PriceAlert and frontend lib/types.ts gain confirm: 'touch'|'close', confirm_interval (15m/1h/4h/1d), closes (1-3) and rearm_pct (default 0.3). Touch alerts stay in AlertService, but evaluate() re-arms a repeat alert only after price has been rearm_pct beyond the level on the far side (store rearm_side), replacing REPEAT_COOLDOWN_MS. Close alerts become a new signal 'level_close' in signal_alerts.py. It reuses the per-(symbol, interval) closed-candle watcher and fires when the last `closes` closes are beyond the level (or inside the zone) and the one before was not: '4h closed above 7.95 (close 8.03), 2 closes in a row'. UI: a 'Fire on' select (Touch / 15m / 1h / 4h / 1d close) in NewAlertForm and AlertEditor. Dragging the amber line keeps the mode. llm.py rule parser: 'if the 4h closes above X' → this alert.
ideas.risk: Two storage paths for 'price alerts' (AlertService vs SignalAlertService). Keep one row type in the UI so the owner doesn't see the split.

ideas.title: Attention-ranked brief with 'since last brief'
ideas.pitch: The morning brief opens with the 3 coins that need me (INJ broke its H4 demand, SOL is in a desk zone), gives the 12 quiet ones a single line, and tells me yesterday's realized PnL.
ideas.why: render_brief gives every coin the same 4-6 line block whether or not anything happened, so a 20-coin brief is 4-8 Discord messages of mostly unchanged numbers. changes.py already computes exactly 'what changed since then' (zones broke/tested/new, structure, Kimi, desk, alerts), but only for the chart card.
ideas.how: brief.py build(): for each coin call changes.changes(market, sym, iv, since=int(last_sent_at/1000), kimi, desk, alerts), which already exists. Score each coin: held +3, inside a zone +2, a zone broke or structure changed +2, Kimi signal +1, |since_last| ≥ 3% +1, desk call running +1. Coins scoring ≥ 2 get the full block plus 'Since last brief:' lines from changes()['lines']. The rest collapse into 'Quiet: BTC 61,200 (+0.4%), ETH 2,410 (−0.2%) …'. Add 'Yesterday: realized +$42 (3 sells)' from pnl_calendar when a key is set, and the desk's record change since the last brief. Cap changes() at the 20 highest-scoring coins (it runs analyze twice per coin). With rich cards, each attention coin becomes an embed field.
ideas.risk: More CPU per brief (two analyze runs per coin); COIN_TIMEOUT and the semaphore already bound it. The first brief has no 'since' and falls back to the 24h view.

ideas.title: Event and news guard for the coins you hold
ideas.pitch: 30 minutes before CPI I get one card: what's coming, what I hold, which desk buys could fill in the spike and which of my alerts sit within 2% of price. Headlines that mention INJ reach me without opening the news tab.
ideas.why: The calendar and coin-tagged news exist, but they only show in the brief's 'Today' list, the Events tab and agent answers. A spot holder's biggest overnight risks are macro prints and coin-specific news, and both are already parsed.
ideas.how: A loop in a small backend/app/guards.py (started in main.py, declared in jobs) every 5 min. (1) events.upcoming_events(hours=2, impact='high'): for each event entering the lead window (default 30 min) not yet sent (kv set in db.py), send one card with title, time, forecast/previous (already parsed), held coins and value (holdings watch context), the desk's waiting calls (desk.calls(status='waiting')) and armed price alerts within 2% of price. (2) events.headlines(symbol, hours=1) for held + watchlist coins (match_coins tagging already done): new URLs, deduped in a notified_news table, grouped by coin into one low-priority card per poll. Toggles and lead time in the Brief tab.
ideas.risk: News volume on a hot coin. Low priority plus the digest keeps it calm, with a per-coin daily cap. Forex Factory throttles frequent polling, but events.py already caches it for an hour.

readers.subsystem: portfolio (Binance account, journal, paper, grid bots, dip ladder, DCA, sell check, coach, PnL calendar)
readers.map:
binance_account.py: read-only key store (mode-600 file or env), permission check through apiRestrictions before every call (rechecked hourly), signed GETs for balances, myTrades, allOrders, wallet totals, futures fills and positions, and Simple Earn.
binance_import.py: imports spot fills (only {asset}USDT for spot-wallet coins, grid-bot pairs and listed pairs) and USD-M fills. It tags each fill manual, bot or unknown (override, then clientOrderId prefix, then tracked-grid match), rebuilds flat→position→flat round trips into the journal (closed manual trips only), and builds positions(): spot rows with average entry, Earn rows (no cost basis), futures, and bots kept apart. Also open_position_keys for the trade manager and real-vs-simulated grid fills.
journal.py: plan trades replayed on 1m candles (fills, targets, breakeven, R, MFE/MAE, stats, equity curve). Imported trades carry their fills' PnL and have no stop. postmortem.py writes reviews only for trades with a stop.
paper.py: a USDT spot wallet replayed from orders on 1m candles. Group logic gives a plan or ladder OCO-like stop and targets. The agent desk has a second instance of it.
gridbot.py: Binance Spot Grid replay (4 path points per 1m bar), saved bots, comparison with numbers copied from Binance. grid_planner.py: picks a range from zone edges, sets grid count and type, backtests 7/30/90 days.
dip_ladder.py: zone-based buy rungs, take profit and invalidation, and a walk-forward 90-day test. dca.py: lump sum vs weekly vs daily vs dips, backtest only.
sell_check.py: lost-support and at-resistance checks, on demand (agent, /api/sell-check) and as signal alerts. holdings_watch.py: keeps those alerts on the spot coins held. trade_manager.py: manages trades, including Binance holdings, and closes them when the position disappears.
coach.py: habits from closed manual spot round trips, on 1h candles. pnl_calendar.py: realized PnL per day at average cost from the fills.
Frontend: AccountPanel (Setup, Positions, PnL, Coach, Fills, Watch holdings), JournalPanel, PaperPanel, GridBotPanel (tracker, planner, real vs sim), DcaPanel, TradeManagerPanel (can pick a Binance position).

issues.title: Paper: after 'Sell all', a plan's stop later sells coins from a different buy
issues.detail: simulate_symbol only adds to gfills[group] when the selling order belongs to that group (around line 281), and the 'position closed' cancel (around line 289) needs `o.group`. PaperPanel's Holdings 'Sell all' (PaperPanel.tsx around line 196) places an ungrouped market sell, so it sells the plan's coins but group_held(p) still reports them. The plan's stop and targets stay pending. The next buy of that coin releases them (lines 254-256), and `have = min(book.held, group_held(p))` lets the old stop sell the new coins. I confirmed this with a replay in a scratch script: plan buy 2 @10 with stop 9, then Sell all, then a manual market buy of 3, then a dip to 8.9. The plan stop o2 filled 2.0 and only 1 coin remained. Fix: when a sell from outside group G takes coins, debit the groups that own them, oldest fill first, by adding negative entries to gfills. Cancel a group's sells once it holds nothing and has no pending buy. Have 'Sell all' cancel that coin's pending sells.

issues.title: Moving coins into Simple Earn closes managed Binance trades
issues.detail: A trade added in Live trades from a Binance holding has source_id 'holding:spot:INJ'. positions() builds manual.spot only from spot_balances (loop around line 717), and open_position_keys (around line 794) includes only those rows. Subscribing the INJ to Simple Earn (flexible or locked) therefore removes the key. trade_manager.sync_positions (trade_manager.py around line 392) then closes the trade at the last price and records 'the position is no longer open on Binance'. A spot remainder under $5 does the same. Fix: count holding:spot:{asset} as open when spot own_qty plus that asset's Earn qty is worth at least MIN_OPEN_VALUE. TradeManagerPanel's list of positions to pick from should include Earn too.

issues.title: Coins in Earn are not watched, and their fills may never be imported
issues.detail: HoldingsWatch.coins reads only positions['manual']['spot'], so INJ locked in Earn never gets the lost_support or at_resistance alerts. binance_import._spot_symbols adds only f"{a}USDT" for assets in the spot balances. A coin that sits fully in Earn before the first import never has its fills imported, so it has no average entry in Positions, the brief or the agent facts. FDUSD- or USDC-quoted buys of a held coin are also skipped unless the user types the pair. Fix: add manual.earn assets to both lists, and also try {asset}USDC and {asset}FDUSD. Unknown pairs already go to _invalid through code -1121.

issues.title: Average entry mixes fills quoted in different assets
issues.detail: positions() selects fills by base asset only: `mine = [f for f in fills if f.market == 'spot' and split_symbol(f.symbol)[0] == asset]` (around line 722). average_entry then averages them as if all were USD. Fills of INJBTC or INJBNB added under 'Other spot pairs' at about 0.0003 get averaged with INJUSDT fills at about 20, which corrupts avg_entry and unrealized_pnl, and those feed the brief and the agent's 'You hold… +x%'. pnl_calendar already guards against this with USD_QUOTES. Fix: keep only USD-stablecoin quotes in average_entry, or convert each fill to USD at its fill time using the quote's USDT close from the candle cache.

issues.title: Fees paid in BNB are left out of every PnL figure
issues.detail: _fee() returns (0, 0, True) for a commission in BNB, and build_round_trips, average_entry, pnl_calendar.daily_pnl and coach only add a note. Most Binance users pay fees in BNB for the 25% discount. For them, journal realized_pnl, every PnL-calendar day, the coach's 'Fees take a big share' check and the win/loss split are all too high. Fix: value BNB (and any other) commission at the fill time with the BNBUSDT 1h close (market.get_range, cached per hour), and pass a {hour: price} map into the pure functions. Keep the note only when no price is available.

issues.title: The on-demand sell check counts the candle that is still open
issues.detail: sell_scan uses market.get_klines, which returns the forming bar (market_data._binance_cached returns merged[-total:] including the open bar), for both the chart timeframe and the daily. _lost's 'closed below it 2 times' can therefore be 1 close plus the current price, and _rejection reads the wick of an unfinished candle. signal_alerts calls alert_check on closed_only candles (signal_alerts.py around lines 472 and 549), so the agent's 'what should I sell?' and POST /api/sell-check can disagree with the alert that fires later. Fix: apply kimi_service.closed_only(candles, interval) to both frames in sell_scan, and mention a provisional break on the live candle separately.

issues.title: 'What should I sell or trim?' checks the watchlist, not what is held
issues.detail: Around line 751: `sell_symbols = [symbol] if one_coin else (req.watchlist or DEFAULT_WATCHLIST)`. _positions(binance) is fetched in the same gather (line 760), so it cannot feed the coin list. With a read-only key the question should cover the coins held (spot and Earn) and give each one's average entry and PnL. The 'Alert me when these coins need selling' button then arms alerts on watchlist coins rather than holdings. Fix: await positions first (cached 30 s) and use holdings worth $10 or more, falling back to the watchlist.

issues.title: Imported Binance trades can never be given a stop, so real trades get no R or post-mortem
issues.detail: JournalPatch (around line 190) accepts only notes, tags, setup, cancel and close, and update() refuses close and cancel for imported entries. The docstrings say R works 'unless the user gives one' / 'R only when the user gave a stop', but there is no API or UI to give one. As a result the trades with real money in them never get R statistics, postmortem.generate refuses them ('imported without a stop', postmortem.py around line 651), and the weekly review lists them only as dollar PnL. Fix: allow stop and targets in JournalPatch for imported entries (checked against direction), and keep them through sync_imported the way notes, tags and setup are kept.

issues.title: Grid bots stop working after about 395 days, and every refresh replays the whole history
issues.detail: resolve_start raises 'The runtime is too long' when (now - start)//60 + 1 > MAX_RANGE_BARS (570,000 one-minute bars, about 395.8 days). A saved bot keeps its start_time, so once it is older every result() call fails. The card errors, and positions().tracked and the import's bot matching quietly lose the bot. Before that point, each 1m refresh reloads and replays every minute since the start (around 1M path points at 6 months). Fix: save a checkpoint of the replay state (gap line, base, quote, grid profit, matched count, daily rows) per bot at each UTC day and continue from the latest one.

issues.title: The 20,000-fill cap silently rewrites history
issues.detail: _trim() keeps only the newest MAX_FILLS = 20,000 fills, and bot and unknown fills count toward that. _reclassify then rebuilds round trips without the dropped buys. journal.sync_imported deletes every imported entry that is no longer produced (`if ext not in want and old.source == 'binance'`), so closed real trades disappear from the journal and stats. The PnL calendar loses old days and average entries shift. An active account, or one where an API bot trades on the spot wallet, reaches the cap. Fix: store fills in SQLite (db.py) without the cap, or at least never remove a closed imported journal entry because its fills were trimmed.

issues.title: Position sizing shows leverage in spot-only mode
issues.detail: sizePlan sets leverage = notional / account and only warns above maxLeverage (default 10). With Spot only on, the plan card (AgentPanel.tsx around line 319) still prints 'needs 3.2x' and the Copy order text adds 'Lev 3.2x'. A spot buy can't exceed the cash available, so the size shown can't actually be placed. Fix: in spot mode, cap qty at free cash (the account setting, or the Binance stablecoin balance when a key exists), show the risk % that results ('capped by cash: 0.6% risk'), and drop the leverage wording.

issues.title: Partial sells are invisible to the journal and the coach
issues.detail: build_round_trips closes a spot trip only when the position falls below 0.5% of its peak (DUST), and coach.trades_from keeps only closed trips. A holder who scales into INJ and sells 30% at resistance has one trip that never closes: no journal entry, no 'sold early' check, nothing for the coach to see. pnl_calendar.daily_pnl already realizes each sell at average cost, so the same running average could produce per-sell events for the coach and the journal.

issues.title: Paper: a cancelled plan buy leaves its stop and targets pending
issues.detail: When a plan's limit buy is cancelled before it fills, its stop and targets are reached with nothing held. They go into `waiting` and stay pending as 'waiting for coins to sell' indefinitely. The cancel at line 289 only runs after a sell has filled. Fix: once every buy in a group is cancelled or unfilled and group_held is 0, cancel the group's pending sells with reason 'plan buy cancelled'.

issues.title: Positions have no totals, and Earn is shown separately from spot
issues.detail: PositionsView shows spot rows (value and unrealized PnL each) with no sum. Earn has its own total, and nothing adds up spot, Earn, stablecoins, futures uPnL and the Trading Bots wallet. An asset held both in spot and in Earn appears as two unrelated rows, and the Earn row has no average entry or PnL even when its buys were imported, because average_entry is applied only up to the spot qty (from_fills_qty = min(tracked, own)).

issues.title: The grid planner's backtest has look-ahead bias
issues.detail: backtest_grid replays today's planned range over the last 7, 30 or 90 days. That range was chosen from zones and the 30-day low and high formed inside the same window, so time in range and APR look better than a forward test would. The notes mention that a range can break, not this selection bias. dip_ladder.backtest_ladder already shows how to do it walk-forward (see the ideas).

ideas.title: Portfolio cockpit: total account value over time, allocation and 'did trading beat holding'
ideas.pitch: One number for everything I own (spot, Earn, stablecoins and bots), a curve of it over time, how concentrated I am in INJ, and whether my trading beat simply holding.
ideas.why: Positions today are four separate lists with no total. Nothing records account value over time, so the owner can't tell whether the account is growing, what his drawdown is, or whether active trading beats holding. Concentration risk (for example INJ at 45%) is never mentioned. This would also become the baseline every other money feature reports against.
ideas.how: New backend/app/portfolio.py. snapshot(positions) merges manual.spot and manual.earn per asset (qty, value, and cost basis from binance_import.average_entry applied to spot plus Earn qty), stablecoins, futures uPnL and the Trading Bots wallet (positions['bots']['wallet']['usdt']) into a total. Storage: db.migrate('portfolio', ['CREATE TABLE portfolio_snapshots (ts INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, total REAL, stables REAL, bots REAL, assets TEXT)']). A job registered with jobs.declare('portfolio_snapshot', ...) runs hourly, keeping hourly rows for 14 days and daily rows after that. Backfill 30 days on the first run from GET /sapi/v1/accountSnapshot?type=SPOT (USER_DATA, readable with a read-only key, daily balances), priced with daily closes from the candle store. Metrics: change over 24h, 7d and 30d; max drawdown; allocation % with a flag for any non-BTC coin above 35%; 'vs HODL' (the coin quantities held N days ago at today's prices, compared with today's total); 'vs BTC'. API: GET /api/portfolio and /api/portfolio/history?days=. Frontend: a new first tab 'Overview' in AccountPanel.tsx with the total, change chips, an allocation bar and a value curve (generalize EquityCurve.tsx to {time, value}). brief.holdings_lines gains 'Account $X (+2.1% since last brief)', and agent.portfolio_facts gains the total and allocation.
ideas.risk: Deposits and withdrawals look like gains or losses until flows are imported (sapi capital deposit and withdraw history). Mark a jump in stablecoins with no matching fill as a flow and say so. accountSnapshot has request weight 2400, so call it at most once a day.

ideas.title: An exit plan for each coin held: where to trim, how much, and where the idea is wrong, armed as alerts
ideas.pitch: For every coin I hold: a scale-out ladder at the next resistances sized from my cost basis, plus the level where the thesis breaks, sent to Discord as each level is hit.
ideas.why: sell_check only reacts once a coin is already at resistance or has lost support. It runs on the watchlist and never says how much to sell. A spot holder grows the account by taking profit on purpose, and selling winners early is the coach's main warning, which a pre-committed scale-out plan addresses directly.
ideas.how: New backend/app/exit_plan.py. For a holding (positions: qty including Earn, avg_entry), load closed 4h and 1d candles and get zones with sell_check._zones (S/R with 2+ touches plus supply/demand) and mark_confluence for the daily. Trim rungs: the next 2-4 resistance or supply zones above price, at least 1 ATR apart, each at the zone's lower edge (as dip_ladder picks its take profit), capped at 35% above price with ATR steps as the fallback. Size profiles: 'take my cost out' (rung 1 sells cost/price coins, the rest is house money) and 'quarters' (25/25/25 with a 25% runner). Invalidation: a lost D1 support or demand (sell_check._lost on daily closes), trailed up to new higher lows with trade_manager's trailing logic. Output per rung: price, coins, USDT, % of position, and PnL against the average entry. 'Arm' creates alerts.py cross alerts with notes ('Trim 25% INJ ≈ $310'); the holdings watch already covers lost support. A rung counts as done when an imported manual sell lands within 0.5% of it, and the plan is rebuilt weekly. API: POST /api/exit-plan {symbol, profile} and GET /api/exit-plans. UI: an 'Exit plan' button on each Positions row that draws the rungs (HorizontalLineOverlay, as in ladder_overlays) with an Arm button. The agent answers 'how should I take profit on INJ?' with this plan.
ideas.risk: In a downtrend the zones above can be far away and won't fill soon, so cap their distance and say when a rung is unlikely to fill. It stays advice only; the read-only key can't place orders.

ideas.title: Correct cost basis: Convert trades, USDC/FDUSD pairs, BNB fees and Earn rewards
ideas.pitch: My average entry and PnL should match reality even when I bought with Convert, paid in FDUSD, paid fees in BNB or earned coins in Earn.
ideas.why: Every money feature (Positions, brief, agent 'you are +8%', coach, PnL calendar, exit plans) depends on cost basis. Today it silently leaves out Convert trades (they are not in myTrades), non-USDT pairs of held coins, BNB fees and Earn yield, so profits are overstated and many coins show 'no buys imported'.
ideas.how: In binance_import._spot_symbols, try {asset}USDT, {asset}USDC and {asset}FDUSD for every spot and Earn asset (bad pairs are already cached in _invalid through -1121). Add BinanceAccount.convert_trades(start_ms, end_ms) → GET /sapi/v1/convert/tradeFlow in 30-day windows. Turn each row into an AccountFill (key 'convert:<orderId>', a {coin}USDT buy or sell, price = ratio, kind manual, reason 'Binance Convert'). Pass a {hour: BNBUSDT close} map, built in run() from market.get_range, into _fee, average_entry and pnl_calendar.daily_pnl so BNB commissions come off. Read Simple Earn rewards (GET /sapi/v1/simple-earn/flexible/history/rewardsRecord and the locked equivalent) as zero-cost lots, with an 'earn' column per day in the PnL calendar. Tests with fixtures in tests/test_binance_import.py.
ideas.risk: Convert and rewards endpoints have heavy per-account weights (tradeFlow is 3000), so run them on manual imports or once a day only. Check the response field names against a recorded live payload.

ideas.title: Review real trades: suggested stops and automatic setup tags, so imported trades get R, stats and post-mortems
ideas.pitch: Show me which of my own Binance trades, by setup, actually make money, with a post-mortem on each, not just the agent's paper plans.
ideas.why: Imported trades are the real-money record, yet they have no stop, so they get no R, no post-mortem and only one setup label ('Binance spot'). Journal → Stats by setup is meaningless for them, and the weekly review leaves them out of the R numbers.
ideas.how: Add stop and targets to journal.JournalPatch for imported entries, and keep them through sync_imported the way notes and tags are kept. New backend/app/trade_context.py: for each imported trip, load 1h and 4h candles before opened_at (coach._candles already fetches this range). Use ta_agent.cluster_levels, supply_demand_zones and atr on candles up to opened_at only (no look-ahead) to suggest a stop 0.25 ATR below the support or demand zone holding the entry, the trade_plan.py rule. Tag the setup as one of 'H4 demand', 'H4 support', 'breakout above resistance', 'after a pump' (coach.CHASE_PCT), 'Kimi B+ within 3 bars' (kimi_service, cached) or 'inside a desk zone' (coach._desk_zones). JournalPanel shows 'Set stop (suggested 18.42)' on imported rows. Once a stop is set, journal_stats by_setup, postmortem.generate and weekly_review include the trade. Mark inferred stops as 'estimated' in the stats.
ideas.risk: An inferred stop is a reconstruction, not the trader's actual plan: label it and let the user edit it. Keep these trades out of the desk's learning.

ideas.title: Grid bot health checks and a suggested new range, sent to Discord
ideas.pitch: Tell me when my INJ grid is idle below its range, is holding a loss, or no longer beats holding the coin, and suggest a better range.
ideas.why: Bots are tracked but nothing watches them. A grid that drops below its range quietly turns into a losing coin position, and today only a yellow line in the panel says so. Binance has no Spot Grid API, so the tracked settings are the only way to watch a bot.
ideas.how: New backend/app/grid_health.py, registered with jobs.declare('grid_health', every 5 min), looping over gridbots.list() and calling result(). Rules, each sent once per change of state through alerts.notify and record (state kept in JSON with read_store/write_store, like holdings_watch): out of range for more than 2h; position_pct under 10 with floating_pnl < -grid_profit ('floating −$42 vs grid +$11'); no matched trades in 24h while in range (grids too wide); the simulated TP or SL reached; runtime over 360 days (the replay limit). Add hold_return_pct and vs_usdt to GridBotResult; simulate already has p0 (start price) and last_price. After 24h out of range, run grid_planner.plan_grid and backtest_grid on the current and the suggested range over 7 days ('INJ grid idle 31h below 18.20; 16.90–20.40 with 38 grids earned +2.1% vs 0.0% over 7 days'). BotCard in GridBotPanel.tsx gets health chips and an on/off per bot.
ideas.risk: These are simulated bot states, not Binance's real ones, so messages should say 'your tracked settings'. Use hysteresis so a price hovering at the edge doesn't send repeated alerts.

ideas.title: DCA plan with weekly Discord reminders and a check of what was actually bought
ideas.pitch: Every Monday: 'DCA day: buy $75 of INJ (1.5× because price is in D1 demand)'. Then the app checks whether I actually bought.
ideas.why: dca.py is a one-off backtest. A spot holder who accumulates INJ benefits most from a written rule that buys more at demand zones and less at resistance, with reminders and a check that he followed it.
ideas.how: Add a 'smart' strategy to dca.py: the weekly base amount times 1.5× inside a 1d support or demand zone (detectors run on candles known that day, walk-forward as in dip_ladder.backtest_ladder), 2× when 30%+ below the 90-day high, 0.5× at resistance with RSI hot (sell_check._overhead), and unspent money carried forward. New backend/app/dca_plans.py: saved plans {symbol, weekly_usdt, weekday, time, tz, rules} via read_store/write_store, timed like brief.weekly_due_slot, messages through alerts.notify. Adherence: manual Binance buys of that coin within 48h of each slot are marked done or missed, and the plan's average cost is compared with the coin's average price. API: /api/dca/plans CRUD. DcaPanel gets 'Make this my plan' and the adherence history.
ideas.risk: The multipliers can read like buy signals. Cap them at 2× and set a monthly limit.

ideas.title: Coach individual sells: trims, sells below cost, and adding to losers
ideas.pitch: Coach the way I actually trade, scaling in and trimming, not only trades that end with zero coins.
ideas.why: The coach only sees flat-to-flat round trips (issue above), so most of a holder's decisions, the trims and the adds, are never analyzed.
ideas.how: Refactor the average-cost loop in pnl_calendar.daily_pnl into an iterator that yields (fill, avg_cost, realized, position_after) per fill, and use it in coach.py over binance.fills(kind='manual', market='spot'). New findings: trims_early (sells that leave 20% or more of the position, how often price rose 5% within 7 days, and how much was left on the table); sold_below_cost (sells under the average cost, and price 14 days later); sells into strength vs weakness (sell_check._overhead and _lost on 4h candles known at the time) and how each did; averaging down (buys below the current average cost) vs adding above it. Reuse CoachService._candles; keep the MIN_TRADES threshold per finding.
ideas.risk: Small samples; each finding must state how many sells it rests on, as the existing ones do.

ideas.title: Position sizing from real balances, capped for spot, with a concentration warning
ideas.pitch: Size plans from my real USDT, never more than I can actually buy, and warn me when one buy would make a coin half my account.
ideas.why: Sizing uses a hand-typed account size, shows leverage to a spot-only trader, and ignores what is already held, so a plan card can suggest a buy that is impossible or badly over-concentrated.
ideas.how: lib/sizing.ts: add a spotOnly flag (from the AgentPanel spotOnly state). qty = min(risk-based qty, freeCash/(entry*(1+fee))), and return effectiveRiskPct and a capped flag. Free cash = manual.cash USDT/USDC/FDUSD from fetchAccountPositions when a key exists, else the account setting. SettingsDialog gets 'Use my Binance balance', which fills the account size from the portfolio total. Concentration check: (current value of the coin including Earn + new notional) / total above 35% gives the warning 'INJ would be 48% of your account'. The plan card and Copy order use the capped size.
ideas.risk: An extra positions call per plan card; the result is already cached for 30 s server-side, so reuse one fetch per session.

ideas.title: Walk-forward test of the grid planner itself
ideas.pitch: Before I trust the planner on INJ: how would its ranges have done if it had picked a new one every week without seeing the future?
ideas.why: The current backtest replays today's range over the past, and that range was chosen from that same past, so the results look better than they should. A walk-forward test shows whether the planner's way of choosing a range works on this coin.
ideas.how: grid_planner.walkforward_grid(svc, symbol, days=90, hold_days=7): at each weekly point t, build_plan on the planning timeframe's candles up to t, then gridbot.simulate on the next 7 days of 1m bars (start_time=t, end_time=t+7d); chain the weeks. Report per week the APR, time in range, whether the range broke, and total against holding (same structure as dip_ladder.backtest_ladder). POST /api/gridbot/walkforward; GridBotPanel's BacktestView shows it beside the plain test as 'If you had used the planner every week'.
ideas.risk: Needs 90 days of 1m candles (cached in SQLite after the first run) plus about 13 plans and simulations, a few seconds. Run it in asyncio.to_thread like the existing backtest.

ideas.title: A brake after losing streaks, big daily losses or revenge buys
ideas.pitch: If I'm down 3% today, or I re-buy a coin right after selling it at a loss, ping me once and suggest waiting for the next 4h close.
ideas.why: Avoiding big mistakes matters as much as finding setups. The data is already there (imported fills, daily PnL, holdings), but nothing reacts to it while it happens.
ideas.how: After each BinanceImportService.run (auto-import every 5-60 min), compute today's and this week's realized PnL with pnl_calendar.daily_pnl as a % of the portfolio total (from the cockpit idea, or the positions total). Also flag 3 losing sells in 24h, and a buy of the same coin within 2h of a losing sell. Thresholds live in a small JSON store (default −3% per day). Send one Discord message per day through alerts.notify and record it, show a banner on plan cards for the next N hours (served from GET /api/guard), and add a coach finding 'revenge_buys' with the historical results of those re-buys.
ideas.risk: It can feel like nagging: once a day at most, easy to switch off, thresholds the user sets.

readers.map:
page.tsx stacks MarketHeader (CoinGecko, F&G and futures metrics plus SessionClock, polled every 30 s) on top of ChartWorkspace.
ChartWorkspace.tsx (1,500 lines) owns all UI state in localStorage through usePersistentState: grid cells (1/2/4), named watchlists, indicators, layer visibility, dock, drawings per symbol, AI overlays per symbol:tf, pins and chats. It also holds undo/redo (useUndo, which merges a drag into one step), the full keyboard map, the streaming agent (runAnalysis), screenshot reading, the top-down walk, replay and QuickPrompt. It builds the 16 dock tabs: 4 inline plus the 12 EXTRA_PANELS from dockPanels.tsx.
ChartCell.tsx wraps one AgenticChart per grid cell. Inactive cells read their saved overlays, pins and drawings read-only. The active cell gets the tool, drawings and callbacks.
AgenticChart.tsx is a Lightweight Charts v4 engine. It loads 500 bars (the IndexedDB cache plus a delta fetch, then /ws/klines; ratios and indexes are polled). Indicators are computed client-side, with sub-panes faked through scaleMargins. It runs about 12 series primitives (BoxZone, LabeledRay, TrendLine, DrawingLayer, Kimi, Sessions, Heatmap, VolumeProfile, EventLines, Countdown, AxisMask) that share one LabelRegistry so labels don't collide. Its own pointer handling covers taps, moving a whole drawing, dragging alert lines and the right-click ask/alert/draw menu.
lib/layers.ts composeOverlays merges agent overlays, pinned answers, overlay sets from dock tabs (onChartOverlays keys, saved in ac:panel-overlays), alert overlays and the best higher-timeframe zone above and below price. LayersPanel shows an eye toggle for each of the 29 LayerIds, plus lists of AI levels, pins and drawings to delete.
Dock.tsx is an icon rail with one resizable panel. A tab mounts the first time it opens and then stays mounted while hidden. On mobile the panel goes full-screen and a horizontally scrolling bottom nav holds 18 entries.
Watchlist.tsx: named lists, 5 sorts, drag to reorder, a 10 s ticker poll, a 2-minute zone scan, 48 h sparklines, and a right-click menu with Open in chart N, Copy to list and Remove.
DrawingToolbar.tsx has 8 tools plus undo/redo, magnet, lock, alert and delete. DrawingStyleBar floats over a selected drawing.
ScannerPanel, DeskPanel and StatusPanel each poll their own endpoint every 30 s. Scanner and Desk draw the selected setup or call on its chart through onChartOverlays.
SettingsDialog covers chart, time and multi-chart toggles, the AI model, position sizing, the Binance key and a JSON backup of every ac:* localStorage key.

issues.title: Agent desk events reach the browser and are dropped: no toast, sound or live refresh
issues.detail: backend/app/agent_desk.py _notify() calls self.alerts.broadcast({"type":"desk","call":...}) at line 488 for every new call, fill and result. The /ws/alerts onmessage handler in useAlerts.ts (around lines 216-244) only handles snapshot, signal_snapshot, fired, signal_fired, trade_advice and history, so the 'desk' message is ignored. The only trace is a row in Alerts → History. So when the desk calls INJ 4H or a buy fills, nothing appears in the app (no toast, no beep(), no desktop Notification), and DeskPanel keeps showing stale data for up to 30 s (REFRESH_MS). Fix: add a msg.type === 'desk' branch that calls a new onDesk callback. ChartWorkspace pushes a MessageToast ('Desk 4H call: INJ buy 24.10–24.60 · 62%') and dispatches a window event that DeskPanel listens for to call load() at once. Skip shadow (watched) calls, as the backend already does.

issues.title: 'Since you last looked' never shows if the tab stays open
issues.detail: The effect runs only when symbol or interval change. While mounted, setInterval(writeSeen, 120000) keeps stamping ac:seen:SYM:TF regardless of document.visibilityState. Background tabs and a waking laptop still fire that timer. Concrete path: leave INJ 4h open in a background tab overnight, come back in the morning. 'seen' is minutes old and the effect never re-runs, so the card that should cover the night never appears. It only works after a reload or a coin switch. Fix: only call writeSeen while document.visibilityState === 'visible'. On visibilitychange to visible, re-read prev and, if now − prev ≥ MIN_AWAY_S, POST /api/changes again. Also write 'seen' only after the request succeeds, so a backend outage doesn't use up the card.

issues.title: Dock rail clips the last tabs (Status, Account) on short laptop screens
issues.detail: The rail <nav className="flex w-11 shrink-0 flex-col ... py-2"> has 16 buttons at h-9 with gap-0.5. That needs 16×36 + 15×2 + 16 = 622 px with no overflow-y handling, under MarketHeader (h-9) and ChartHeader (h-11), and the page root is overflow-hidden. Any viewport under about 702 px tall clips the bottom icons. That includes a 1366×768 laptop, whose Chrome viewport is about 650 px. The Status tab, the one with the 'something is broken' badge, is last and is the first to vanish. Fix: overflow-y-auto scrollbar-none on the rail, plus an overflow '⋯' button that lists the hidden tabs, or group the rarely used tabs (DCA, Grid bots, Backtest, Account, Status) under a 'More' entry.

issues.title: Saves fail silently once localStorage fills up
issues.detail: writeStored() and the write effect in usePersistentState both swallow quota errors ('ignore quota / privacy errors'). What lives in localStorage grows without bound: ac:chats keeps 50 sessions × up to 40 AgentMessages, each carrying overlays, facts, setups (each with its own overlays), steps and scan rows; ac:overlays:SYM:TF is written for every chart the agent ever drew on and never pruned; and ac:panel-overlays is kept too. Once the roughly 5 MB origin quota is hit, new drawings, alerts settings and watchlist edits look saved in memory but are lost on reload, with no warning. Fix: on QuotaExceededError, show a one-time banner, prune ac:overlays:* keys untouched for 30 days and trim chat sessions to text only (drop facts and setups). Better: move chats to IndexedDB, which candleCache.ts already uses, or to the backend SQLite.

issues.title: Each live tick or drag pointermove re-renders the whole workspace and every mounted dock tab
issues.detail: Nothing is memoized (no React.memo anywhere in components/). The tabs array and its render closures are rebuilt on every render, and Dock.tsx calls t.render() for every tab ever opened, hidden ones included. Two paths fire constantly. (1) AgenticChart.emitFeed → onFeed → ChartWorkspace setFeed on every Binance kline push for the active chart, and dockProps.price goes to every EXTRA_PANEL. (2) Dragging a drawing calls onDrawingsChange on every pointermove → changeDrawings → record() (JSON.stringify of the whole drawings array twice) → setDrawings → a localStorage write plus a SYNC_EVENT → a full re-render of AgentPanel (40 rich messages), AlertsPanel (1,600 lines), JournalPanel and so on. Hidden tabs also keep polling: Watchlist tickers every 10 s, its scan every 2 min, N kline sparklines every 5 min; Desk makes 4 requests every 30 s; Status polls every 30 s. Only the heatmap checks document.hidden. Fix: put the feed in a small store read through useSyncExternalStore by ChartHeader and the panels that need price; wrap each dock tab in a memoized component; pass an 'active' flag so panels pause polling (usePolled key=null); keep drag state local and commit once on pointerup.

issues.title: Right-click 'Alert me at X' and 'Draw a line at X' go through the LLM
issues.detail: The ask menu (lines 1517-1535) sends all three entries to onAskAgent(prompt), which is runAnalysis. Setting an alert at a known price therefore costs a full agent round trip: rule parser or qwen2.5:7b on the 3070 Ti, several seconds. It can misparse the price, adds a user and an agent message to the chat, and 'Draw a line' becomes a custom_* AI overlay rather than a user drawing you can drag and style. Fix: add onQuickAlert(price) and onQuickLine(price) props. ChartWorkspace calls addAlerts([{kind:'cross', price, price_low:null, price_high:null, label:`Line ${formatPrice(price)}`}], symbol) and changeDrawings([...drawings, {type:'hray', points:[{time, price}], ...}]) directly, with undoNote feedback. Only 'Ask the agent about X' stays an agent prompt.

issues.title: Drawings can only be moved whole: no endpoint or corner editing
issues.detail: drawOne() draws handle circles on a selected drawing, but nothing hit-tests them. AgenticChart's pointer 'down' handler (line ~1350) always sets dragRef = {id, start, orig: d.points}, and 'move' shifts every point by the same offset. So you cannot fix one end of a trendline, resize a rectangle zone, re-anchor a fib or adjust one leg of an XABCD without deleting and redrawing it. HIT_PX = 6 is also too small for touch on mobile. Fix: add pickHandle(x, y) for the selected drawing that returns {id, index}, move only points[index] in 'move' (snapped to OHLC with magnet via toPoint), and use a hit radius of 14 when e.pointerType === 'touch'.

issues.title: [ / ] and Alt+↑/↓ step through a different order than the watchlist shows
issues.detail: stepWatchlist() (line ~865) walks `watchlist`, which is currentList.symbols in manual order. Watchlist.tsx renders `ordered`, sorted by 24h change, nearest zone, unusual volume or name when sort ≠ 'manual'. With 'Nearest zone' selected, pressing ] jumps to a coin far down or up the visible list, which defeats sorting by zone and then flicking through. Fix: lift the sorted order up (Watchlist reports it through an onOrder(symbols) callback, or move the sort into a shared helper) and step through that.

issues.title: Changing the grid can swap out the chart you were looking at
issues.detail: active = Math.min(storedActive, gridMode === 1 ? 3 : gridMode − 1). Path: Watchlist → right-click → 'Open in chart 3' (grid becomes 4, active 2) → G (single chart, still cell 2) → G again (two charts). Active is clamped to 1, so the coin you were on disappears, the header and timeframe now drive cell 1, and drawing or agent actions go to another coin. Fix: when the grid shrinks below the active index, copy the active cell into the last visible slot (or slot 0) and setActive to that index, instead of clamping only in render.

issues.title: Floating bars sit over the whole grid, not the active chart, and some overlap
issues.detail: DrawingStyleBar (top-2 centre), the pickedLevel bar (top-2 centre), the error banner, SinceLastLooked (right-3 top-2, w-80), QuickPrompt (bottom-9 centre) and the undo note (bottom-10 centre) are all positioned in <main>, not in the active ChartCell. In a 2- or 4-chart grid they float over the middle seam or over another coin's chart. For example, the 'Since you last looked at INJ' card lands on the top-right cell while INJ is top-left. The undo note at bottom-10 also covers the QuickPrompt input at bottom-9 for 1.8 s after every undo, 'Alert set' or snapshot. Fix: render these inside ChartCell when active (it is already a positioned container), and move the undo note above the prompt.

issues.title: The desk's selected call stays drawn on its chart after the panel closes and across reloads
