issues.detail: The comment says 'cleared when another is picked or the panel closes', but Dock never unmounts tabs, so the unmount cleanup only runs on a page unload. onChartOverlays writes to ac:panel-overlays, which is persisted, so the 'desk:selected' box, TP and stop reappear on that coin after a reload, with nothing to say where they came from (they sit in the 'Other panels' layer). The same applies to the Scanner's 'scanner' key. Also, the Minimum confidence range input calls save() on every step while dragging, which is up to 14 PUTs, and each merges a stale `s`. Two timeframe checkboxes clicked quickly can lose the first change. Fix: give panel overlays an owner and an expiry (or keep them out of storage), label them ('Desk call · INJ 4H'), save the slider on pointerup, and send patches computed from the latest state.

issues.title: Hidden shortcuts and small inconsistencies
issues.detail: Rail buttons use title={t.label}, so the 13 tab hotkeys (V, Q, J, Y, X, C, O, E, B, U, W, A, L) are only discoverable through '?'. Account and Status have no hotkey. ChartHeader uses the Maximize2 icon for 'Fit chart', which reads as 'maximize'. Fired-alert toasts in AlertToasts.tsx cannot be clicked to open the coin, so you navigate to SOL yourself. SettingsDialog shows 'Highest leverage' to a spot-only user (SPOT_ONLY_KEY defaults to true) and files 'Find levels automatically' under 'Several charts'. The mobile DrawingToolbar gets onLock={setLocked} without the desktop reset of the tool and selection. Fix: put the hotkey in each rail title (add hotkey to DockTab), make toasts clickable (pickSymbol(alert.symbol)), hide leverage when spot-only, and share one onLock handler.

ideas.title: Desk on the chart, live
ideas.pitch: When the desk calls INJ on the 4H I get a toast right away, its buy zone, take-profit and stop are already on my INJ chart, and a small chip says 'Desk 4H · waiting to buy · 62%'. I no longer have to open the Desk tab to find out what my own agent is doing.
ideas.why: Today the desk's running calls are drawn only for the one call selected in DeskPanel, and its WS events are dropped (see issues). The desk is the newest and most 'agentic' feature, but the chart ignores it. This makes the chart the place where the desk's opinions live.
ideas.how: (1) hooks/useAlerts.ts: handle msg.type==='desk' and expose an onDesk callback. ChartWorkspace turns it into a MessageToast with an action that calls pickSymbol(call.symbol, call.interval) and openDockPanel('desk'), and dispatches 'ac:desk-changed'. (2) New hooks/useDeskCalls.ts calls fetchDeskCalls('active', signal, 50) with a new symbol param (/api/desk/calls already accepts symbol=). It refetches on symbol change and on 'ac:desk-changed', then calls onChartOverlays('desk:active', symbol, calls.filter(c => !c.shadow).flatMap(deskOverlays)). (3) lib/layers.ts: add LayerId 'desk' ('Desk calls', group 'Chart agent') and map panelLayer('desk') to 'desk', so the eye toggle works. (4) AgenticChart chip row (where the Session and Heatmap chips are) gets 'Desk 4H · Waiting to buy · 62%', which opens the Desk tab with that call selected (CustomEvent detail {callId}; DeskPanel calls select()). (5) DeskPanel listens for 'ac:desk-changed' and calls load() at once.
ideas.risk: Clutter on busy charts. The layer toggle and leaving out shadow calls cover it. Deduplicate with the 'desk:selected' set by call id, since composeOverlays already dedupes by id.

ideas.title: Spot position tool (entry, invalidation, take-profit) with one-click paper, journal and alert
ideas.pitch: I drag an entry and an invalidation on INJ and get a green and red R:R box: '+8.1% / −3.4% · 2.4R · 41 INJ at 1% risk after fees'. From the box I paper-buy it, log it, or set a 5m-confirmation alert on the zone.
ideas.why: The building blocks already exist (sizePlan in lib/sizing.ts, planToPaperOrders and placePaperOrders in lib/paper.ts, planToJournalEntry and createJournalEntry, addTrigger, alertFromDrawing), but they are only reachable from agent plan cards. A spot trader plans most trades by hand. This turns his own drawing into a plan in about 3 seconds, long-only to match his spot-only trading.
ideas.how: lib/types.ts: add DrawingType 'position' with TOOL_POINTS 2 (entry, then stop; the take-profit defaults to 2R and is a third point that can be dragged). DrawingLayerPrimitive: add drawPosition(), a green box from entry to TP and a red box from entry to stop, with a label from a TradePlan built out of the points through sizePlan(plan, ac:sizing) including feePct. A stop above the entry draws grey with 'invalid for spot'. Hit-testing reuses the rect logic. DrawingToolbar: a new tool button using a free key (e.g. Z). DrawingStyleBar: when d.type==='position', show buttons for Paper buy (placePaperOrders(planToPaperOrders(plan, symbol, sized.qty))), Log to journal, Alert at entry (addAlerts cross) and '5m confirmation' (addTrigger with zone source 'fixed', using entry and stop as the zone). This works best together with handle editing (next idea).
ideas.risk: Users may expect the box to update live like TradingView's, showing hit or not. Leave that out of v1, or mark TP and stop as hit with mapperRef bars after the anchor time.

ideas.title: Command palette on Ctrl+K: coins, timeframes, tabs, indicators, layouts and the agent
ideas.pitch: Ctrl+K and typing 'inj 4h' jumps straight there, 'kimi' toggles Kimi, 'desk' opens the desk, 'layout swing' loads my swing layout, and anything else becomes 'Ask the agent: …'. One box finds everything.
ideas.why: The app now has 16 tabs, 17 indicators, 13 tab hotkeys, saved layouts and a right-click menu, and most of it is discoverable only through '?', tooltips or hover. Ctrl+K currently opens SymbolSearch, which handles symbols only. A palette is the cheapest way to make a large feature set fast and findable, and each result can show its hotkey so people learn the shortcuts.
ideas.how: Turn components/SymbolSearch.tsx into CommandPalette.tsx (keeping the symbol-only mode for the 'watchlist' and 'compare' callers). Sources, ranked by prefix match: (a) a symbol plus an optional timeframe token parsed against TIMEFRAMES ('inj 4h', 'eth/btc d') → pickSymbol(sym, tf); (b) recent symbols from a new ac:recent list (push in ChartWorkspace.pickSymbol and setSymbol); (c) actions from a small registry built in ChartWorkspace: every DockTab (id, label, icon, hotkey from EXTRA_PANELS), the indicator toggles (export the list ChartHeader renders as MenuToggle into lib/indicatorsMenu.ts), layouts (WORKSPACES_KEY, applyWorkspace), settings toggles (log scale, grid, countdown, crosshair sync), 'Replay', 'Snapshot', 'Run desk 1H/4H/1D' (runDesk), 'Scan market 4h'; (d) a last row 'Ask the agent: <text>' → askAgent. For the top 8 symbol rows, show price and 24h change from one fetchTickers call.
ideas.risk: It overlaps with the existing S, Space and Ctrl+K bindings. Keep S and Space as symbol-first and Ctrl+K as the full palette.

ideas.title: Your coins at a glance: holdings, desk, alert and note badges in the watchlist
ideas.pitch: In my watchlist INJ shows 'held · avg 21.40 · +13%', a violet dot for the desk's waiting buy, a bell with 2 alerts and a note marker, so I can see where to look without opening four tabs.
ideas.why: Watchlist rows show price, sparkline, zone badge, trend and RSI, but none of the owner's own context. The data is already on the client: alertsApi.alerts, ac:coin-notes, fetchAccountPositions (today used only for the per-symbol myEntry overlay) and desk calls. For a spot holder, 'what do I hold and where is it' is the main question.
ideas.how: ChartWorkspace builds badges: Record<symbol, {held?: {qty, avg, pnlPct}; desk?: {status, confidence, interval}; alerts: number; note?: string}>. Sources: alerts filtered by armed and symbol; coinNotes; fetchAccountPositions(false) every 60 s when fetchBinanceKey reports configured (both are already imported, so reuse them); fetchDeskCalls('active') every 60 s and on 'ac:desk-changed'. Pass it to Watchlist as a prop and render small chips on the second row, using the up/down colours already in use. Add a sort 'My holdings first' to SORTS and a filter toggle 'Only coins with something happening' (holdings, desk call, armed alert or zone badge). Also fix keyboard stepping to follow the displayed order (see issues).
ideas.risk: Very little. Positions need the read-only key and are skipped silently without it. Keep the row height fixed so long lists don't jump.

ideas.title: Click a level to act on it, and make the right-click actions instant
ideas.pitch: I click the H4 demand box and get a card: '24.10–24.60 · 3.2% below price · fresh', with buttons for alert on entry, alert on 5m CHoCH inside, ask the agent about it, copy price, remove. Right-click 'Alert me at 7.15' fires in 50 ms instead of waiting on the LLM.
ideas.why: Clicking an AI level today (pickedLevel, ChartWorkspace lines 1284-1295) offers only 'Remove'. Turning a zone into an alert or trigger means opening Alerts → Triggers and picking the zone again. The right-click alert and line actions go through runAnalysis (see issues). The click-a-level-then-act loop is the core workflow of this app, and it currently takes 4-6 clicks plus an LLM call.
ideas.how: lib/alerts.ts: add alertFromOverlay(o) next to alertFromDrawing (a box gives a zone spec, a horizontal_line gives a cross spec). In ChartWorkspace, replace the pickedLevel bar with a LevelCard showing the label, the range, the distance from `price` and o.strength when present, with actions: addAlerts([alertFromOverlay(o)], symbol); addTrigger({symbol, interval:'5m', zone:{source:'fixed', price_low, price_high, direction: /demand|support/.test(o.kind) ? 'long' : 'short', label}, confirm:'any'}), the same call planTrigger already makes; askAgent(`What about the ${o.label} at ${range}?`); navigator.clipboard.writeText(price); Remove. Allow it on HTF, pinned and panel levels too, with Remove hidden when the level isn't one of `overlays`. AgenticChart: add onQuickAlert and onQuickLine props for the ask menu, as in the issue.
ideas.risk: Low. direction must respect spot-only: a supply zone gives a 'reached resistance (trim)' alert, not a short.

ideas.title: Proper drawing editing: drag anchors, Shift-constrain, touch-sized handles
ideas.pitch: I drag the end of my trendline to the new wick, pull a rectangle's corner to widen the zone, and on the phone I can actually grab a line with my finger.
ideas.why: Handles are drawn but can't be grabbed (see issues). Editing is the most frequent chart interaction after drawing, and it's where this app feels least like TradingView. The position tool also depends on it.
ideas.how: DrawingLayerPrimitive: add pickHandle(x, y, radius): {id, index} | null for the selected drawing (distance from each px() point; for 'rect' also the two unspecified corners, mapped to [p0.time, p1.price] and [p1.time, p0.price]). AgenticChart pointer 'down': try pickHandle first and set dragRef {id, index, orig}. In 'move', update only that point through toPoint (so magnet snapping works) and keep the rest. With e.shiftKey on a trendline, hold price at the other point's price (horizontal) or snap to 45° in pixel space. Hit radius is e.pointerType === 'touch' ? 14 : 6 and is passed to pick() and hits(). Alt+drag duplicates (reuse duplicateSelected).
ideas.risk: It interacts with the alert-line drag and pan logic in the same handler. Check handles first, then drawings, then alerts, as today.

ideas.title: Load older history when scrolling left
ideas.pitch: I scroll left on INJ 1h and keep going back months instead of hitting a wall after 3 weeks.
ideas.why: HISTORY_BARS = 500 (lib/config.ts) and there is no lazy loading: 500 bars is 21 days on 1h, 83 days on 4h and 8 hours on 1m. Checking how price reacted at a level last year means switching timeframe. The backend already pages backwards internally (market_data.py builds endTime requests around lines 342-354), so the cost is a small API change plus one frontend effect.
ideas.how: backend main.py /api/klines: add before: int | None (UNIX s) and pass it as end_time to a market.get_klines variant, served from candle_store where possible. lib/api.ts: fetchKlines(…, {before}). AgenticChart: subscribeVisibleLogicalRangeChange. When range.from < 25, no older-load is in flight, the chart isn't custom or replaying, and fewer than 5,000 bars are loaded, fetch 500 bars before candlesRef.current[0].time. Then prepend, mapper.setData, candle and volume setData, and shift the visible logical range by the number of bars added (the same anchor trick render() already uses), then refreshIndicators(true). Stop when a fetch returns nothing. Write the merged series to candleCache, and show a small 'Loading older…' chip at the left edge.
ideas.risk: Memory and indicator recompute cost grow with bar count, hence the 5,000 cap. Kimi markers are already filtered to the first loaded candle, so more of them show, which is fine. The agent still sends only the last 500 candles.

ideas.title: Snappy workspace: live price in its own store, memoized and lazy-loaded panels, no polling while hidden
ideas.pitch: Dragging a line stays at 60 fps even with Agent, Alerts and Journal opened once, and the app opens faster.
ideas.why: See the re-render issue: each tick or drag pointermove re-renders every mounted panel, hidden tabs keep polling, and the page bundle is one 538 KB chunk (.next/static/chunks/app/page-*.js) because dockPanels.tsx statically imports all 12 panels, including GridBotPanel (1,646 lines), AccountPanel (1,075) and JournalPanel (855).
ideas.how: lib/feedStore.ts: a tiny external store (subscribe/get/set) for {price, open24, source}. AgenticChart writes to it; ChartHeader and price-using panels read it through useSyncExternalStore, and dockProps loses `price`. Dock: render each tab through a memoized <TabHost active={t.id===p.tab}> and give panels an `active` prop so usePolled keys become null while hidden. dockPanels.tsx: use next/dynamic(() => import('./GridBotPanel'), {ssr:false, loading: Spinner}) for every EXTRA_PANEL. A visibility hook (document.hidden) pauses Watchlist, Desk, Status and useMarketMetrics timers. During a drag, keep the moving points in a ref and in layerRef.setDrawings, and call onDrawingsChange once on pointerup.
ideas.risk: A panel that doesn't handle `active` could miss updates. Default to polling on the first open and refetch whenever active turns true.

ideas.title: Live tab title, unread badge and a 'welcome back' on focus
ideas.pitch: My browser tab reads 'INJ 24.31 ▲1.2% · 4H'. When an alert or desk call fires while I'm elsewhere it shows '(2)' and a dot on the icon, and when I come back after a few hours the 'since you last looked' card is waiting.
ideas.why: A trader keeps this open next to Binance and Discord. Nothing in the frontend sets document.title, public/ is empty (no favicon or manifest), and the since-you-last-looked card misses the 'tab left open' case (see issues). Cheap, satisfying touches.
ideas.how: ChartWorkspace: an effect on [symbol, interval, price, change24] sets document.title, throttled to 1 s. Keep an unread counter that increments in onAlertsFired, onSignalFired and the new desk handler while document.hidden, prefixes the title with '(n)', and resets on visibilitychange. A canvas-drawn favicon (16×16 candle in the accent colour, red dot when unread > 0) is set through a <link rel=icon> data URL. Add public/manifest.webmanifest with an icon so it can be installed as a PWA window on desktop and phone. Fix SinceLastLooked to re-check on visibilitychange.
ideas.risk: Very little. Throttle the title updates so a 1m chart doesn't thrash.

ideas.title: Level freshness: show when the AI levels were drawn and offer a refresh
ideas.pitch: Above the chart: 'Levels from 3 days ago · price +8.4% since · Refresh'. Then I know the demand box I'm staring at predates the breakout.
ideas.why: onDataReady auto-detects levels only when a chart has none saved (convoRef.current.overlays.length === 0), so ac:overlays:SYM:TF can be weeks old and nothing on screen says so. Stale zones look exactly like fresh ones, which is the worst kind of wrong for a levels-first app.
ideas.how: In ChartWorkspace.changeOverlays (and in playWalk and readShot, which call it), also writeStored(`ac:overlays-meta:${sym}:${tf}`, {at: Date.now(), price, lastBar}). Read it with usePersistentState next to overlaysKey. When age is over 30 bars of INTERVAL_SECONDS[interval], or |price/meta.price − 1| is more than 2× the last ATR (lib/indicators atr), show a chip in the AgenticChart chips row ('Levels from 3d ago · +8.4% since') with a Refresh button that calls runAnalysis('', {silent:true}). Optionally add a Settings toggle 'Refresh stale levels automatically' that does the same from onDataReady.
ideas.risk: An automatic refresh would replace levels the user curated (by deleting some). Keep it manual by default, and it stays undoable through changeOverlays.

ideas.title: Phone-first navigation: a 'More' sheet, swipe through the watchlist, long-press menu
ideas.pitch: On my phone I swipe the coin name left or right to flip through my list, long-press a price to alert on it, and the bottom bar has 5 clear buttons instead of 18 that scroll sideways.
ideas.why: On mobile the bottom nav lists Chart, Draw and all 16 tabs in a horizontally scrolling strip (ChartWorkspace MobileTab map), so most tabs are offscreen with no affordance. There is no touch path to the right-click menu (contextmenu isn't reliable on iOS), and [ / ] stepping is keyboard-only.
ideas.how: ChartWorkspace mobile nav: Chart, Draw, Agent, Watchlist, Alerts and More. More opens a bottom sheet with a grid of the remaining tabs (icon, label, badge from DockTab.badge). ChartHeader on mobile: pointer-swipe detection on the symbol button (|dx| > 40 px) calls a new onStep(±1) that reuses stepWatchlist. AgenticChart: a long-press (pointerdown held 500 ms without moving 4 px, pressRef already tracks 'moved') opens the same askMenu at that price. Use a larger touch hit radius for drawings (see the editing idea).
ideas.risk: A long-press could conflict with LWC's touch crosshair. Only open the menu when tool==='crosshair' and the press didn't pan.

ideas.title: Grid upgrades: maximize a cell, a 1+2 layout, per-cell timeframe
ideas.pitch: With four charts open I double-click the INJ header to blow it up full screen, Esc puts it back, and I can pick 'one big plus two small' for daily, 4H and 15m top-down work.
ideas.why: Grid modes are 1, 2 or 4 (GRID_CLASS, NEXT_GRID). Focusing on one chart means changing the saved grid, which loses the arrangement, and a cell's timeframe can only be changed by activating it first and then using the top bar. Top-down analysis is exactly what the agent preaches (top-down walk, HTF zones).
ideas.how: types GridMode: add 3, with GRID_CLASS '3': 'grid-cols-[2fr_1fr] grid-rows-2', where cell 0 gets row-span-2 (pass a className from cellList), and add it to ChartHeader GRID_MODES and NEXT_GRID. A new transient `maximized: number | null` state in ChartWorkspace: when set, cellList = [maximized] without touching ac:grid. Toggle it by double-clicking the ChartCell header or with Alt+Enter, and clear it on Esc. ChartCell header: a compact timeframe <select> that patches only that cell (setCells by index) without activating it. Anchor the floating bars inside the active cell (see issues).
ideas.risk: Very little. Crosshair sync and ChartCell instances survive because cells keep their key `cell-${i}`.
